items.title: Galamsey today is worse than it was in 2024 – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: The National Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has claimed that illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, has worsened under the current administration compared with the situation in 2024. He has challenged the government to account for its campaign promises on tackling illegal mining, arguing that the measures being implemented have failed to produce the environmental improvements Ghanaians were assured of before the National Democratic Congress (NDC) assumed office. Mr Aboagye said the continued pollution of water bodies, the persistence of illegal mining activities and the recent deaths of six people during a confrontation linked to anti-galamsey operations raise questions about the effectiveness of the government’s strategy. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, he criticised the approach adopted by the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), questioning why enforcement operations were focused on tracking excavators when, according to him, illegal mining activities taking place openly and supported by audio and video evidence had not been adequately addressed. “What the hell are you doing on the streets transporting excavators when you have audios and videos and daytime galamsey which you haven’t dealt with? What are you doing? What are you doing killing people when you haven’t even arrested those in broad daylight?” he asked. His comments follow a confrontation involving residents, suspected illegal miners and NAIMOS personnel at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. The incident reportedly occurred on Wednesday afternoon when some residents and suspected illegal miners attempted to prevent NAIMOS personnel from tracking excavators seized from the area. The confrontation resulted in the deaths of six people, prompting renewed scrutiny of the government’s anti-galamsey operations and the methods being used to enforce mining regulations. Mr Aboagye questioned whether the loss of lives had translated into any meaningful progress in the fight against illegal mining, pointing to the continued pollution of water bodies as evidence of the problem. “Look at this water. These six people who are dead, has the water colour changed? What did they die for?” he queried. He criticised what he described as attempts to manage public reaction to the incident through statements and appeals without sufficiently addressing the underlying challenges confronting the anti-galamsey campaign. The NPP communications director also accused the NDC government of failing to demonstrate a significant departure from the policies and enforcement methods used by previous administrations. He recalled that before the 2024 general election, the NDC had presented Ghanaians with a roadmap outlining how it intended to tackle illegal mining if elected into office. According to him, those commitments were contained in the party’s manifesto and campaign materials and formed part of the assurances given to voters. He has therefore challenged the government to identify the specific measures it has implemented and explain why the situation has not improved. “These people, before they came to office, gave us a roadmap. It’s still in their manifesto and it’s still on their campaign videos. They told us, vote for us when we come, these are the things we will do. The barest minimum, which ones have they done?” he asked. Mr Aboagye argued that the government must be judged not only by the policies it announces but also by the results those interventions deliver. He said even if some of the promised measures had been implemented, the administration had a responsibility to explain why they had not produced the expected outcomes. “And the ones they have done, if it hasn’t given us results, then what is their explanation?” he added. He further maintained that the current administration had not introduced any fundamentally different approach to the galamsey crisis since assuming office. “Ever since they came to office, there is not a single thing they have done that is different from what is being done in the past,” he stated. Demands accountability over Manso Keniago deaths Mr Aboagye insisted that the deaths at Manso Keniago should not be treated as an isolated incident or overshadowed by government communications. He called on the authorities responsible for combating illegal mining to explain the circumstances surrounding the confrontation and account for the effectiveness of their operations. He also questioned the decision to focus on the movement and tracking of seized excavators while, in his view, individuals involved in openly conducted illegal mining activities had not faced corresponding enforcement action. “The situation at hand, we must call the people who are responsible for dealing with this thing out. We shouldn’t allow them to be doing PR with this situation,” he said. He maintained that the government had made specific commitments to address the menace and must now demonstrate that those promises are being translated into tangible results. “The fact of the matter is that they gave us specific things that they will do to solve the problem. The situation is worse,” he added.

items.title: 40m MSMEs hold key to Nigeria’s economic future, Uzodimma, business leaders say
items.description: …Imo gov unveils blueprint for grassroots economic growth By Nnamdi Ojiego Nigeria’s nearly 40 million micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which account for close to half of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and nearly nine out of every 10 jobs, hold the key to its economic future, Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State and business leaders have said. They spoke on Friday, at the maiden edition of the Lagos Country Club Policy Dialogue with Government Leaders in Ikeja, Lagos, where they called for a deliberate shift towards developing local economies through infrastructure, affordable financing, reliable electricity, digital skills and stronger partnerships between government and the private sector. Delivering the keynote lecture entitled, “The Future Is Local: Stimulating Grassroots Economies for Inclusive Growth”, Uzodimma argued that Nigeria’s next phase of economic growth must come from its communities, particularly the towns and rural areas whose productive potential remains largely untapped. “My central argument is straightforward. Nigeria’s growth will be sustainable only when it is built on the strength of its many local economies. Government must lay the foundations, and private capital, much of which is represented here, must turn them into productive enterprises, jobs and prosperity. Neither can do this alone,” he said. Uzodimma said the concentration of economic opportunities in major cities had contributed to rural-urban migration, poverty and pressure on urban infrastructure, arguing that development must reach the communities people were leaving behind. Quoting National Bureau of Statistics figures, he said 72 per cent of rural Nigerians were poor, compared with 42 per cent in urban areas, while rural communities accounted for 80 per cent of the country’s poor population. “When local economies sit idle, the consequences do not stay local. Young people leave for the big cities or stay behind with nothing productive to do. That idleness has a way of finding the wrong employers. Crime and insecurity feed on it,” he said. Drawing on the research of Professor Andrés Rodríguez-Pose of the London School of Economics, the governor warned that neglected communities could eventually turn their frustration against the political and economic system. “In our own country, neglected places have expressed their frustration at the ballot box and through far more dangerous means. A local economy that gives young people a stake in peace is among the best security investments a government can make,” he added. To demonstrate how local economies could be stimulated, Uzodimma outlined what he described as the three pillars of his administration’s approach in Imo: laying the foundations for investment, supporting local enterprise and investing in people. He said more than 130 roads had been constructed since his administration assumed office in 2020, reconnecting communities with markets and improving commercial activities across the state. On electricity, he described the Orashi Power Project, launched under the Light Up Imo programme, as a major intervention aimed at reducing the cost of doing business. He also identified digital infrastructure and land administration as important foundations for grassroots development, noting that the state had introduced the Imo State Land Information System and MyImoApp to improve access to land records and tax payments. Earlier, Chairman of the occasion and former Managing Director and Chief Executive of Grand Cereals Limited, Alex Goma, acknowledged the Federal Government’s economic reforms but questioned the extent to which the gains had reached ordinary businesses. He noted that the removal of petrol subsidy, exchange-rate unification and tax reforms had helped restore some macroeconomic stability, but argued that small businesses were still struggling with the high cost of operations. “That is macroeconomic stability. It was hard won, and it deserves to be protected. But the honest question in this room is this: has that stability reached the market stall?” he asked. “Ask the leather worker in Kano, the grain trader at Dawanau, the adire dyer in Abeokuta, the tailor in Ilorin or the shoemaker in Aba. For most of them, the answer is: not yet.” Goma said small businesses continued to contend with expensive credit, unreliable electricity and multiple taxation, while many remained excluded from formal financing because of the requirements imposed by financial institutions. He called for policies that would make financing more accessible, reduce energy costs and reward businesses that maintained proper records, paid workers promptly and complied with relevant regulations. In his address, President of Lagos Country Club, Seyi Adewunmi, said the policy dialogue was conceived to bring government, business leaders and citizens together to address the disconnect between economic policies and the realities of ordinary Nigerians. Adewunmi stressed that small businesses constituted the backbone of the economy and deserved policies that would translate into improved access to credit, infrastructure and markets. He said: “This dialogue is designed to bridge the gap between policy formulation and economic realities, a place where government, the private sector and citizens can sit at the same table and speak plainly to one another. What we begin today, we intend to keep. This is the first edition, not the only one. “For too long, many of us have spoken of the Nigerian economy as though it lives only in Abuja, in the Central Bank, in the oil terminals and in the headlines. But the real Nigerian economy wakes up at 5 a.m. It is the shoemaker in Aba, the tailor in Yaba, the trader in Onitsha, the farmer in Benue, the young developer in Computer Village.” The post 40m MSMEs hold key to Nigeria’s economic future, Uzodimma, business leaders say appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ketu North MP condemns cash displays, urges aspirants to reject money politics
items.description: Member of Parliament for Ketu North, Edem Agbana, has expressed concern about the growing influence of money in politics, urging contestants in the ongoing National Democratic Congress (NDC) regional executive elections to be guided by their leadership abilities rather than material displays. He has taken issue with videos and photographs circulating on social media showing some aspirants openly displaying cash and other items as they campaign for positions in the party. Mr Agbana made the remarks during an interview on Saturday, November 14, where he described the development as troubling and cautioned the contestants against campaign conduct that could undermine the NDC’s social democratic values. “I want to make a passionate appeal to the aspirants. As a government that is trying, and as a party that is social democratic by ideology, we want to plead with them regarding the open display of cash and other things,” he said. Mr Agbana said the increasing monetisation of politics was a matter of concern to many within the party, stressing that the open display of money and other material items should not be encouraged. “I think the monetisation of our politics is a very big concern to many of us. Seeing videos and pictures of people openly holding some of these items is something that we must all condemn,” he said. His comments come as the NDC holds regional elections to select new executives who will be responsible for coordinating the party’s activities and providing leadership across the regions. Beyond his concerns about campaign conduct, Mr Agbana expressed the hope that the elections would be conducted peacefully, freely and fairly, without incidents in any part of the country.

items.title: ‘We must stop rigging’: Obidients must register as INEC ad hoc staff – Oseloka
items.description: Oseloka H. Obaze, the 2017 Anambra State governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Campaign Manager of the 2023 Obi-Datti presidential campaign, has urged supporters of Peter Obi, popularly known as Obidients, to register as ad hoc staff of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general election. Obaze made the appeal in a post on his X platform on Saturday, urging eligible supporters to take advantage of the ongoing INEC recruitment exercise, which he said would close in four days. He called on them to participate in the electoral process by serving as election officials at polling units, wards and collation centres to help prevent electoral malpractice. “Despite ongoing INEC shenanigans, we must follow them bumper-to-bumper. Eligible Obidients must go out and register to be INEC ad hoc staff. It closes in four days,” he said. Obaze said the participation of Obidients in the exercise would enable them to be present at different stages of the electoral process and contribute to ensuring credible elections. “We must be in the electoral rooms, halls, corridors, collation centres, wards and polling units to make a difference and stop any form of rigging and electoral manipulation,” he added. He argued that Nigerians opposed to electoral malpractice should use constitutional means to ensure that the 2027 general election is free, fair and credible. According to him, supporters of democratic governance have the numbers and motivation to make a difference in the country’s electoral process. “Those attempting to destroy Nigeria are in the minority, we are in the majority and must stop them constitutionally by compelling the 2027 elections to be free, credible and fair,” he said. Obaze urged the supporters to seize the opportunity to participate in the electoral process, expressing confidence that their involvement would help secure a credible election. items.title: ‘NACOC officers are not adequately equipped’ – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Miracles Aboagye, has urged the government to commit more resources to the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), saying the commission’s budget must reflect the seriousness of Ghana’s fight against drug trafficking. He said the government must provide NACOC with adequate funding and logistical support to enable its officers to effectively tackle the growing threat of narcotics trafficking. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, during a discussion on recent drug busts linked to Ghana, Mr Aboagye said the passion and commitment of NACOC officials must be matched with sufficient financial support from the state. He singled out the Deputy Director-General in charge of Enforcement, Control and Elimination at NACOC, Twum, for his dedication to the work, but questioned whether the commission had the resources needed to deliver on its mandate. “Sometimes when I hear Twum speak, I feel the passion in him. I mean, I really feel that he’s passionate about the work,” he said. However, Mr Aboagye said his observations of NACOC personnel at the airport suggested that they were not adequately equipped to deal with the responsibilities assigned to them. “But when I go to the airport, and I see the NACOC guys, they don’t look fortified enough. You realise that they don’t have enough to be able to do the kind of work that they do,” he stated. He said that the government’s seriousness about tackling drug trafficking should be reflected in its budgetary allocation to narcotics control. According to him, the government must make a clear financial commitment to the sector so NACOC can acquire the equipment and resources required to strengthen its operations. “If the government really takes this narcotics thing seriously, it should reflect that this is how much we are dedicating to narcotics control, so that Twum and his people can also get the resources they need to work,” he said. Mr Aboagye warned that failing to adequately fund the commission could undermine public confidence in the country’s efforts to combat drug trafficking. He further cautioned that repeated reports of cocaine consignments worth billions of dollars leaving Ghana could create the impression that the country’s economy was being supported by proceeds from the illegal drug trade. “Otherwise, the easiest conclusion is that the economy clearly is being financed by cocaine,” he said. He added that the continued movement of large quantities of cocaine linked to Ghana raised serious questions about what happened to the drugs while they were within the country. “If you have a country where, consistently, you are getting billions of dollars of cocaine getting out, only God knows what happened when the cocaine was in the country,” he stated. The 2027 budget indicates that the Narcotic Control Board will be made to retain 4.2 million cedis in internally generated funds for its operations.

items.title: NACOC is highly under-resourced; the drug problem is beyond cocaine – Senyo Hosi
items.description: Convener of the OneGhana Movement, Senyo Hosi, has described the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) as highly under-resourced, warning that Ghana’s drug problem extends beyond cocaine trafficking to the growing use of synthetic substances. He says the country risks overlooking a major part of the drug menace if its response focuses largely on cocaine, particularly as synthetic drugs pose a serious threat to young people. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, Mr Hosi said NACOC lacked the personnel, equipment, and logistical support needed to tackle the problem effectively. “It is a highly under-resourced institution,” he said, referring to NACOC. He recalled seeing NACOC officers stationed at some border points without proper offices, with some forced to work under trees. Drawing on his experience travelling in the oil business and his interactions with a former head of the Commission, he said the situation reflected the difficult conditions under which officers had been operating. Mr Hosi acknowledged that NACOC had expanded its presence from about eight districts before the current government took office to 81 districts. However, he argued that the expansion must be matched with adequate resources to strengthen the Commission’s operations. Beyond the resource challenges, Mr Hosi urged the government to broaden its approach to tackling drug trafficking and substance abuse, stressing that cocaine was not the only concern. “The drug problem should not be made a cocaine problem at all. The bigger problem we have is with the synthetics. Serious problem. But that’s what our youth are getting into,” he said. He warned that although Ghana serves as a transit point for cocaine consignments, the country must also be concerned about the growing domestic consequences of drug use. Mr Hosi said the threat should not be treated as a distant security concern, urging families, particularly those in the middle class, to recognise that young people across society could be exposed. He also expressed disappointment that the 2027 Budget did not give sufficient attention to the drug menace and the resources required by NACOC, arguing that the issue deserved greater national priority. Mr Hosi said strengthening the Commission would require more than expanding its presence across the country, insisting that officers must be equipped with the tools and logistical support needed to detect and disrupt drug trafficking.

items.title: Oliver Kevor re-elected NDC Eastern Regional Chairman
items.description: Ing. Dr Mark Oliver Kevor will continue to lead the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Eastern Region after retaining his position as Regional Chairman in the party’s executive elections. Ahead of the polls, Dr Kevor identified grassroots mobilisation and the strengthening of party structures as key priorities for his next term, saying he wanted to position the region as an NDC stronghold. He outlined a constituency-by-constituency and branch-by-branch strategy to expand the party’s presence and improve its organisation across the region. “Our goal must be clear: to turn the Eastern Region green, constituency by constituency and branch by branch,” he stated. Dr Kevor also pointed to his experience working with the late Dr Edward Omane Boamah as an influence on his approach to political organisation, highlighting the value of data, discipline, strategic planning and attention to detail. His re-election offers him another opportunity to implement the agenda and strengthen the NDC’s grassroots presence in the Eastern Region.

items.title: États-Unis : ce que le reflux du vote hispanique signifie pour l’élection de 2028
items.description: Lors des élections de mi-mandat, seuls 29 % des électeurs hispaniques ont soutenu les candidats républicains à la Chambre des représentants, contre 70 % qui ont soutenu les démocrates, ce qui marque une baisse de 30 points de l'écart entre les partis par rapport à 2024. Cette évolution sera clef pour le prochain cycle électoral. Elle s’explique avant tout par le bilan républicain depuis le retour de Donald Trump à la Maison-Blanche. En effet, l’électorat hispanique avait massivement voté républicain en 2024 pour deux raisons principales : d’une part, la promesse d’une reprise économique et d’une baisse de l’inflation, et d’autre part, la promesse d'un rétablissement de l’ordre à la frontière. Or, sur ces deux sujets, l’action de l’administration républicaine n’a pas été jugée satisfaisante. L’inflation continue en effet de croître, notamment sur fond de guerre contre l’Iran, mais aussi à cause de la guerre commerciale lancée dès janvier 2025. En matière d’immigration, la brutalité des arrestations a provoqué une onde de choc, y compris chez les citoyens naturalisés. Au sein du Parti républicain, cette défaite électorale pourrait trancher un débat qui date des années 1990. À la base de la stratégie théorisée par Karl Rove sous la présidence de George W. Bush et incarnée aujourd’hui par le secrétaire d'État Marco Rubio, un courant au sein du parti considère que les valeurs familiales, religieuses et entrepreneuriales des Hispaniques en font des alliés naturels du GOP, à condition de concevoir un discours d'inclusion. À l’opposé, un deuxième courant défend une stratégie de coalition raciale. Inspirée de la « stratégie Steve Sailer » popularisée dans les cercles nationalistes, il s'agit de s'adresser aux intérêts transpartisans de l'électorat blanc plutôt que de chercher à séduire des minorités structurellement acquises aux démocrates. Les deux victoires de Donald Trump, en 2016 et 2024, ont validé tour à tour chacune des deux stratégies : en 2016, une rhétorique anti-immigration a permis de capter une frange de l'électorat ouvrier blanc, démobilisé par le Parti démocrate, dans la Rust Belt ; en 2024, il a réussi une percée historique auprès des Latinos . Pour l'aile identitaire du mouvement MAGA, le résultat des élections de mi-mandat tranche désormais le débat et constitue la preuve que l'électorat latino-américain reste fondamentalement antagoniste. Mais cette tentation du repli identitaire, combinée aux tendances démocratiques, ouvre un autre dilemme. En effet, alors qu'ils ne représentaient que 9 % de l’électorat américain en 2006, les Hispaniques en constituent désormais 16 %, avec 5,2 millions d'électeurs supplémentaires entre 2022 et 2026. À l'inverse, la part des Blancs non hispaniques dans l'électorat inscrit a chuté de 74 % en 2006 à 61 % en 2026, avec une perte de 2,6 millions d'électeurs sur les quatre dernières années. Les stratèges du parti républicain se retrouvent ainsi pris en étau entre deux réalités : d'une part, un électorat blanc majoritaire, mais vieillissant (âge médian de 52 ans The U.S. Electorate’s Changing Racial and Ethnic Makeup », Pew Research Center, 10 septembre 2026.'> 1 ), dont la base la plus fidèle constitue le cœur du mouvement MAGA et exige une fermeté absolue en matière d'immigration depuis 2015 ; d'autre part, une population hispanique jeune (âge médian de 39 ans) et en pleine expansion. Pour le moment, l’administration républicaine semble trancher en faveur de la stratégie « Steve Sailer », et la nomination de Stephen Miller au poste clef de directeur de cabinet de la Maison-Blanche dès le 9 novembre 2026 peut être lue dans ce sens. En confiant les responsabilités de l'exécutif à l'architecte en chef de la ligne dure en matière de politique migratoire, Donald Trump confirme que le contrôle démographique (via une politique migratoire stricte et des expulsions) prime désormais sur la conquête électorale. Cette stratégie est complétée par une poussée pour fidéliser les électeurs hispaniques restés loyaux au Parti républicain en 2026, un socle loin d'être négligeable dans les États pivots. Ainsi, plutôt que de les courtiser en tant que minorité ethnique aux intérêts spécifiques, l'objectif est de les intégrer à l'identité englobante de la « civilisation occidentale ». C'est dans ce contexte qu'on peut interpréter la rhétorique déployée lors du discours prononcé à Athènes par le secrétaire d'État Marco Rubio le 7 octobre 2026 . Dans ce contexte, la désignation d'un ennemi extérieur et intérieur est devenue indispensable. Elle s'appuie désormais sur la menace du péril communiste brandie face à la percée de figures de l'aile gauche du Parti démocrate, comme Abdul El-Sayed, élu sénateur du Michigan. Le regard tourné vers 2028, si le bilan économique ne permet pas de rétablir une coalition d’intérêts, les éléments de la bataille identitaire sont d’ores et déjà en place. L’article États-Unis : ce que le reflux du vote hispanique signifie pour l’élection de 2028 est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Tinubu Northern Youth Forum has announced its decision to withdraw support for President Bola Tinubu and back former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The group also announced a change of identity, adopting the name Arewa Youth For Atiku (AYA) as part of its new political direction. The decision was contained in a statement signed by Adamu Jikan Manu on behalf of the group on November 13, 2026. According to the statement, the formal endorsement of Atiku, declaration of support and official defection to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) will take place on Saturday, November 14, at the party’s North-East Strategic Office in Azare, Bauchi State. The ceremony will be led by the group’s Convener, Hon. Auwal Ibrahim Sansani, CNA. The group said its transition from Tinubu Northern Youth Forum to Arewa Youth For Atiku was intended to provide a broader platform for youth engagement, political awareness, community outreach and participation in the democratic process across Northern Nigeria. It called on its members, supporters, community and religious leaders, youth and women organisations, students, market associations, professionals and other stakeholders to attend the declaration ceremony. The statement said the group believed Nigeria needed responsible leadership, national unity, effective governance and meaningful citizens’ participation. It also urged Nigerians who shared its vision to join its campaign for peaceful and democratic participation ahead of the 2027 general election. The group concluded its statement with the slogan: “Join the Atiku Train. Vote Atiku, Save Nigeria.” The post Tinubu Northern Youth Forum dumps president, backs Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Peshawar ATC moves to declare Sohail Afridi proclaimed offender in Radio Pakistan attack case
items.description: PESHAWAR: An anti-terrorism court here has started proceedings to declare dysfunctional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as a proclaimed offender in the Radio Pakistan attack case as the relevant police official claimed that Mr Afridi couldn’t be traced. In the order sheet, Judge Wali Mohammad Khan noted that the detective foot constable (DFC) of the East Cantonment police station returned the warrants issued against the accused, including Sohail Afridi and Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf activist Mohammad Amir Khan, with overleaf reports stating that both of them couldn’t be found or traced. “Proclamation notices under Section 87 of CrPC should be issued against accused Sohail Afridi and Amir Khan, with notice to the DFC for recording a corroborative statement,” he said. He fixed Nov 24 for submission of the DFC’s report and further proceedings. Police official says dysfunctional CM remains untraced The judge had ordered the issuance of arrest warrants for the accused on Oct 28 after a supplementary charge-sheet was submitted, naming Afridi, Amir, former provincial ministers Taimoor Saleem Khan and Kamran Bangash and PTI Peshawar president Irfan Saleem as the accused in the May 2023 ransacking and torching of the Radio Pakistan building in Peshawar. Subsequently, the court issued warrants against Afridi and Amir on Nov 5. The warrants issued for Mr Afridi’s arrest listed his residential address in Bara, Khyber district. However, they didn’t describe Mr Afridi as the dysfunctional chief minister. The other three newly nominated accused appeared before the court and were granted interim pre-arrest bail. The dysfunctional chief minister has not been seen since the imposition of the governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Oct 11. While his whereabouts remained unknown, first a federal minister and then some other government functionaries disclosed that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody. The other accused, Amir Khan, was also reportedly taken into custody a few days ago but has so far not been produced before any court. The alleged illegal detention or abduction of Mr Afridi was challenged by his brother, Amir Khan, in the Peshawar High Court. However, the court halted proceedings in the matter after the Federal Constitutional Court suspended its powers to hear cases under Article 199 of the Constitution. Section 87 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) states: “If any Court is satisfied after taking evidence that any person against whom a warrant has been issued by it has absconded or is concealing himself so that such warrant cannot be executed, such Court may publish a written proclamation requiring him to appear at a specified place and at a specified time not less than thirty days from the date of publishing such proclamation.” The law also provides that a proclamation issued by the court shall be publicly read in some conspicuous place of the town or village in which such person ordinarily resides; it shall be affixed to some conspicuous part of the house or homestead in which such person ordinarily resides or to some conspicuous place of such town or village. A copy must also be affixed to a conspicuous part of the courthouse. Last month, the prosecution submitted a supplementary charge-sheet, nominating Mr Afridi and the other four PTI members as accused in the case. None of them had been named in the first information report or earlier charge-sheet. The supplementary charge-sheet followed findings by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency and the National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) regarding video clips purportedly showing the incident and profile pictures of the suspects. According to a report by investigation officer Deputy Superintendent of Police Khushal Khan, Radio Pakistan Peshawar station director Tufail Ahmad recorded a supplementary statement in light of the forensic findings, nominating the five men as accused. The forensic examination was ordered on Dec 12, 2025, on an application filed by the Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation’s counsel, Shabbir Hussain Gigyani. The PFSA subsequently concluded that the facial features of the five men matched those of suspects allegedly seen participating in the rioting in the video footage. A Nadra report identified CNIC numbers apparently belonging to the men and described them as probable matches for the profile pictures submitted for examination. The newly nominated accused have challenged the authenticity of the videos, claiming that the footage doesn’t relate to the incident. The court is currently conducting the trial of 75 accused in the case, including current and former lawmakers. The FIR was registered at the East Cantonment police station on May 10, 2023, on the complaint of then station house officer Arbab Naeem Haider under various provisions of the Pakistan Penal Code and the Anti-Terrorism Act. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Over 80 brands await shoppers on final day of Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair at Ghud Park, Accra Mall
items.description: There is still time to shop, discover new brands and enjoy exciting offers at the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026, as the three-day exhibition enters its final day today, Sunday, November 15. If you have not visited yet, today is your last opportunity to make your way to Ghud Park at Accra Mall and experience an exhibition bringing together more than 80 brands from across Ghana. From food and beverages to fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, household products and real estate, visitors can explore a wide range of locally made products and services, meet business owners and take advantage of special deals and discounts. Something for everyone The fair, powered by Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank, has brought together established businesses and emerging brands, giving visitors an opportunity to discover products, support local enterprises and connect directly with the people behind the businesses. Major participating institutions include Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) and Glico Life. Other exhibitors include Wilmar Africa, showcasing its Fortune Spread brand; Sintex Tank, offering water storage solutions; DBS, in housing and roofing; and Greenhaul Solutions, which focuses on waste management and scrap procurement. Whether you are looking to shop, explore new products, discover business opportunities or simply spend time with family and friends, the fair offers an opportunity to do so in one place. Shopping meets entertainment The exhibition has also featured musical performances, including a set from Ghanaian duo Lali X Lola, adding to the atmosphere of shopping, networking and entertainment. The event builds on the maiden edition held in October 2025, which attracted more than 160 exhibitors and over 1,000 visitors on its opening day. Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank, the initiative seeks to give small and medium-sized enterprises greater market access, brand visibility and opportunities to connect with potential customers and business partners. The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 closes today, Sunday, November 15. Visitors are encouraged to pass through Ghud Park, Accra Mall, before the exhibition wraps up and take advantage of the final opportunity to shop, explore and support Ghanaian businesses.

items.title: We sang new national anthem, observed national protocols – NDC chieftain blasts critics
items.description: Hon. Joseph Osemudiamen Mawuli Orukpe, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate for Ikeja Federal Constituency, has dismissed claims that members of the party refused to sing the new national anthem during the Peter Obi town hall meeting in Ikeja, Lagos State. Orukpe described the allegation as false and misleading, insisting that members of the party present at the event observed national protocols and duly rendered the new national anthem. He stated this in a video posted on the Nigeria Democratic Congress Lagos State’s X platform on Saturday. Orukpe, who said he was physically present at the town hall meeting, accused elements of the ruling party of attempting to mislead Nigerians by promoting what he described as a false narrative about the conduct of NDC members at the event. “Let me state categorically: That claim is false, misleading and completely unsupported by the facts,” he said. According to him, the new national anthem was duly sung by members present at the gathering, contrary to claims circulating in some quarters. He also faulted some media platforms for allegedly amplifying the narrative by circulating selected footage of the event without publishing the complete video showing NDC members singing the national anthem. The NDC candidate said the full footage was available and challenged those making the allegations to release it for public scrutiny. “In this age of digital media, facts are not difficult to establish. The complete footage exists. Let the public examine the evidence and judge for themselves,” he said. Orukpe maintained that the party’s commitment to Nigeria was not determined by controversies or political allegations, adding that its members respected the country’s national symbols, institutions and sovereignty. He urged Nigerians to reject what he described as propaganda and misinformation, insisting that political disagreements should not be used to distort events. “Nigeria deserves better than propaganda. Ikeja deserves better than misinformation. And our democracy deserves a politics anchored on truth,” he added. Vanguard Newspaper The post We sang new national anthem, observed national protocols – NDC chieftain blasts critics appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Keyamo: No one sings ‘On Your Mandate’ in place of anthem, accuses NDC of secessionism
items.description: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has defended the use of the campaign song, On Your Mandate, to welcome President Bola Tinubu at public events, insisting that it is never sung in place of Nigeria’s national anthem. Keyamo also accused the National Democratic Congress (NDC) of promoting secessionism, alleging that singing an outlawed national anthem in place of the legally recognised anthem amounted to an expression of a desire to have a separate country. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Sunday while responding to what he described as attempts by some individuals to equate the use of Tinubu’s campaign song with the singing of the former national anthem. The minister explained that supporters of Tinubu always observe the national anthem at official events before singing On Your Mandate to celebrate the President. “At no time have supporters of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu sung ON YOUR MANDATE IN PLACE of the National Anthem. At every occasion, the NATIONAL ANTHEM is always sung as a mark of recognition of one of our most important national symbols, and then the President is serenaded by his supporters with ON YOUR MANDATE,” he said. Keyamo maintained that nobody should prevent the presidential candidate of the NDC, Peter Obi, from adopting a song, including the former national anthem, as his campaign or personal song. He, however, insisted that such a song must be performed either before or after the legally recognised national anthem has been rendered. The minister also defended the Police Band’s use of the instrumental version of On Your Mandate to herald Tinubu’s arrival at public functions or his decision to address an audience. According to him, the practice is consistent with established presidential protocol, under which the Police Band plays an instrumental piece whenever the President arrives at an event or rises to speak. He cited the administrations of former Presidents Olusegun Obasanjo, Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, Goodluck Jonathan and Muhammadu Buhari, saying the Police Band similarly played musical pieces to herald their arrival at the National Assembly or before they addressed gatherings. Keyamo said the On Your Mandate instrumental is sometimes played by the Police Band to announce Tinubu’s presence or speech, but only after the national anthem has been rendered. He further argued that the practice was not unusual, pointing out that several states in Nigeria have their own anthems, which are performed after the national anthem at official functions. The minister, however, drew a distinction between the adoption of a campaign or state anthem and the singing of an outlawed national anthem in place of the officially recognised one. He described the alleged action by the NDC as an expression of a desire to have a separate country. “Singing an outlawed anthem IN PLACE of a legally approved NATIONAL ANTHEM by the NDC is surely an expression of a desire to have a separate country, and that is an INGREDIENT OF A SECESSIONIST GROUP,” Keyamo said. items.title: NDC regional executive elections: The chairmen who retained their seats and those who lost
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has elected regional chairmen in 13 of Ghana’s 16 regions following its 2026 regional executive elections held on Saturday, November 14. Results from the Central, Oti and Savannah regions are still pending, with the Central Region contest yet to be formally declared. The elections produced notable changes in some regional leadership positions, while several incumbent chairmen retained their seats. In some regions, voting was delayed. In Ashanti, heightened security at the election centre meant voting had not started by early afternoon, although the contest was subsequently concluded. Key outcomes from the regional contests Greater Accra: Benjamin Danso unseated incumbent Regional Chairman Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore by 500 votes in one of the major upsets of the elections. Northern Region: Godfred Apasinaba Wumbei won the chairmanship with 328 votes, defeating Alhaji Tanko Maida, who received 236. Ashanti Region: Augustus Andrews Nana Kwasi retained the chairmanship with 814 votes, ahead of former Regional Organiser Isham Alhassan Yaw Bonsu, who polled 622. Upper East Region: Alhaji Bolnaba secured another term with a 220-vote margin. He has led the region since December 2005. Bono Region: Nyamekye-Marfo secured more than 90 per cent of the votes. He had previously been returned unopposed in 2018 and 2022, making this his first contested regional chairmanship election. Upper West Region: Alhaji Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Randy, defeated incumbent Abdul Nasir Saani Bunas to become the new Regional Chairman. Randy polled 196 votes against Bunas’ 164, while Sombawiere Samba Sankara received 28. Randy’s victory came four years after he lost to Bunas in the 2022 regional elections. Western Region: Nana Kojo Toku retained the chairmanship after securing 225 votes. He defeated Samuel Kwame Borlu, who polled 209, while George Arthur received 114 votes. His re-election followed a petition by the Apinto royal family, which had asked the party to bar him from contesting on the grounds that he is a gazetted chief and that the NDC Constitution prohibits chiefs from active party politics. Ahafo Region: Owusu Nkrumah Ababio has been elected the new Regional Chairman after defeating two other contenders in the elections held at Nana Bosomprah Park in Goaso. Mr Ababio secured 106 votes to defeat his closest challenger, Joseph Baradoe, who polled 94. Ahmed Ali Awinbila received three votes. Central Region: The outcome remains undeclared. Incumbent Chairman Richard Asiedu has demanded a recount following reports that he lost the contest. How the elections were conducted The Electoral Commission conducted the polls, while the police provided security. Delegates were required to vote in person, as proxy voting was not permitted. The youth and women’s organisers and their deputies were elected at separate wing conferences, most of which took place on Friday, November 13. In Greater Accra, Mohammed Abdul Muqmin Juda won the Youth Organiser position with 103 votes against 26 for his closest contender. The main regional conferences elected the remaining executives, including vice-chairmen, secretaries, organisers, treasurers, communications officers and Zongo Caucus coordinators. Delegates included constituency executives, regional Members of Parliament, ministers, district chief executives and party elders. National Congress next The regional elections form part of the NDC’s internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections. The party is expected to hold its National Congress on December 19, 2026, to elect its national officers. Ahead of the congress, Chief of Staff Dr Julius Debrah urged successful candidates to work with those they defeated to promote unity within the party. Campaigning for the national positions has also begun, with Akwasi Oppong Fosu among those seeking the national chairmanship.

items.title: “Os deseo sufrimiento”: gloria y caída de Jensen Huang, rey de Nvidia, verso salvaje de la IA
items.description: Jensen Huang es el protagonista de una historia imposible , una de esas epopeyas de superación y gloria que han ayudado a cimentar el mito estadounidense de las oportunidades, de país joven, rico y salvaje donde todo es posible con esfuerzo. Nacido en Taiwán en 1963, llegó a los nueve años a Estados Unidos junto a su hermano, como menor no acompañado, con el fin de reunirse con un tío que vivía en el Estado de Washington, pero que lo internó por error en una academia para chicos problemáticos en Kentucky. Los padres lograron emigrar a los dos años y la familia se reunió en Oregón, donde Jensen destacó en los estudios y logró su primer empleo sirviendo mesas en la cadena de comida rápida Denny’s. Se graduó en ingeniería eléctrica dos años antes de lo habitual. En la universidad conoció a Lori Mills, una de las pocas chicas que estudiaban esa carrera, y se casaron. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El drama de las víctimas de fraude que no pueden recuperar su dinero: “El banco me dijo que era culpa mía”
items.description: Cuando Laura Marchena pidió un préstamo al banco, nunca imaginó que tendría que pasar los siguientes 12 años pagando por 26.000 euros de los que nunca llegó a disponer. Lo que no sabía es que el supuesto empleado que, creía, la estaba ayudando a evitar un fraude, en realidad le iba a vaciar la cuenta. “Se presentó con sus credenciales y me dijo que un señor de Albacete estaba intentando pedir un préstamo a mi nombre. Para bloquearlo tenía que pedirlo yo primero y luego devolverlo al banco”, relata esta mujer, que prefiere utilizar un nombre ficticio para contar su historia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Política y finanzas juegan a favor de Hernández de Cos para la presidencia del BCE
items.description: La carrera por presidir el Banco Central Europeo parece un sprint, pero aún no ha terminado, y se ha parecido más a una maratón, por más que los acontecimientos se hayan sucedido a velocidad de vértigo. El pasado 29 de octubre, la presidenta Christine Lagarde anunciaba su dimisión, efectiva el 7 de febrero. Este viernes, dos semanas después, el canciller alemán Friedrich Merz anunciaba que el acuerdo final es cuestión de días . A fecha de hoy, el favorito cada vez más claro es el español Pablo Hernández de Cos, director gerente del Banco Internacional de Pagos de Basilea y exgobernador del Banco de España, por delante del otro candidato oficial, el holandés Klaas Knot. Aunque, como advertía el líder alemán, Friedrich Merz, en Dublín este mismo viernes: “Las conversaciones tampoco han concluido todavía”. Y eso quiere decir que, en el poco tiempo que falta para adoptar decisión, el escenario puede cambiar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Left embraces socialist label in US as stigma fades
items.description: NEW YORK: “Socialism,” once considered a scarlet letter in the United States, is growing increasingly buzzy and mainstream as a slate of politicians embracing the label has gained significant ground. In the wake of November’s midterms, members of the Democratic Socialists of America — a leftist organisation that’s made inroads within the Democratic Party — now lead cities across the country including its two largest, New York and Los Angeles. DSA-endorsed politicians boosted their congressional seats from two to eight and won dozens of local elections, victories partly due to the Dem­ocrats’ wider battering of President Donald Trump’s Republicans. The so-called “bluenami” of Democratic wins “would not have been possible without a socialist surge,” DSA communications chair Cara Tobe said. “People are starting to realise and learn that socialism is not a big scary word,” she said, noting that the Democrats’ focus on affordability was lifted straight from the DSA playbook. But some political scholars aren’t convinced “socialism” earned votes. “A rising tide lifts all boats. This was a huge win for the Democratic Party across the board,” said Stephen Ansolabehere, professor of government at Harvard University. Hans Noel of Georgetown University attributed the success of Democrats — and DSA-backed candidates — to dissatisfaction with Trump. “It’s important to remember that while DSA-aligned candidates did very well this year, that’s mostly in the primaries and in very Democratic areas,” the politics professor said. Yet polls show a rising acceptance of socialism in the United States, a quintessentially capitalist country where politicians have long conflated the term with communism to vilify it. The DSA, founded in 1982 with a focus on labour organising, was for years a relatively tiny left-wing pressure group. In 2015, about 6,000 supporters paid dues, but after Donald Trump’s first presidential election new membership surged. Today, the group has more than 130,000 members and has proven an electoral force, with legions of volunteers helping elect candidates nationwide to state and local office. Mamdani effect Socialism has gained visibility through the campaigns and successes of prominent left-wing political stars, including the barnstorming of self-described socialist Bernie Sanders, who twice ran for president and has elevated younger candidates nationwide. His protege Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has posted a successful congressional career and now is rumoured to be considering a presidential run of her own. And New York’s young and charismatic Mayor Zohran Mamdani has proven a poster child for furthering progressive politics under a socialist banner in cities, with a focus on core DSA issues including affordable housing, immigrant protections and healthcare access. It’s a model politicians elsewhere in the nation are picking up on. Eric Blanc, a Rutgers University labour studies professor, said Mamdani’s successes have “normalised” socialism, with candidates viewing the moniker as “a net positive for them to get elected.” DSA member Nithya Raman was just elected mayor of Los Angeles on a platform of “pothole politics” — vowing to fix broken infrastructure — while harnessing the anger of younger voters over affordability. The growing cadre of socialist mayors leading city governments are far from the first of their kind in the US. Most notably, the so-called “sewer socialists” ran Milwaukee for more than half a century through 1960, dramatically scaling up public works projects including a modern sewer system, public housing and social infrastructure. Mamdani has frequently referenced the sewer socialists as inspiration. Raman has also pointed to the legacy as offering a vision for future success. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Ciberataques contra refrigeradores y falsas bombas: los frentes de la amenaza híbrida en Europa escalan en plena tormenta política
items.description: Ciberataques, correos con amenazas falsas de bomba, enjambres de drones que ponen en riesgo servicios e infraestructuras civiles. Es la guerra híbrida. Y Europa, en plena turbulencia política y económica, embarcada en un tenso ciclo electoral en varios países e inmersa en una crisis energética que alimenta el descontento, está bajo asedio. El foco está sobre los enemigos habituales: Rusia, Irán e incluso China; pero no se descarta que agentes no estatales que buscan aprovechar la coyuntura estén tras alguno de los ataques. items.title: La guerra en Ucrania salpica al este de Polonia con el eco de explosiones, alarmas antiaéreas y evacuaciones
items.description: Desde la ventana de Barbara en Dorohusk-Osada (Polonia) se ve Ucrania a menos de un kilómetro y medio de distancia. Esta jubilada polaca de 66 años también oye algunos bombardeos. Últimamente le parecen más frecuentes y las explosiones se sienten más cerca. La casa, los cristales y hasta la luz, tiemblan. Ante el temor a que los ataques rusos alcancen suelo polaco, especialmente en las regiones fronterizas de Podkarpackie y Lubelskie , las autoridades han reactivado las sirenas antiaéreas, calladas desde la II Guerra Mundial. “No puedo decir que no tenga miedo, pero prefiero no pensarlo mucho”, dice Barbara (no da el apellido) antes de entrar en el supermercado. Seguir leyendo

items.description: La prensa de Washington lleva más de una década enganchada a una droga conocida en el mercado negro de las noticias como el Trump Bump (algo así como el Subidón Trump). Tiene (o tenía) efectos inmediatos sobre la audiencia de los medios, y dispara (o disparaba) la relevancia de estos en la eterna pelea por la atención a base de hablar incesantemente del presidente de Estados Unidos. Es barata, se produce en cantidades industriales y provoca adicción. También, ese cierto remordimiento que dejan las gratificaciones inmediatas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: NDC elects new Upper West chairman as four incumbents lose positions
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Upper West Region has elected procurement consultant Alhaji Alhassan Adam, popularly known as Randy, as its new Regional Chairman. The 49-year-old defeated incumbent chairman Abdul Nasir Saani Bunas, polling 196 votes against Bunas’ 164. Sombawiere Samba Sankara, immediate past Nadowli-Kaleo Constituency Chairman, received 28 votes. Randy’s victory marks a return to the contest after he lost to Bunas in the party’s 2022 regional elections. The elections, which involved 392 delegates and 63 aspirants, also saw four incumbent regional executives lose their positions. Abu Balifema, immediate past NDC Chairman for Wa East, was elected First Vice Chairman, while Boniface Tienaa secured the Second Vice Chairman position. Both defeated three other contenders in the respective races. In the Women’s Organiser contest, Khalida M. A. Seidu defeated incumbent Prisca Domenyenvi Kuupole to secure the position. Ms Seidu, Deputy National Coordinator of the Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) and daughter of former Wa Central MP M. A. Seidu, polled 23 votes. Eunice Kaminta received eight, while Ms Kuupole, who is also the Upper West Regional Coordinator of the Ghana School Feeding Programme, obtained five votes. Gladys Sufuyani and Florence Kpan were elected as Deputy Women’s Organisers. The incumbent Regional Youth Organiser, Banye Joseph, also lost his position to Dery Joshua. Mr Joshua polled 21 votes against 18 for Mr Joseph, while Benedict Ninfaazumah received nine votes. Denis Andaban Yelebangniba was elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser after defeating Issa Suleimani Muthiew. Dauda Buckman Empire won the Regional Organiser position, defeating incumbent Mwinibahaara Saad Thomas, a Presidential Staffer and Political Adviser to the Upper West Regional Minister. Mr Empire polled 244 votes, while Mr Thomas secured 92. Bashiru Liman received 51 votes. Rashid Bickson was elected Deputy Regional Organiser after defeating four other candidates. Alex Bere won the Regional Secretary position, defeating four other contenders, in a result that gives Wa West Constituency representation in the party’s regional leadership. Mr Bere polled 130 votes, ahead of Samson Asibi Abu, who obtained 97; Edward K. Daery, with 82; and Nurideen Pelpuo, who received 63. Dr Ansongna B. Claudius was elected Deputy Regional Secretary after defeating four other aspirants. Biekpe Sylvester and Moomin Razak Gadao won the Communications Officer and Zongo Caucus positions respectively. Speaking after his election, Randy called for unity among party members and acknowledged the contributions of his opponents. “This victory is not for me, it is for all of us. Our former Regional Chairman and my two elder brothers, they have fought a good fight. This victory, we will have to work together to see to it that things can ride,” he said. He said he had anticipated victory based on the work his campaign team had undertaken across the constituencies and the outcomes of the constituency-level elections. “We were 99% into victory based on the quality work we have done across the constituencies and the outcome of the various constituency elections that motivated us,” he said. On reconciliation, he promised to engage members from all sides and address concerns within the party. “We will get things right. We will have to sit down, discuss, open up. We don’t have to cover up anything. We just have to open up to them, whatever the difficulty, then we sort it out,” he said. Randy also said the party would work to retain all 11 parliamentary seats in the region and increase its winning margins. “We will maintain 11/11 with increasing margins. That is what we expect to do. And we will have to reset the party as well in the region,” he added.

items.title: PSOE y PP recrudecen la pelea por el primer puesto en la recta final hacia el 29-N
items.description: Alberto Núñez Feijóo ya se ve en La Moncloa. Tanto que incluso se anima en Santiago de Compostela, su tierra, en un mitin hasta la bandera de gente fiel, a explicarles a los suyos cómo se llega al gran palacio del poder desde otro, el de Montepío, donde vivió 12 años como presidente de Galicia. “De Montepío a La Moncloa hay 600 kilómetros y 15 días. Es todo recto, la misma carrera, y antes de entrar en Madrid por la de Galicia, ahí está”, dice señalando con ilusión ese objeto de deseo que se le escapó en 2023 y ahora ve al alcance de la mano. Pedro Sánchez, su gran rival, aún confía en impedirlo movilizando a la izquierda. “Gracias a la movilización, en 2023 frenamos a la involución. Ahora lo ha hecho Lula en Brasil, y en EE UU los demócratas. Y ahora en España vamos a hacer historia y vamos a frenarles en las urnas”, clama desde Palma . Seguir leyendo

items.title: El PSOE gana por la izquierda lo que pierde por la derecha, según el tercer ‘tracking’ de la campaña
items.description: El cuadro general que viene ofreciendo la muestra diaria de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la Cadena SER, a dos semanas de las elecciones, sería el de una rotunda victoria del conjunto de la derecha, un fiasco para el conjunto de la izquierda y, en aparente contrasentido, un resultado en el caso específico del PSOE lejos de lo catastrófico. Los socialistas pueden mantener un nivel de apoyo muy similar al de 2023 . Y hasta entra dentro de las hipótesis verosímiles que, al contrario que entonces, sean la fuerza más votada si en el bloque de la derecha ocurre lo contrario: que el partido mayor ceda ante el menor, como apuntan los trabajos de 40dB. Esto es más asombroso si cabe teniendo en cuenta que en Sigüés casi nadie sabe qué partido gobierna en el Ayuntamiento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Qué es El Niño? Así enloquece el clima global una pequeña región tropical del Pacífico
items.description: Imagine una olla puesta al fuego con el agua bullendo hasta el borde. Añada un cazo más y el líquido hirviendo acabará rebosando. Es lo que está ocurriendo con el fenómeno de El Niño , un evento natural y cíclico que trastoca el clima en muchas partes de la Tierra, eleva la temperatura media mundial, acarrea pérdidas milmillonarias, hambrunas, muertes... El Niño es ese cazo último que se vierte sobre un planeta sobrecalentado ya por el cambio climático causado por el ser humano, principalmente, con el uso de los combustibles fósiles durante demasiadas décadas a pesar de las alertas científicas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Emma Suárez: “Me he quitado la ansiedad de llegar a todo y a todos. Ahora me toca a mí”
items.description: La veo desde lejos, inconfundible con su aire casual y su eterno flequillo rubio, sentada en un velador como única clienta de un elegante y acristalado quiosco madrileño en una mañana gris y lluviosa, componiendo una estampa a lo musa de Hopper , si Hopper hubiera sido madrileño y no gringo y Madrid tuviera mar y no río. Fuera, el otoño explota en toda la gama del rojo al ocre en los espectaculares árboles del Parque del Oeste, aumentando la sensación de oasis de calma entre las prisas urbanas de un martes víspera de una huelga general y del inicio de la campaña electoral. Se agradece. Vengo de ver Hermanas , la película en la que Emma Suárez interpreta a una esposa, madre, hermana y tía en un marco de abusos sexuales dentro de la familia, y tengo el corazón en un puño. Seguir leyendo UNA VIDA EN 110 PELÍCULAS Tenía 14 años cuando se presentó a unas pruebas, por probar, y resultó elegida. Era el casting de Memorias de Leticia Valle , la película basada en la obra de Rosa Chacel, y supuso el estreno en el cine, y en la actuación, de Emma Suárez (Madrid, 62 años). Desde entonces, ha participado en 110 películas, por las que ha ganado tres premios Goya, y decenas de obras de teatro y series de televisión. El 27 de noviembre estrena la película Hermanas , junto a Elena Anaya.

items.title: Sergio Ramírez: “Estos años de exilio han sido una lucha por aferrarme a mi lenguaje, por no perderlo”
items.description: Sergio Ramírez (Masatepe, Nicaragua, 84 años) es grande, sereno; camina ayudado de un bastón. Socarrón, dice que de su ingreso en la RAE, hoy a las 19.00, lo que le pone más nervioso es que tiene “que dar un paseo y subir a una grada, con el problema con la pierna”. Premio Cervantes en 2017 , luchador de la primera hora del sandinismo y exvicepresidente de Nicaragua, se exilió en España en 2021 y en 2023 el régimen de Ortega le despojó de su nacionalidad. Hoy dos detalles le señalan como heredero de Mario Vargas Llosa. El primero: ocupará su sillón, el L. El segundo: a él dedicará su discurso de investidura, Un novelista ecuménico . Se sienta. Escucha las preguntas. Desparrama sabiduría y sentido común. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Broncano y las inquilinas
items.description: Dos noticias, una misma historia. Un presentador de televisión se disculpa por decepcionar a su público y una huelga por la vivienda necesita recurrir a los sindicatos de clase para poder ser convocada. Dos episodios que, si se leen juntos, plantean una misma pregunta: ¿Qué ocurre con nuestros intermediarios, las instituciones que durante el siglo pasado organizaron nuestra manera de estar juntos en política? Al margen de reconocer su incomprensible entrevista a Abascal, de dejarse vampirizar por los intereses partidistas o aceptar que Vox pusiera sus propios espectadores, errores que él mismo reconoció, lo más revelador de Broncano fue decir que entre el programa y sus seguidores se ha generado una comunidad de “identificación”. El cómico hablaba de una relación que va más allá del entretenimiento, de una forma de pertenencia y confianza donde hay incluso cierta expectativa de representación; un público que se reconoce en él porque comparte una manera de mirar la realidad y espera que sea consecuente con ella. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Será la edad
items.description: Sé que no suena ortodoxo en estos momentos, pero servidora, para acabar perpetrando esa celebración de la democracia que es el voto, ha decidido ahorrarse la campaña . Paradojas de la vida: un acto de responsabilidad alimentado por otro que, para algunos, sería de irresponsabilidad. En el cuento Justo el Treintaiuno, el uruguayo Onetti describe cómo una mujer se sienta a diario en el inodoro y lee un cartel que reza: “Gracias, Dios mío, por no haberme hecho mujer ni negro ni judío ni perro ni petizo”. Ironías onettianas aparte, yo diría, “Gracias, Dios mío, por no haberme hecho periodista política ni analista ni politóloga ni presentadora de informativos”, gracias, Señor, por hacerme tan carente de responsabilidades como para permitir que me ahorre algo que me hace sentir que mi reino no es de este mundo. No es que no me concierna lo que nos viene ocurriendo, en lo absoluto, pero el ruido me distrae. Con ruido no veo, como diría el enfermizo Juan Ramón. Tanta es mi confusión que cuando el jueves escuché en el desayuno que había comenzado la campaña pensé si no estaría perdiendo capacidad cognitiva, dado que yo pensaba que esto era algo que había comenzado hacía meses, qué digo meses, años, que vivíamos en campaña permanente, con esas homilías de los domingos que los informativos glosan o esas exabruptos que a diario nos avergüenzan. Ocurre que, de vez en cuando, la realidad nos saca del bucle, ocurre, por ejemplo, que un sindicato nacido de las puras necesidades sociales, el de inquilinas, consigue movilizar a partidos e incluso urge a las grandes organizaciones sindicales a hablar de lo que importa. Ocurre que por unos días la conversación se despereza, y se diría que lo que realmente importa vuelve a tomar la calle y a protagonizar las tertulias, pero ay, amigas, el baño de realidad acaba porque raudos nuestros clásicos se apoderan del asunto. Para la oposición, tanto huelguistas como manifestantes están manipulados por el diabólico Sánchez, de tal forma que cualquier protesta se califica de acto electoral, así catalogan las movilizaciones por la vivienda, la enseñanza, la universidad, los servicios públicos, la sanidad. El insulto es su manera de evitarse el mostrar un proyecto alternativo. Y es curioso porque esta permanente teoría acusatoria contra el Sánchez maniobrero acaba por librar al propio Sánchez de su parte de responsabilidad, que también la tiene. Seguir leyendo

items.title: EL PAÍS celebra los 500.000 suscriptores con un espectáculo teatral de historias de la redacción
Medio millón de “gracias” sobre el escenario
items.description: Con menos de tres centímetros cada uno, colocados uno detrás de otro, los nombres y apellidos de los 500.000 suscriptores de EL PAÍS ocuparían en línea recta 14 kilómetros. Esa es, más o menos, la distancia que separa la redacción central de EL PAÍS en Madrid en la calle Miguel Yuste del escenario de teatro Pavón de La Latina, donde este sábado se celebró un espectáculo con un título tan sencillo como diáfano: “500.000 gracias”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mélenchon se consolida en una Francia agitada
items.description: Doce del mediodía. Salón del Made in France en París. Quesos gigantes, embutidos, sartenes, navajas, café, vino. Producto nacional. El escenario perfecto para la foto electoral estos días. En una esquina, se mueve sin gracia, público ni magnetismo Éric Zemmour, candidato ultraderechista, xenófobo, supremacista. A pocos metros, decenas de personas, cámaras, muchísimos adolescentes de barrios populares ―sudaderas, plumones negros, deportivas― esperan a su ídolo como si fuera una estrella del trap . Entonces, un hombre de 75 años, blanco, canoso, bien vestido aparece por una puerta lateral. Lo opuesto a un ídolo de la generación Z. No es Zohran Mamdani, ni Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez. No lleva coleta, no viste deportivas ni camisetas con eslóganes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Israel asfixia la esperanza en Gaza tras más de un año de bloqueo a la reconstrucción
items.description: Mohammed Al Jalis estaba durmiendo con su mujer y su bebé de dos meses cuando le despertó el agua colándose en su tienda de campaña en Deir El Balah, donde ha acabado malviviendo, desplazado desde Al Tufah, un barrio del este de Ciudad de Gaza hoy mayoritariamente en manos —hasta nadie sabe cuándo— de las tropas israelíes. “Pensábamos que la lona y la esterilla impedirían que entrara, pero nos sorprendió ver que se inundaba por completo”, recuerda. El matrimonio salió de la tienda con el bebé “sin saber adónde ir” para encontrarse a más gente en la misma situación: con la ropa empapada en medio del frío y la lluvia. “No pudimos salvar nada. Casi todo se mojó: la comida, la harina, las mantas, los colchones...” Seguir leyendo

items.title: La estrategia de Núcleo Nacional: reclutar jóvenes, agitar la calle y quedarse en la sombra
items.description: Las instrucciones de “el jefe” sobrevolaban el grupo de WhatsApp de White Boys, una organización juvenil de extrema derecha que operaba en Asturias. Aunque él apenas participara en las conversaciones, los cabecillas esperaban a conocer la opinión de Jesús Ruiz, dirigente de Núcleo Nacional (NN) de 62 años, antes de tomar decisiones. Temían que el hombre al que algunos se referían como el “ führer ” les recriminara haber actuado sin avisarle. Así, acudían a sus convocatorias para asistir a una parrillada (en la que posaron haciendo el saludo nazi junto a una bandera de la organización), o explicaban a los 40 integrantes que a Jesús no le gustaba que tomaran drogas. “No le mola nada, nada’, que lo sé yo. Que yo en Valladolid, me fumé un porro, y la que me cayó por la noche, jajaja. Fue increíble. Me dijo: ‘Somos antidroga 100x100”, explicaba uno de los jóvenes que transmitía las instrucciones al resto. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mensajes al bajar del cayuco: “Mamá, soy Modou. Cogí un barco, llegué a España”
items.description: De un vistazo, es difícil distinguir a Modou, Maden y Yenkube. Visten el mismo abrigo acolchado azul, idénticas zapatillas de goma, chándales gemelos. Ovillados en las mantas de la Cruz Roja parecen cifras. Tres más, de una muy abultada: los más de 15.000 migrantes que desde mediados de octubre han llegado a Canarias a bordo de cayucos, llevando al archipiélago a una situación de emergencia migratoria extraordinaria . En noviembre, ya van 6.000. Los expertos aluden a razones geopolíticas para explicar la reactivación de la ruta (la situación crítica de Senegal , procedencia mayoritaria de los migrantes) y atmosféricas (los vientos alisios y la relajación de los controles), pero a Modou, Maden y Yenkube les bastan dos palabras para precisar qué les empuja: Futuro. Otro. Pagaron el mismo precio por él, unos 60.000 dalasis gambianos, 730 euros por un pasaje a una posibilidad. Las cifras coinciden, las historias no. Seguir leyendo
