items.title: Middle power aspirations
items.description: AS the global order shifts away from unipolarity toward fragmented multipolarity, middle powers have gained unprecedented strategic weight. In a fragmented multipolar world, middle powers serve as indispensable diplomatic bridges and economic shock absorbers that keep the international system functioning despite great-power paralysis. Middle powers lack hegemonic ambitions, and retain the credibility to mediate active conflicts, build agile issue-specific coalitions, and maintain open trade and supply-chain corridors across rival blocs. Ultimately, these middle powers are preventing total global bifurcation of the international system between Washington and Beijing by stabilising their immediate regions and upholding international rules. However, scholars and policymakers rarely agree on a single checklist for middle power status, largely because different states exert influence through different mechanisms. Some, such as South Korea or Australia, earn the label through thriving, high-tech economies and global trade integration. Others, like Norway or Qatar, leverage niche diplomacy and active mediation to punch above their geographic weight. Still others, such as Türkiye and Pakistan, rely primarily on formidable military capabilities and regional security projection. Scholars generally evaluate middle power status across three core pillars including military capability, diplomatic outreach, and comprehensive national strength. National strength is largely defined by sustainable economic vitality and technological adaptation. Over the past two years, Pakistan has demonstrated a resurgence in the first two arenas, vaulting itself back into global strategic relevance. Yet, because its third and most foundational pillar remains weak, Pakistan’s recognition as an emerging middle power rests on a fragile foundation that cannot endure without a decisive domestic economic pivot. A credible middle power must possess the military capacity to defend its sovereignty and project stabilising influence across its neighbourhood. Between 2025 and 2026, Pakistan highlighted its hard-power credentials through both high-intensity deterrence and institutionalised defence partnerships . History shows that hard power and ingenious statecraft cannot substitute for domestic economic strength. During the brief but severe four-day conflict with India in May 2025, South Asia witnessed its first multi-domain confrontation integrating aerial clashes, drone swarms, and precision missile exchanges. Pakistan’s military response, culminating in Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, demonstrated modern warfare capabilities and aerial superiority. Pakistan’s swift military response compelled a rapid White House-facilitated ceasefire on May 10. By denying a larger neighbour unilateral escalation dominance, Islamabad reinforced its conventional and strategic deterrence. Since May 2025, Pakistan translated its battlefield credibility into a web of security pacts across the Middle East and the Muslim world. In September 2025, Islamabad and Riyadh signed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement, and in August 2026, Pakistan joined Saudi Arabia and Türkiye to sign the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. These pacts not only created a formal collective deterrence network but also enhanced Islamabad’s strategic utility in the Gulf. The Badr agreement with Türkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia, has further strengthened Pakistan’s position as a net security provider of Arab Gulf states. Beyond military muscle, middle powers distinguish themselves through niche diplomacy. Following the outbreak of direct US-Israeli military hostilities against Iran in early 2026, traditional Gulf mediators found their channels strained. Adopting a posture of active neutrality, Islamabad stepped in. In March 2026, the US accepted Pakistan’s role as a primary conduit to Tehran, which led to the historic Islamabad peace talks in April 2026 and the subsequent June MoU that temporarily reopened the Strait of Hormuz. Even as the truce faced repeated strain through late 2026, the civil and military leadership of Pakistan continued shuttling proposals between Washington, Tehran, and European capitals. The decision to join Trump’s Gaza peace plan as a founding member also proved Islamabad could exercise diplomatic power beyond its immediate borders. However, despite these military and diplomatic milestones, history demonstrates that hard power and ingenious statecraft cannot substitute for domestic economic strength. In this third pillar, Pakistan exhibits severe structural deficits that undermine its middle power aspirations. Macroeconomic indicators showed surface stabilisation in FY2025-26 with inflation remaining between 7-9 per cent and GDP growth edging up to 3.7pc. However, the underlying growth model remains weak. For instance, investment hovers near 15pc of GDP, far below the 20-plus per cent threshold required to sustain the 6pc growth rates needed to absorb a booming youth population. Deindustrialisation and high energy costs continue to stifle export competitiveness. Foreign investors are largely concerned with the security situation in Balochistan and KP. Unrest in AJK has further marred prospects of foreign direct investment. The privatisation process is critically slow, while political consensus is absent over reforms for new provinces. With a low tax-to-GDP ratio and heavy external debt servicing, state solvency still relies heavily on remittances, multilateral bailouts, bilateral rollovers (such as a $3 billion Saudi cash deposit in April 2026) rather than productive capital formation. Hence, Pakistan today represents a textbook case of an asymmetric emerging middle power. Its disciplined military and seasoned diplomatic corps have successfully leveraged regional crises to earn Islamabad a seat at high-stakes global tables. However, geopolitical leverage built on security crises and external rent is inherently transactional. When regional wars subside or great-power priorities shift, Islamabad — lacking economic autonomy and technological innovation — will risk losing its strategic relevance. Therefore, to cement its status as a genuine middle power, Pakistan must execute an urgent domestic pivot. This requires dismantling elite economic capture, broadening the tax base, overhauling education to build a tech-literate workforce, and enhancing an export-driven industrial base. Until Islamabad matches its battlefield deterrence and diplomatic agility with sustainable economic sovereignty, its middle power status will remain an aspiration suspended over a precarious fault line. The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own. X: @itskhurramabbas Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Ligue des nations: Mbappé de retour face à la Turquie
items.description: L'attaquant Kylian Mbappé, forfait lors de la défaite des Bleus face à l'Italie jeudi (3-1), disputera la rencontre contre la Turquie dimanche à Bordeaux pour le compte de la Ligue des nations, a annoncé le sélectionneur Zinédine Zidane. « Mbappé sera avec nous demain », a affirmé Zidane devant les médias à la veille de ce match décisif pour la qualification en quarts de finale de la compétition. Touché aux ischio-jambiers mercredi à la veille du déplacement en Italie, le capitaine de l’équipe de France avait déclaré forfait avant de reprendre l'entraînement vendredi. Il était indisponible après le premier match de Zidane en tant qu’entraineur face à la Turquie (1-0), le 25 septembre, en raison d'une blessure au genou. Evoquant ses relations avec Mbappé, le sélectionneur a indiqué que « tout se passait parfaitement », relevant que la participation du meilleur buteur de l'histoire des Bleus dimanche « change tout ». Privés notamment de Kylian Mbappé et d'Ousmane Dembélé lors de la rencontre disputé à Milan, les Français se sont appuyés sur une attaque remaniée, avec Michael Olise, Désiré Doué et Bradley Barcola. Deuxième du groupe 1 à égalité avec l'Italie, la France aura besoin d’au moins un nul contre les Turcs pour valider son ticket en vue des quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations. The post Ligue des nations: Mbappé de retour face à la Turquie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Aviation professionals call for stronger training pathways for aspiring Ghanaian youth
items.description: Aviation professionals have called for stronger training opportunities and career guidance to prepare more young Ghanaians for employment in the aviation industry. They say while many young people aspire to become pilots, cabin crew members and other aviation professionals, limited access to information and structured training continues to make it difficult for some to navigate their way into the sector. The concerns were raised at the Take Off Experience, an initiative established by the founder of Global Aviation Consult, Ivy Hammond, to connect young people’s interest in aviation with practical guidance on entering the industry. Ms Hammond said she created the platform after observing that many aspiring professionals had ambitions but lacked the information and direction needed to pursue them. “The Take Off Experience came about because many young people have dreams, but they do not have the guidance. I wanted to bridge the gap between preparation and aviation,” she said. She hopes the initiative will inspire young people and help develop a pool of Ghanaian professionals capable of taking up different roles in the industry. “In the long run, I want to have professionals in the industry in Ghana who are capable of taking up roles. I want us to be able to tell everybody that we have the personnel in Ghana and we can make it work,” she added. Ms Hammond cautioned young people against viewing aviation as an industry defined only by glamour and luxury. She said pursuing a career in the sector requires preparation, discipline and a willingness to work hard. “If aviation is what you want to go into, do not let it end at a dream. Seek the right guidance. But note that this space is not all luxury. It involves a lot of hard work, commitment and selfless service,” she said. Former cabin crew member Josephine Smart, who is now retired, described the initiative as a timely intervention and called for more programmes to expose young people to the realities of aviation careers. “I must say that I am really impressed. I think it is long overdue. For someone to come up with this initiative is laudable,” she said. Mrs Smart also explained that recruitment into cabin crew positions is not necessarily conducted every year, as airlines generally advertise vacancies based on their staffing requirements. “Whatever airline is there now, unfortunately, recruitment is not done on a monthly basis. It is when they lack crew that they advertise for more. So, if in the next five or ten years they do not need any crew, they will not employ,” she explained. She believes an expansion in the number of airlines operating in Ghana could create more opportunities for people seeking to enter the industry. She also expressed hope that plans to establish a new national airline and revive Ghana Airways would create additional employment opportunities for young professionals. Retired Flight Lieutenant Kelly Yemoh Quarshie said the Take Off Experience provides an important platform for young people seeking answers about career opportunities in aviation. However, he argued that individual initiatives must be supported by a broader national effort to develop the skills and personnel required by the sector. He expressed concern about what he described as inadequate structured training opportunities for several aviation professions, including pilots, air traffic controllers, cabin crew and ticketing personnel. “We don’t have any national programme to train professionals in the aviation space, be it pilots, air traffic controllers, cabin crew or ticketing personnel. We are not training enough,” he said. His comments highlight the need for a more coordinated approach to aviation education, professional development and career planning. While initiatives such as the Take Off Experience seek to help young people understand the available career paths, stakeholders say sustained investment in training and the creation of more employment opportunities will be important to developing Ghana’s aviation workforce.

items.title: Judges must speak
items.description: A JUDGMENT is a public document, written in the name of the Constitution and delivered in open court. The people may read it, praise it and criticise it, and the academy, bar, press and civil society should do so freely. Criticism is not the enemy of judicial authority; it is its source. A judiciary whose judgments are never read critically will never grow. One voice is largely missing from that conversation: the judge who wrote the judgment. In Pakistan, judges mostly retire into silence. That must change. Retired judges must come out among the people, above all into the law schools, and explain their reasoning, or say, with hindsight: “I think I got that one wrong.” Such candour teaches the profession and builds public trust and confidence in the institution. A sitting judge who knows retirement means facing the public will brush nothing under the carpet. A judgment open to criticism falls into one of three kinds. The first plainly violates the Constitution and the law. The second was legally permissible when given, but its consequences proved damaging. The third is the judgment in which the judge was complicit, bending the law to reach an outcome decided elsewhere. To assess one, read it whole and in context: the moment, the circumstances, the law as it then stood. Then ask whether it was permissible, plainly wrong, or the judge simply listening to power. Let me test three of my own. In Pakistan, judges mostly retire into silence. That must change. In the 2023 case on Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa elections, Justice Jamal Khan Mandokhail and I wanted the high courts to decide first: Lahore had already ordered elections, with appeals pending, and Peshawar was seized of the petitions. Law and practice both counselled that restraint. We read the outcome as four to three, because two colleagues who had already voted to dismiss could not, in our view, be dropped from the count; Justice Athar Minallah, one of them, recorded as much. In hindsight, the mistake, I believe, was the chief justice’s hurried leap in; hearing the matter in appeal, the court could have spoken with one voice. Had we set the count aside and presented a united court, whether that would have produced elections is anyone’s guess. Later, the chief justice’s own bench rejected the four-three objection and fixed May 14 for Punjab polls, yet could not enforce it. The date passed, contempt was never pursued, and the court fell silent. The larger lesson is that a court must stand united, and the chief justice’s strength is the real spine that holds it together. The Supreme Court as it stands today shows how much rests on that spine. In the Justice Qazi Faez Isa case , the court unanimously quashed the reference, the majority for malice in law; I held it malicious in fact as well. The majority directed the FBR to examine the family’s properties and report to the council; three of us held that no direction was needed, the FBR being free to act under the tax law. On review, that view prevailed. No one is above the law, and no one below its protection: a judge’s spouse answers under the tax law, a judge under the Code of Conduct, only in accordance with law. I am often asked whether we saved the wrong man. We saved due process and the independence of the judiciary, and in doing so we saved a man. What people thought of him later was not our concern then. A judgment is not a character certificate. In the Practice and Procedure case, I believed, and still believe, that the court had to become collegial rather than be run by one man. Opening the door was not itself the mistake; so long as the court stood united, no one could have walked through it. What we failed to see was that the court was weak within, and weakness inside invites those outside. And it did: a 2024 ordinance gave the chief justice’s nominee a seat on the bench-forming committee. Had earlier chief justices brought in the collegial model through the full court, that door need never have opened from outside. This is a lesson, not an accusation. Each choice was made in good faith, within the law. In hindsight, wiser choices may have been available, but choosing in the moment is the judicial function, and there the judge must be trusted. Unless a judge was complicit, there is nothing to apologise for, only lessons to share. What must worry us most is complicity. It is not an error of judgment but a surrender of it, and it has hollowed out our courts. A judgment bent to power may be overruled, but the betrayal stays on the record. Error is part of judging. Capitulation is not. And complicity has a way of showing its face, in the promotions, benefits and advantages that later reward it. Today, that trail must be made visible. A word to the critics. Those quick to call out judicial error must be as open-hearted in acknowledging courage. Dissent, refusal of oath and resignation are the building blocks of an independent judiciary. Ask what a judge gained by resigning when a simple yes would have secured everything. Nothing, except the honour of the institution. Criticism that records every failure and never that courage leaves the next generation no one to look up to. So let the conversation begin, and let it be honest. Let judges speak: give the context of their decisions, own their errors without fear and explain their choices without apology. And let complicity be named for what it is. Judicial independence has never been absolute. Sadly, there has always been a chink in the armour, a door left ajar, and someone willing to push it open. No single judgment or judge will close that door. But an honest and open conversation, carried from one generation to the next, can. That will be the real victory: not a court that never errs, but a court with no door through which power can enter. The writer is a professor of practice at SAHSOL, Lums, and currently a distinguished visiting fellow at Yale University. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: ANALYSIS: An unLucky bet
items.description: WHEN Lucky Motor Corporation (LMC) began assembling the Peugeot 2008 in the year 2022, it was launched with much fanfare. Here was a European name in a market long dominated by Japanese, Korean and, more recently, Chinese brands. Today, fresh bookings for the SUV have been suspended. At least one of its dealerships now sells Chinese vehicles, and dealers speak cautiously about the model’s future. The company says production has not stopped. Petrol prices shot up after the Middle East conflict began in February, forcing buyers towards various types of electrified vehicles. A petrol-only 1,200cc European SUV now finds itself on the wrong side of that move. Other petrol models have also struggled. Honda Atlas Cars recently discontinued the Honda BR-V. LMC’s own hybrids have felt the pressure too. On Nov 3, the company cut the prices of the 1.6T FWD Kia Sportage L HEV and the 1.6T AWD HEV by Rs700,000 and Rs800,000, respectively. The Peugeot’s prices have also been cut sharply. LMC’s website lists the 2008 Active at Rs5.799 million, down from Rs6.999m. The 2008 Allure is listed at Rs6.499m, down from Rs7.799m. Both offers are subject to terms and conditions. Lucky Motor’s Peugeot 2008 arrived in 2022 as Pakistan’s only locally assembled European SUV. Four years later, high petrol prices and a move by buyers to electrified cars have left it out of step with the market. LMC Chief Executive Muhammad Faisal confirmed to Dawn that the company has stopped taking new orders, but denied claims that the assembly line has also been shut down. ‘Only bookings closed’ “We are not taking fresh bookings at the moment and are delivering those vehicles which have been booked earlier. We still have orders for Peugeot which we are serving and therefore have not stopped production,” he said. According to Mr Faisal, LMC has assembled more than 6,000 Peugeot vehicles at its plant in the Port Bin Qasim Industrial Park since the first quarter of 2022. He said all Kia service centres can provide after-sales service to Peugeot customers. “We still have parts in stock for Peugeot,” he added. Not everyone in the market tells the same story, though. Some industry sources claim that production was quietly halted a few months ago. They say this has worried owners about future after-sales service and the supply of expensive parts. Dealers upcountry gave Dawn differing accounts. Some said only fresh bookings had been suspended, while others said production had been discontinued, but LMC denies this. Dawn visited Rashid Minhas Road in Karachi and found that Macca Motors, once an authorised Peugeot showroom, now displays vehicles from the Chinese brand GAC. A showroom employee also confirmed that bookings for the Peugeot had been suspended. Good car at the wrong time LMC’s website still lists five dedicated Peugeot showrooms: one each in Islamabad, Sialkot and Karachi, and two in Lahore. Market sources, however, claim the dedicated outlets are no longer operating as such. Dawn also surveyed the Sunday Car Bazaar in Sector 11-D, North Karachi, which is considered the city’s main used-car market, but no Peugeot was on offer. Owners who spoke to Dawn had a lot of praise for the vehicle’s looks, driving experience, comfort, suspension, and durability, which they said put it ahead of its Japanese, Korean, and Chinese rivals. Their main concerns were about running costs, parts availability and poor resale value. One owner said the car’s fuel economy of 8 to 8.5 kilometres per litre was a serious drawback. Petrol prices are now easing, he said, but the mileage still puts buyers off. “I purchased it for Rs7.5m two years back, but the new model is now priced at Rs6.5m. I am getting only Rs5.5-5.7m if I sell,” he said. Another owner said LMC had not told existing customers anything about the model’s future. It had also not assured them that parts would remain available, which was hurting the reputation of a good SUV. LMC’s partnership with Peugeot began in mid-2019, when it signed an MoU and expression of interest with Groupe PSA, now part of the Stellantis Group. The pivot towards China The company was then known as Kia Lucky Motors. In 2021, it signed a Licence and Technical Assistance Agreement with Stellantis to assemble and distribute Peugeot vehicles in Pakistan. Earlier this year, it signed an agreement with China’s Guangzhou Automobile Group (GAC) to launch and assemble them in Pakistan. Mr Faisal said the Kia Sportage was “going strong” and could compete with other models in its segment. He said the Picanto had completed its lifecycle. items.title: Muddled hierarchy
items.description: THE Federal Constitutional Court marked its first anniversary on Friday with a commemorative stamp. Speaking on the occasion, its chief justice remarked on how fleeting the year had been. Litigants, lawyers and the judges of the Supreme Court might have described it differently. A year after the 27th Amendment rewrote the structure of the country’s judiciary, one of the most basic questions raised by the new order remains unanswered: which court, the FCC or the SC, has the final word? This was, perhaps, bound to happen. Critics had foreseen problems in the short and hurried route the government took from the 26th to the 27th Amendment . In October 2024, the 26th Amendment carved constitutional benches out of the SC, with their members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission in which judges no longer held a majority. Critics warned then that the independence of the judiciary was at stake. Barely a year later, and in evident haste, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges resigned in protest the day it became law. Thousands of cases were soon transferred to the FCC, and the SC was stripped of its constitutional jurisdiction. What has followed has seemed less a division of labour than a contest for primacy. Last December, the FCC held that its rulings bind all courts, including the SC, but that the latter’s do not bind the FCC. In May, Chief Justice Yahya Afridi pushed back, ruling that the two are coordinate courts, neither an appellate forum over the other. Last month, the FCC rebuked an SC bench for revisiting a matter the FCC considered settled, raising concerns over judicial discipline. The sparring shows no sign of stopping. The text of the amendment arguably favours the FCC, while the SC relies on the overall constitutional scheme to assert its position. That both positions can be argued is precisely the problem. Two hasty amendments have created an ambiguity that leaves the two courts defining their relationship through pointed observations in their judgments. The costs are borne by litigants, whose cases risk being shuttled between forums. The FCC, meanwhile, has worked with seven judges against a sanctioned strength of 13. And its order barring the Peshawar High Court from hearing petitions on emergency and governor’s rule in KP has pushed citizens away from a court closer to home. Since parliament created this ambiguity, it must now resolve it. The jurisdiction of the two courts and a mechanism for settling disputes between them should be spelt out in law, not left to judges to fight over. Lastly, the judiciary’s structure is not its only problem. As long as its independence remains in doubt, it will struggle to win public confidence. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Gas output halves in 10 years, says SSGC chief
items.description: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) has been forced to restrict supply to domestic consumers three meal times a day because of depleting indigenous production over the past decade, its managing director said on Saturday. According to Muhammad Amin Rajput, the schedule was necessary as the country’s gas production had fallen about 50 per cent over the last decade, while imported LNG supplies, too, were hard to come by since April due to the Iran war. “By focusing on supply during cooking hours, the company can protect domestic consumers,” the managing director said in an exclusive interview with Dawn. He said SSGC’s gas availability had fallen to around 605 million cubic feet per day due to depletion in gas fields, compared with 695mmcfd last year. “Of this, around 300mmcfd is being given to domestic consumers, while the rest is supplied to industry, power and fertiliser sectors,” Mr Rajput added. The utility has decided to supply gas during the breakfast, lunch and dinner windows to ensure that every household got the fuel when it mattered most. “The SSGC has been monitoring availability continuously since last week,” Mr Rajput said. Supply to households restricted to three meal times He said domestic gas supply in the city was adequate. Residents in many areas, however, complained the flame was too low for cooking purposes. “A localised issue should not be generalised across the entire network that serves roughly 50,000 kilometres of pipelines, 16,000 of them in Karachi alone. The SSGC has 3.2 million customers across Sindh and Balochistan, including two million in Karachi,” Mr Rajput observed. Use of compressors, pumps The SSGC MD blamed the low pressure on the illegal use of gas compressors and suction pumps. These devices can drain away the supply to an entire block or building, he cautioned. “Besides being illegal, substandard devices pose safety risks and have caused property damage, and sometimes even loss of life.” Mr Rajput urged consumers to report such use, saying that removing the devices would help restore pressure during supply hours, even though they may inflate bills by distorting meter readings. He said his company had rehabilitated about 7,000 kilometres of distribution pipelines in 2025-26, replacing ageing and corroded pipes, mostly in Karachi. “That has improved pressure at tail-end locations and reduced unaccounted-for gas.” He said the situation was further compounded by substantially reduced availability of RLNG supplies from Qatar. “Besides meeting domestic requirements, the Petroleum Division has secured limited gas supplies to meet other critical needs. These include the power and fertiliser sectors,” the SSGC chief said. These competing requirements call for prudent management and judicious allocation of available resources. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Parliament’s nod deemed a must for referendum
items.description: • President, prime minister insist any move to create new provinces must follow Constitution • Zardari reiterates PPP’s opposition to division of Sindh • Naqvi’s ‘message’, Imran’s situation also discussed LAHORE: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday agreed to “strictly adhere to constitutional provisions” governing the creation of new provinces or administrative units, with any proposed referendum on the contentious issue also requiring parliamentary approval. Official sources privy to the development told Dawn that the understanding was reached during a meeting between the two leaders at the prime minister’s Model Town residence, amid a fresh debate over the creation of additional provinces and a proposal by the interior minister to seek public opinion through a referendum. President Zardari, who was accompanied by former prime minister Raja Pervez Ashraf and Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, made it clear that the PPP’s position remained aligned with the Sindh Assembly’s resolution opposing the creation of new provinces. He stressed that any move in this direction must strictly follow the procedure prescribed by the Constitution, a position endorsed by PM Shehbaz, the sources said. PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq and the prime minister’s sons Hamza and Suleman were also present at the meeting. The two leaders also agreed that parliament could not be bypassed in deciding whether a referendum should be held and what questions should be put to the public, according to the sources. “The majority in parliament will decide whether a referendum is to be held and what its question(s) should be. Without consensus, the matter cannot move an inch. Parliament cannot be bypassed,” an official source quoted the meeting as agreeing. The discussion came two days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the creation of new provinces or administrative units, arguing that the exercise could settle the debate once and for all. He had also assured political parties that they would be taken on board before any decision was finalised. However, the PPP leadership appears unwilling to soften its position, particularly on Sindh. The party has consistently invoked a unanimous resolution passed by the Sindh Assembly opposing the province’s division, maintaining that it reinforces its position against any such move. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and other senior party leaders have repeatedly declared that the division of Sindh is neither legally nor politically acceptable to the party. The debate has also highlighted differing positions within the ruling coalition. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif recently argued that Pakistan could have as many as 12 provinces if the exercise was guided by administrative requirements rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations. He maintained that the country’s growing population necessitated smaller administrative units capable of delivering public services more efficiently. However, the PML-N has so far refrained from articulating a formal policy, saying it would present its position when the matter came before parliament. Naqvi’s message, Imran’s issue The sources said President Zardari and PM Shehbaz also held a brief one-on-one meeting to discuss a message reportedly conveyed to the president by Interior Minister Naqvi during his recent visit to Nawabshah. The issue of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan also came under discussion. According to the sources, the meeting was informed that Mr Khan’s recent hours-long interaction with his lawyers and the release of his two sisters from jail were not linked to any particular behind-the-scenes deve­lopment. Meanwhile, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office said the two leaders held detailed discussions on the country’s overall political, economic and security situation, emphasising coordination among the ruling coalition partners. The official statement did not specifically mention the discussion on new provinces or the proposed referendum. PM Shehbaz also briefed President Zardari on his recent visit to Turkiye, where he attended the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) and highlighted Pakistan’s efforts on climate action. The two leaders exchanged views on cooperation among allied parties, continued consultation and progress on public welfare initiatives. They reaffirmed their commitment to working together to accelerate economic stability and development, the statement added. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Microsoft annonce le rétablissement complet de ses services après une panne mondiale
items.description: Le géant américain Microsoft a annoncé samedi avoir complètement « rétabli le service », mettant fin à une panne mondiale qui a perturbé pendant plus d'un jour et demi l'accès à ses messageries Outlook et à plusieurs de ses applications en ligne depuis jeudi. « Nous avons mené à bien nos efforts pour résoudre le problème à l'origine de l'incident et rétabli le service pour les utilisateurs et les régions qui restaient affectés », a écrit le géant américain des logiciels sur le réseau X. Le groupe, dont les applications Microsoft 365 comptent plus de 450 millions d'utilisateurs professionnels payants, sans compter les particuliers, avait présenté vendredi ses excuses. Il assurait que la panne était due à « un problème technique », sans lien avec une cyberattaque ou l'intelligence artificielle. Selon Microsoft, l'incident a été provoqué par « un problème survenu lors d'une précédente augmentation des capacités du réseau ». Ce défaut, passé inaperçu, s'est révélé lors d'une modification plus récente de ce réseau : une partie des serveurs a cessé de fonctionner, et ceux qui restaient ont été débordés, comme une autoroute dont on fermerait plusieurs voies. Le groupe a promis un rapport complet une fois son enquête terminée. La panne a débuté jeudi sur le continent américain, Microsoft reconnaissant ensuite qu'elle pouvait toucher des utilisateurs « dans n'importe quelle région » du monde. Outre Outlook, elle a perturbé la plateforme de communication Teams et l'assistant d'IA Copilot. Administrations, hôpitaux et entreprises ont été gênés dans de nombreux pays. Aux États-Unis, le réseau hospitalier de l'université de l'Iowa a dû demander à ses patients de passer par leur portail en ligne pour joindre leurs soignants, et le fabricant de camions Workhorse a reporté la publication de ses résultats trimestriels. Microsoft a par ailleurs mis en garde samedi contre « une campagne d'hameçonnage active exploitant la perturbation » : de faux courriels imitant ses notifications affirment que des messages bloqués pendant la panne seront supprimés sous 24 heures si le destinataire ne clique pas pour les récupérer, a indiqué sur X sa division de veille sur les menaces informatiques. L'incident a également affecté l'accès à certains logiciels de Microsoft via des assistants d'intelligence artificielle tiers, notamment ChatGPT et Claude. En juillet 2024, une autre panne informatique, liée à une mise à jour défectueuse, avait paralysé des aéroports, des hôpitaux et de nombreuses autres organisations à travers le monde. The post Microsoft annonce le rétablissement complet de ses services après une panne mondiale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: US flight chaos caused by repair of old copper wiring: Trump admin
items.description: Weary travellers endured more flight disruptions as service resumed at US airports after an hours-long total stoppage, with officials saying the situation should return to normal on Sunday. The Trump administration blamed the mess that began Friday on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines. The nationwide ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before they were due to depart by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events. “Tired. Exhausted. Frustrated. Yeah, you know, it’s just a mess, right?” Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP as she waited for a flight Saturday morning at New York’s La Guardia airport. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) chief Bryan Bedford said that 12,000 flights were cancelled on Friday and between four and five thousand flights out of 41,000 scheduled for Saturday were likely to be cancelled as well. But as of Saturday evening, the tracking website FlightAware had recorded more than 6,200 cancelled flights. Speaking at a news conference in Washington, Bedford offered a “sincere apology to the American travelling public.” He predicted a full resumption of flight schedules by “close of business on Sunday.” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday’s four-hour ground stop was declared after maintenance work to upgrade an old copper wire to a high-speed fiber cable had caused “issues” with communication with airplanes and radar feeds. “Either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment… it started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system,” Duffy told reporters. In another embarrassment, Saturday’s news conference — where administration officials also appealed for more funds to upgrade outdated systems — was delayed due to technical problems with the audio feed. Returning to normal Friday’s disruption was only the second time such a ground stoppage had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks . The nationwide halt was lifted at 8:15 pm Eastern Time Friday (6:15am PKT Saturday). During the outage, footage from airports showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways and passengers thronging concourses, desperate for information. FAA officials reopened the airspace “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Duffy. Tim Johnson, consumer director at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, said although US flights have resumed, there could be “some follow-on disruption” as airlines re-book passengers and get all services back to normal. At La Guardia airport, some travellers were more sanguine than others about the continued disruption of their flights. “We’re stuck here for the next, I don’t know, 36 hours,” said Pat Curlett, a 62-year-old Ford worker. “No one expects the whole airline system to go down,” said 77-year-old traveler Steven Rathe, who was waiting to embark on a four-leg trip from New York to Albuquerque. “We’re lucky it wasn’t longer. So they’re flying today and for that I’m grateful.” Ageing infrastructure The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos — it also raised serious concerns about the country’s ageing infrastructure. Duffy appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernise the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.” “Cut the crap,” retorted Illinois state governor and prominent Democrat, JB Pritzker, on X. “Trump and Republicans have controlled Congress and could have funded the system.” New York Governor Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign or be fired by Trump, writing on X: “We’re fortunate no lives were lost.” US lawmakers called for investigations into what caused the massive disruption and whether the country is adequately secure from cyber criminality. “If today proves anything, it’s that we need to update our air traffic control system & rebuild our airport infrastructure,” Republican Senator Eric Schmitt said on X. President Donald Trump was uncharacteristically quiet about the outage that had knock-on effects for international flights to and from the United States, making no public statement about the ground stop as of Saturday night.

items.title: Creating new smaller provinces a ‘national necessity’: Kamal
items.description: KARACHI: Senior Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader and Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal on Saturday called the creation of smaller provinces “a national necessity” and not a “political desire”, arguing that the existing four-province administrative structure has failed to deliver and that the formation of new provinces is essential for the effective functioning of the state. Addressing the inauguration ceremony of the Sindh regional office of the Allied Health Professionals Council (AHPC), the minister said Pakistan’s provinces were exceptionally large compared with those of many countries worldwide. He said Punjab alone had a larger population than 180 countries, while the other three provinces were also more populous than many countries. Referring to dozens of provinces Iran, Afghanistan and India have, he highlighted the difference between Pakistan’s administrative structure and those of other countries in the region. The minister said that 57.5 per cent of the divisible federal revenue pool was allocated to the provinces, which had received a combined Rs8,844 billion during the current financial year. However, he regretted that the funds were not reaching villages and grassroots communities because provinces had failed to devolve resources and authority further down the administrative hierarchy. MQM-P leader rejects concerns over national unity; likens new provinces to building additional rooms in a house to accommodate expanding family “The biggest problem is that the provinces have not devolved resources to the grassroots level. The money is being allocated to the provinces but unfortunately not reaching the villages,” he added. Describing Karachi as Pakistan’s economic engine, he said the city’s economic potential remained largely untapped, and it could play a pivotal role in pulling the country out of its economic difficulties. “Even 10pc of Karachi’s potential has not been tapped yet. The IMF cannot pull Pakistan out of this economic quagmire, but Karachi can,” he said. He explained that creating smaller provinces should not be seen as a threat to national unity. He gave an example of an expanding family that needed additional rooms to accommodate its growing members. “When a family grows, a new room has to be built. It does not mean that the house is being broken up or divided,” he said. Speaking about the AHPC’s regional office in Sindh, the minister called it an important step towards facilitating healthcare professionals and students in the province. He said they would no longer need to travel to Islamabad to resolve their professional and administrative issues. The new office would provide a one-window facility for allied health professionals, students and educational institutions across Sindh, enabling them to access information and seek solutions to their problems locally, he said, expressing the hope that similar council offices would be established in all provinces. The minister also stressed the need to transform Pakistan’s growing population into a skilled workforce, saying the government could not provide public-sector jobs to all 260 million citizens. He said creating employment opportunities for a rapidly expanding population remained a major national challenge and that the country needed to focus on skills development, technical education and human resource development. He said countries with large populations had achieved economic progress by investing in skills and developing their human capital, adding that Pakistan must adopt a similar approach, particularly for its youth. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Sales tax gets new enforcement structure to cut collection gap
items.description: ISLAMABAD: After 17 years of integration, the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection. The decision marks a major reform in tax administration, providing for the selection of officers within the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) and the separation of functional responsibilities, including tax collection and legal matters, to address persistent weaknesses that have contributed to the revenue gap, senior tax officials told Dawn on Saturday. At the chief commissioner level, the administrative structure for sales tax and income tax will remain unchanged for now. However, functional separation will begin at the commissioner level and extend to subordinate officers, with dedicated officials assigned exclusively to sales tax matters. A dedicated member for sales tax and federal excise duty will report directly to the FBR chairman. The new member, with three chiefs and their teams, will give sales tax and federal excise duty continuous attention through data analysis, operations, and follow-up on selected cases. Government will separate sales and income tax functions within IRS Within each chief commissioner’s jurisdiction, separate sales tax zones will be established, headed by commissioners and supported by additional deputy and assistant commissioners. The restructuring will begin at Large Taxpayer Offices on Dec 1, followed by Corporate Tax Offices and Regional Tax Offices. The transition is expected to be completed within two months. The chief commissioners and Member IRS (Operations) will retain administrative and operational control, while the newly designated member will provide technical oversight and coordinate enforcement activities. Both taxes will continue to be administered within the IRS, rather than through separate services. As part of the process, the FBR has begun conducting specialised tests to identify officers with the required expertise in sales tax and income tax administration. “We have already launched an exercise to identify competent officers,” an official said, adding that the assessment would help assign officers to functions matching their professional capabilities. The need for functional separation also emerged from the widening sales tax revenue gap despite its relatively small taxpayer base. Sales tax accounts for nearly 55pc of the combined Rs6.2tr revenue gap, while approximately 90pc of its collections come from just 15,000 taxpayers, according to internal FBR estimates. Official figures showed that around 313,000 persons were registered for sales tax in early 2024, of whom only 190,000 filed tax returns, including many declaring no taxable transactions. In comparison, the number of active income tax return filers stood at approximately 6 million. It was pointed out that the integrated administrative structure had also weakened accountability, as IRS officers could meet their combined revenue targets by concentrating on income tax collections, while paying less attention to sales tax enforcement. A recent proficiency test conducted in Karachi further exposed the imbalance, with officers performing better in practical income tax matters than in sales tax administration, reflecting their greater exposure to income tax work. The FBR’s experience with production monitoring also demonstrated the benefits of targeted enforcement. In 12 manufacturing sectors where monitoring systems were introduced, the revenue gap declined by 12 percentage points of potential collections over two years, while it increased by nine percentage points in seven sectors without such systems. Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will analyse this information and pursue cases involving underreported sales, questionable input tax claims, and other compliance failures, rather than dividing their attention between income tax and sales tax responsibilities. In 2009, the then government, as part of the World Bank project, transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise from Customs to the IRS. The major reasons for integration were that the two taxes are closely linked, because what an officer finds in a sales tax case often gives rise to an income tax demand, and that placing them under different officers would break this link. However, after 17 years of integration, official data showed substantial revenue gaps in both taxes, raising questions about the arrangement’s effectiveness. The sales tax revenue gap was estimated at Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax. Officials said the original justification for integration had also weakened with the introduction of a common digital system operated by Pakistan Revenue Automation Ltd. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: World Bank okays $300m for Sindh’s water, sanitation services
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The World Bank has approved $300 million in financing to expand access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene services for 1.5 million people in selected rural areas of Sindh. The financing will support the Sindh Trans­formational Accele­rated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation, and Hygiene Services Phase 1 Project (STAR WASH-1), the World Bank’s resident mission in Islamabad announced on Saturday. The project is expected to generate more than 14,000 jobs and support the formalisation of the Sindh People’s Housing for Flood Affectees as a rural water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) utility company. “Stunting is among Pakistan’s most severe and persistent human capital challenges, and unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene is a major underlying driver. By expanding access to these services for 1.5m people in rural Sindh, this project will help address one of the root causes of child stunting,” said Bolormaa Amgaabazar, the World Bank country director for Pakistan. Unsafe water and poor sanitation expose young children to repeated bouts of diarrhoea, impairing nutrient absorption and limiting their physical and cognitive development. More than half of children under five in rural Sindh are stunted. STAR WASH-1 aims to provide 1.5m people with access to safe drinking water and safely managed sanitation and hygiene services. The project will finance climate-resilient infrastructure, including solar-powered water supply systems and improved sanitation facilities. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan guidebooks author dies at 83
items.description: GENEVA: Isobel Shaw, an Irish-born travel writer whose guidebooks introduced thousands of visitors to Pakistan, died on Wednesday (Nov 11) at her home in St-Cergue, Switzerland. She was 83. Ms Shaw first came to Pakistan in 1978, when her husband, Robert Shaw, was posted to Islamabad as the Ford Foundation’s representative. During her three years in Islamabad she learnt Urdu and, with Hilary Adamson, wrote A Traveller’s Guide to Pakistan, published in Islamabad in 1981 and one of the first modern guidebooks to the country. Her Pakistan Handbook (1989) was shortlisted for the Thomas Cook Travel and Guide Book Awards, and her illustrated guide to Pakistan ran to five editions. With her son, Ben Shaw, she wrote the Pakistan Trekking Guide (1993) and a trekking guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush, published in Lahore in 2013. Other writers on the region recommended her as the best guidebook writer on Pakistan. During the 1990s she worked as a tourism consultant to the government of Pakistan and gave the keynote address at the Pakistan Tourism Convention in Karachi in 1993. After the 2005 earthquake she gave talks to raise funds for orthopaedic care for survivors. The same year, the Pakistan Society in London honoured her for advancing public knowledge and understanding of Pakistan in Britain. Her last book, Trekking Guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush of Northern Pakistan, was published by Vanguard Books in Lahore in 2013. She returned to Chitral that year, at the age of 70. Born Isobel O’Beirne in Meath, Ireland, in 1943, she studied at Newnham College, Cambridge. She had lived near Geneva since 1981 and is survived by her three children, nine grandchildren and a great-granddaughter. Published in Dawn, November 15th, 2026

items.title: Hamas says senior armed commander killed in Israeli strike
items.description: Hamas' armed wing said on Sunday that ​a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the ‌October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli air strike. The Al-Qassam Brigades identified the commander as Samir Abu ​Younis, 53, the commander of its Rafah brigade, and ​said he was killed on Saturday. The Israeli military said on Sunday that it had struck a senior commander ​in Hamas' armed wing but did not identify him. Medics said ​Abu Younis was killed, and others were wounded in an air strike that targeted him in a street in the Mawasi area of ​Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip. Hamas said Abu ​Younis joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and had held several senior ‌operational roles in Rafah before becoming commander of the brigade. Hamas said his funeral would be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis. An October 2025 ceasefire halted major fighting but has ​not stopped ​Israeli attacks or secured Hamas' disarmament. Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since ​the ceasefire went into effect. Five Israeli ​soldiers have been killed during the same period. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel's military campaign against Gaza, ​launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about ​1,200 people in southern Israel in October 2023. items.title: Abiodun pledges more development for Remoland
items.description: .as Odemo seeks ₦600m for palace reconstruction, highlights security gains, attracts investors to Isara By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the development of Remoland, pledging sustained investments in infrastructure, healthcare, education and economic growth as his tenure gradually winds down. Abiodun also assured the people of Isara-Remo that his administration was working towards establishing a legacy hospital in the community to improve access to quality healthcare and strengthen the delivery of medical services in the area. The governor gave the assurances on Saturday at the 57th Afotamodi Day Festival held in Isara-Remo, Ogun State. The celebration, themed “Preserving Our Heritage, Restoring Our Glory,” also featured a fundraising initiative for the reconstruction of the palace of the Odemo of Isara-Remo, Oba Peter Oluwole Ogunbayo, with an estimated target of N600 million. Speaking through the State Commissioner for Environment, Mr Ola Oresanya, Abiodun described the annual festival as more than a cultural gathering, noting that its 57-year history had established it as an enduring symbol of the identity, traditions and collective aspirations of the Isara people. “For 57 years, this festival has remained a powerful symbol of the history, values, traditions and collective identity of the Isara people,” he said. The governor noted that the festival had continued to provide a platform for preserving the community’s cultural heritage, strengthening family bonds, promoting religious harmony and fostering unity among residents. He commended the Afotamodi Planning Committee, traditional institutions and other stakeholders for initiating the palace reconstruction project, urging Isara indigenes at home and abroad to support its successful completion. According to him, the palace represents far more than a physical structure, as it embodies the authority of the traditional institution, cultural continuity and the collective dignity of the community. “A palace is not merely a physical structure; it is an enduring symbol of traditional authority, cultural continuity, communal pride and the dignity of the institution it represents,” Abiodun stated. On his administration’s development agenda, the governor assured the people that efforts to bridge infrastructure gaps and improve transportation networks across rural and urban communities would be sustained. He disclosed that plans were being advanced for a legacy hospital in Isara-Remo, describing the proposed facility as a strategic investment in the health and wellbeing of the people. He said the hospital, when completed, would improve access to medical services, create employment opportunities and serve as a lasting social investment in the community. Abiodun added that his administration was also strengthening primary healthcare delivery, expanding educational opportunities and investing in skills acquisition, youth empowerment and agricultural development. He said the government remained committed to improving the learning environment, supporting access to quality education and enhancing food security through interventions targeted at farmers and other participants in the agricultural value chain. The governor maintained that the true measure of development was not merely the number of infrastructure projects delivered, but the extent to which such interventions improved people’s living standards and expanded their economic opportunities. He further pledged to leave behind a state with stronger institutions, improved infrastructure, expanded social services, greater investment opportunities and a more vibrant economy. Abiodun urged the incoming administration to sustain ongoing development programmes, warning against allowing political succession to undermine the state’s progress. “Development must be a continuous process, and the progress of Ogun State must never be sacrificed on the altar of political succession,” he said. In his address, the Odemo of Isara-Remo, Oba Peter Oluwole Ogunbayo, described the proposed reconstruction of the palace as a historic responsibility requiring the collective commitment of the entire community. The monarch said the N600 million fundraising target should not be viewed merely as a financial obligation but as a collective investment in preserving the town’s history and restoring the dignity of its traditional institution. “For generations, the Odemo’s Palace has symbolised our heritage. It is therefore our responsibility to ensure that future generations inherit a befitting palace that reflects the dignity of our traditional institution and the rich history of Isara-Remo,” he said. He appealed to community associations, corporate organisations, business leaders and Isara indigenes in the diaspora to contribute generously towards the project. Oba Ogunbayo also used the occasion to highlight measures taken by his administration to strengthen security in Isara-Remo since his emergence as the traditional ruler. He disclosed that about 42 tactical and specialist police personnel had been deployed to the community following engagements with relevant security authorities amid heightened security concerns. The monarch said he had also pursued the establishment of a Nigeria Police Force Area Command headquarters in Isara-Remo to strengthen security coordination and improve response to emergencies across the area. Referring to security challenges in neighbouring communities, particularly the attack on Atoba Village, Orile-Oko, Oba Ogunbayo said he had engaged relevant authorities to support efforts towards securing the release of abducted victims and intensifying security patrols along vulnerable routes. He commended the Ogunbayo Family for providing temporary accommodation for the Police Area Command and acknowledged the Daramola Dynasty Foundation’s efforts towards the construction of a permanent facility for the command. The traditional ruler also recognised local organisations for donating patrol vehicles and other security equipment to support the activities of security agencies. He particularly appreciated four quarry companies for their combined donation of N65 million towards security and community development initiatives. “These efforts demonstrate what responsible leadership, community participation and strategic partnerships can achieve,” the monarch said. He, however, emphasised that security remained a collective responsibility, requiring sustained cooperation among traditional institutions, government authorities, security agencies, corporate organisations and residents. On economic development, Oba Ogunbayo disclosed that three companies had been attracted to Isara-Remo and had commenced land-clearing activities on properties acquired from the Ogun State Government under the Isara Industrial Cluster II Scheme along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. He expressed optimism that the investments would stimulate economic activities, create jobs and open up opportunities for youths, artisans, traders and other residents of the community. The monarch further revealed that plans were underway for the development of a multipurpose market close to the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. According to him, the proposed market would provide an additional commercial platform for farmers, traders, entrepreneurs and business operators to expand their activities and contribute to the local economy. He reaffirmed his commitment to working with the state government, investors and other community stakeholders to position Isara-Remo as an attractive destination for productive investments and sustainable economic growth. Oba Ogunbayo said the 57th Afotamodi Day celebration should serve as a renewed call for unity, cultural preservation and collective action towards building a prosperous community for present and future generations. “The greatness of a community is measured not only by its heritage but also by what its people achieve through unity, responsible leadership and collective action,” he said. The Akarigbo and paramount ruler of Remo land, Oba Babatunde Ajayi in his remark urged the sons and daughters of the community to prioritize unity and further reaffirm their commitment to using their resources and influence to further develop the community. Oba Ajayi emphasized that rapid development can only be achieved when the people rise to complement efforts by the government to make life much better for its citizens. Some of the dignitaries at the event included the Nobel Laureate, Prof Wole Soyinka, an indigine of the community, Chief Mrs Bola Obasanjo, wife of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Hon Oladipupo Adebutu, the 2027 PDP governorship candidate for the state, the Akarigbo and paramount ruler of Remo land, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, the Chief Executive Officer of Adron Homes, Adetola Emmanuel King, the Onirolu of Irolu Remo, Oba Sikiru Adeyiga among others. items.title: Next generation of Falcons, by Patrick Omorodion
items.description: The 2026 FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup may have come and gone but the memories of it would linger for a very long time. The competition which is the lowest among the age grade competitions put together by football’s world governing body, FIFA as nursery for the senior teams participating in the Women’s World Cup started in 2008. Since then, it has held 10 times, only missing out in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic that year. After it returned in 2022, FIFA decided that from the 2024 edition that it would no longer be held biennially but annually. Nigeria’s Flamingos have participated in nine of the 10 times the competition has held, missing out only in the 2018 edition hosted by Uruguay. Only two countries, New Zealand and Japan have participated in all the past 10 editions. Nigeria, Canada, North Korea and Mexico follow with nine appearances each. Before this year, the Flamingos’ best record in the competition was a bronze medal finishing at the 2022 edition in India when they lost in the semi finals to Colombia, 5-6 on penalties after the match ended 0-0. To win the bronze that year, the Flamingos, then tutored by Bankole Olowookere, defeated Germany 3-2 in a penalty shootout after a 3-3 draw in regulation time. When Coach Akeem Busari was appointed in April this year to replace Olowookere, not many knew him even as the head coach of Ibadan-based Pacesetter Queens football club. He silently assembled his team of 21 players from the women’s teams around the country. The team included Kemi Adegbuyi, Awawu Bashiru, Harmony Chidi who is the team’s captain, Oluebube Umejiaku and the first choice goalkeeper, Jane Ijirigho. The Kwara-born coach was in the saddle for only seven months and five days but yet he was able to build his team into a formidable one. He may have had it in mind to at least equal the bronze medal effort of his predecessor. It must have been a shock to the team when they lost their first group game to Poland 2-1. For young players, that could have dampened their morale for the remaining two group games against Puerto Rico and defending champions, North Korea. But they put aside that loss and went on to beat Puerto Rico 2-0. Their next match was against a North Korean side who were not only gunning for their fifth title but aiming for a record of being the first to win it three times in a row. Their demolition of North Korea 3-1 was a signal that Busari knew what he was doing and his girls were executing his match plans accurately. Like Puerto Rico and North Korea, Mexico fell 1-2 in the round of 16, Venezuela proved tough but fell 0-1 in the quarter finals while Brazil, whose best in the competition’s history had been a fourth place finishing at the last edition in 2025, crumbled 1-3 at the Flamingos’ feet in the semi finals. Then came the final against another Asian giant, Japan, and Coach Busari had a lot running through his mind, but the trophy was the greatest dream no doubt. Already he had made history by becoming the first Nigerian and African coach to take a team to the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. He must have told himself and probably drummed it into his players’ ears that the icing on the cake would be winning the title at the end. Like telling them, we are seeing the ‘Promised Land’ but we have to accomplish the journey by entering into it and taking possession. And they may have told themselves, “if we could subdue the defending champions, we could also take out Japan even though they have a better record than us as one time winners”. They had also finished in the runner-up position twice earlier in 2010 and 2016. Apart from the strength of the players which they exhibited from the group stage up to the semi finals, Coach Busari felt that the final stage would be more on psychology and focus and thus passed the message to his girls who had history beckoning at them. “It is just for us to concentrate, let’s put the icing on the cake. Let’s be focused and let’s finish the job because the job is not yet done,” he urged the girls. This pep talk fired the players’ resolve to press the throttle harder and the result was that the team played with cohesion and two of them, Awawu Bashiru who plays for Confluence Queens of Lokoja and Oluebube Umejiaku of Heartland Queens of Owerri, rose to the occasion and shot the Flamingos into the history books. Today the Flamingos have written their names in the sands of time like their male counterparts, the Golden Eaglets, led by Nduka Ugbade, did in 1985 in China. They have all the attributes of becoming world-class players in the nearest future given their exploits at Morocco 2026. Therefore, they must be encouraged and supported to transit into the next category, which is the U-20 team, the Falconets. And then the ultimate for them is the senior team, the Super Falcons who are fast losing their grip as Africa’s decorated side. When the celebration of the World Cup victory ends, the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, should decide whether to promote them to the Falconets with Coach Busari to allow for continuity or appoint another equally experienced handler who is expected to add new discoveries to plug the weak areas noticed in their World Cup campaign. We must get the transition right so that it doesn’t follow the same trajectory as the men where Nigeria leads the world with five U-17 titles but hasn’t been able to go beyond her two silver (1989 and 2005) and a bronze (1985) medal efforts. items.title: Sex agreement should be part of marriage contract
items.description: By Olaosebikan Olaniyi Marriage is a contract, and every serious contract should be explicit about its most important terms. Sex is central to marriage. It affects emotional bonding, physical health, fidelity, and long-term satisfaction. Leaving it to assumptions and unspoken expectations is why so many marriages fail. A sex agreement as part of the marriage contract makes sense for three clear reasons. 1. It Creates Clarity and Honesty Most couples never have an honest conversation about their sexual needs, boundaries, frequency, and values before marriage. They assume love will handle it. A formal agreement forces that conversation. It allows both partners to state what they want, what they do not want, and what is non-negotiable. Clarity before marriage prevents resentment after marriage. 2. It Protects Consent and Mutual Respect Marriage does not equal automatic consent. A sex agreement affirms that both partners have ongoing rights over their own bodies. It can define consent, right to say no without punishment, agreement on fidelity, protection, and respect for periods of illness, pregnancy, stress, or trauma. This protects both husband and wife and builds a culture of respect, not entitlement. 3. It Prevents Future Conflict Many divorces and infidelity cases stem from sexual incompatibility and unmet expectations. One partner wants sex daily, the other weekly. One sees pornography or open marriage as acceptable, the other does not. One wants children immediately, the other wants to delay. If these issues were agreed upon in writing as part of the marriage contract, couples would either resolve them early or realize they are not compatible before making a lifelong commitment. Including a sex agreement does not make marriage less romantic. It makes it more mature. We sign agreements for money, property, and children. Why should we ignore the very act that creates children and sustains intimacy? Marriage should include a clear, mutual, and voluntary agreement about sex. It is practical, it is respectful, and it is necessary for a healthy modern marriage. Lack Of Sex Is The Biggest Damage In Marriage Many things can damage a marriage like money problems, bad communication and family interference. But none damages a marriage faster and deeper than lack of sex, it is more easy for a marriage to crash when she’s always tired of handling room affairs or when he’s busy pursuing dreams forgetting the importance of marital satisfaction. Ma’am, you’re not a nanny, you’re a wife, no domestic assignment in the house should be paramount than attending to your husband’s sexual life, SEX is the main reason why you’re married, sex is why you said I do and should be prioritized. Sex is not just physical pleasure. Sex is the bond that separates marriage from every other relationship. You can talk to a friend, share money with a brother, and laugh with a colleague. But sex is what makes a husband and wife husband and wife. When sex stops, the marriage starts to die, even if the couple still lives in the same house. Lack of sex creates distance. The couple stops touching, stops feeling close, and stops feeling wanted. The husband starts to feel rejected. The wife starts to feel unloved. Small quarrels become big fights because the love that should calm them is no longer being expressed through intimacy. Lack of sex also opens the door to temptation and infidelity. When a man or woman is starved of sex at home, the body and the mind will begin to look outside. It is not an excuse for cheating, but it is the reality of human nature. A marriage that is sexually dead is a marriage that is vulnerable to destruction. Lack of sex destroys confidence and happiness. A person who is constantly denied begins to ask questions: Am I not attractive again? Does my partner still love me? Has my partner found someone else? Those thoughts breed suspicion, anger, and depression. Sex heals what words cannot heal. After a quarrel, a good intimate moment can bring peace back. Sex removes stress, builds trust, and reminds both partners that they belong to each other. Without it, marriage becomes just a business partnership, two strangers sharing rent and children. That is why lack of sex is the biggest damage in marriage. A couple can survive poverty if they still desire each other. A couple can survive distance if they still long for each other. But a couple cannot survive a marriage where sex is dead. For marriage to survive, husband and wife must protect their sex life. They must prioritize it, discuss it, and keep it alive. OLANIYI, is a Relationship Coach The post Sex agreement should be part of marriage contract appeared first on Vanguard News .
