items.title: Broken record: Quaid’s visit, an RSS cell, and Dawn under attack
items.description: As refugees continued to pour into Pakistan, often surviving unspeakable violence en route, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, in a true display of leadership, met with the frazzled masses, urging them to keep hope alive. This, along with the busting of an RSS cell in Karachi, and a violent mob attack on Dawn ’s Delhi press, marked some of the prominent stories from Sept 15 to 21, 1947. Soothing words Many among the millions that had crossed over into Pakistan at the time of Independence had literally been through hell. They had witnessed murder, arson and communal frenzy on their way to what was supposed to be the promised land. In such delicate times, leaders are supposed to put aside protocol and mingle with the masses in order to empathise with them. The Quaid did just that, as a news report from the Sept 18 issue shows. Titled ‘Quaid-i-Azam and sister visit camps of refugees’, it details his visits to three refugee camps and a transit centre. “It was a nerve-wrecking hour that the Quaid-i-Azam and his sister [Ms Fatima Jinnah] spent with the unfortunate victims of Sikh and Hindu communal frenzy in Indian states and the East Punjab. Every refugee to whom they talked had harrowing tales of barbarities and wholesale liquidation of Muslim population to narrate.” Yet despite the horrors they had witnessed, the spirits of the men and women who came to Pakistan remained high, as they “raised full-throated shouts of Pakistan Zindabad and Quaid-i-Azam Zindabad to cheer themselves”. It was also a fact that many who had left behind land and wealth in their ancestral towns and villages were reduced to penury after crossing the frontier. “A jagirdar of Alwar State [now in Rajasthan], who once paid a land revenue of Rs12,000 but now was in tatters, related the gruesome murders of the Muslims of the state and how lakhs and lakhs of Mewati Muslims had either to flee for their lives or were butchered. …” Mr Jinnah was clearly overwhelmed by these accounts of sorrow and savagery, but, in his capacity as governor-general of the dominion, told his people not to lose hope. “The Quaid-i-Azam was visibly moved by their tales of misfortune and asked them to bear the troubles well. The Pakistan State, he said, would do all it possibly could to help them.” Today’s rulers could do much to learn from the empathy and leadership qualities the founder and maker of this nation displayed. The Balochistan question Today, Balochistan is wracked by separatist violence and under-development. The sad truth is that over the past many decades, the province has witnessed many insurgencies, with the rulers unable to progressively resolve its issues, and bring permanent peace to Balochistan. At the time of Independence, Baluchistan, as it was then known, was not one singular entity. In fact, it was divided into so-called British Baluchistan, and four princely states. The latter joined Pakistan in 1948. But early on, there were demands for representative rule, and affiliation with Pakistan. Qazi Mohammad Isa, president of the Baluchistan Provincial Muslim League, was in Karachi to apprise the Quaid and Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan of the demand that “Baluchistan should be made a full-fledged province with a Government responsible to its people.” According to Qazi sahib, the people of the province were eager to join Pakistan. “When his attention was drawn to the question whether Quetta will have to be made over to Kalat State [which had not yet joined Pakistan], he said that the question did not arise at all. The Baluchis wanted to remain in Pakistan, and nothing could be done against the wishes of the people.” The Sangh in Sind The Sangh Parivar — as the stable of far-right Hindu organisations in India are known — has made life for Muslims, Christians and other minority communities in that country very difficult. While the ruling BJP is the political arm of the Sangh, its ideological fountainhead is the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). Once upon a time, the Sangh was active in what is now Pakistan, and in fact, as the Sept 17 edition shows, an RSS cell in Karachi was busted for apparent involvement in terrorist activities. ‘Sevak Sangh plot for revolution in Pakistan’, the headline read, with the subheadings noting that “thirty terrorist leaders arrested: large quantity of explosives confiscated”. The story went on to say that during house-to-house searches, “sufficient documentary and material proof is believed to have fallen into the hands of the authorities to prove the existence of a widespread underground organisation of the Sangh for disruptive work.” Though the authorities were on the trail of the Sangh extremists for some time, “the chance explosion of a bomb in the house of Rai Bahadur Tota Ram in the Shikarpuri Colony, Karachi [which is located not too far from where the Quaid’s mausoleum now stands] on Sept 10, unexpectedly unravelled the machinations of the Sangh organisation.” Though the RSS leaders and cadres eventually left for India, they were soon replaced by extremists ‘of our own’. Dawn under siege It has always been an uphill struggle for the media to speak the truth in Pakistan. But these curbs, attacks and violent episodes are not new; in fact they go back to the time of Partition. As mentioned in the Sept 16 issue, the Dawn Delhi Press came under attack on Sept 14. As Dawn was considered the voice of the Muslim League, and therefore the voice of the subcontinent’s Muslims, it was an easy target for extremists who opposed Pakistan and the Quaid’s grand old party. The news report, quoting the BBC , said that the attack was a “two-hour gun battle of the Dawn press and the military.” The staff at Dawn Delhi sent the following communication to their colleagues in Dawn Karachi: “We have been in the midst of it since Sunday [Sept 10]. Day and night, death and destruction have been peeping round the corner and we have been at the citadel. … Hell was let loose and we were cut off from the world.” From those harrowing days to the present, the struggle to speak the truth continues. With the advantage of hindsight, one has the opportunity to study the historical cycles in a nation’s life. Thanks to this newspaper’s unique, extensive archive of back issues, one can examine the major political, economic and social trends that have shaped Pakistan and the world over the last seven decades and counting. Cliched as it may sound, history repeats itself, and we — as a state and as a polity — largely refuse to learn from it. Through this platform, we will look back at the ‘big’ stories that made it to the front pages of Dawn, as well as significant developments tucked away in the inside pages, from the birth of Pakistan onwards, and try to put them in perspective. We will study the critical issues of the week, starting from Aug 14, 1947 and examine the major themes and issues that made it to the paper.

items.title: COP31: Two-thirds of Africa’s US$2.2bn clean cooking pledges yet to be delivered
items.description: Two years after leaders pledged US$2.2 billion to expand clean cooking in Africa, only about US$740 million has been paid out, leaving roughly two-thirds of the money, about US$1.46 billion, still to be delivered. The figures were presented at a Leaders’ Roundtable on Clean Cooking in Africa at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on 12 November. The meeting was co-hosted by the COP31 Presidency of Türkiye, the United Republic of Tanzania, the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Clean Cooking Alliance. The pledges were made at the first Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa, held in Paris in 2024 and co-chaired by Tanzania’s President Samia Suluhu Hassan. The IEA has been tracking the commitments since, and its Executive Director, Fatih Birol, told the roundtable that about a third of the money had been disbursed (about 34 cents of every dollar pledged). “Where did this money go? It went to 28 African countries supporting concrete projects,” Birol said. President Samia said she was “encouraged that our collective efforts are beginning to deliver tangible results.” According to her, “by July 2026 approximately US dollar 740 million of the commitment made in Paris has been deployed across 22 African countries.” She said a further US$900 million in commitments had been mobilised since the Paris summit, bringing the total to about US$3.1 billion. “Our success must be measured not only by the resources mobilized but also by the number of families gaining access to affordable, reliable and sustainable clean cooking solutions,” she told the leaders. Nearly one billion Africans (about six in every ten people on the continent) still lack access to clean cooking, contributing to about 850,000 premature deaths every year (more than 2,300 a day), President Samia said. To Birol, it is “one of the greatest injustices in this world.” Traditional cooking, he said, generates 1.2 gigatonnes of greenhouse gases a year. “If you want to know what is 1.2 gigaton, it is equal to the emissions from international aviation and shipping put together.” “Why I say it’s a big injustice … because it is easily solve problem if we have the finance for that,” he added. Kenya’s special envoy, Ambassador Ali Mohamed, who spoke on behalf of President William Ruto, said Africa’s clean cooking challenge “requires at least $2 billion every year.” “Our success of course will be measured not just by commitment. It will be measured by the financing that is deployed,” he said. The President of the OPEC Fund for International Development, Abdulhamid Alkhalifa, cited a different figure: “The IEA estimates that Africa needs $4 billion a year for clean cooking issue.” That amount, he said, is “less than … what the world invest in energy in a single day.” “Let us make the smoke-filled kitchen a chapter of Africa’s past, not future,” he urged. For Norway’s special envoy, Hans Olav Ibrekk, the message was clear: “Clean cooking is climate action. We need to move from commitments to implementation at scale.” Lesotho’s Deputy Prime Minister, Justice Nthomeng Majara, warned that “isolated projects and pilot interventions will not be sufficient to achieve universal access.” “Uganda recognizes that access to clean cooking is not merely an energy issue,” said Uganda President Yoweri Museveni’s representative. She said the country’s strategy targets universal access to clean cooking “by 2040 with an intermediate target of 50% access by 2030,” and that President Museveni has issued Executive Order No. 3 banning charcoal. The next test comes at the second Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa, to be held in Nairobi, Kenya, on 27–28 January 2027, which Birol will co-chair with President Ruto. “We are going to fix this problem and solve this biggest injustice of the humanity,” Birol told the meeting. END.

items.title: Les navires européens opérant dans la zone mauritanienne de pêche priés de rentrer ce soir au port de Nouadhibou après la fin de l’accord de pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’UE
items.description: La Garde côtière mauritanienne a publié une circulaire ordonnant la suspension des activités des navires de pêche de l'Union européenne dans la zone de pêche mauritanienne, à l'expiration du protocole d'application de l'accord de partenariat dans le domaine de la pêche entre la Mauritanie et l'Union européenne. Dans une circulaire publiée ce samedi 14 novembre, la Garde côtière a déclaré : que le protocole expire à 00 h 00, et a exigé que tous les navires de pêche européens opérant dans les eaux mauritaniennes cessent leurs activités et se dirigent vers le port de Nouadhibou avant cette date, afin d’accomplir les formalités administratives et maritimes nécessaires à leur sortie de la zone économique exclusive de la Mauritanie. La Garde côtière a averti que tout manquement à ces instructions serait sanctionné conformément à la législation en vigueur. L’accord de pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’Union européenne remonte à 1987, tandis que le protocole d’application actuel arrive à échéance sans que les deux parties ne soient parvenues à un accord sur un nouveau protocole, malgré les cycles de négociations qui se sont tenus au cours des derniers mois.

items.title: COP 31: Tanzania, Lesotho, Uganda share clean cooking gains as US$1.46bn in pledges is yet to arrive
items.description: Tanzania, Lesotho and Uganda have shared how they are expanding clean cooking at home, as leaders at COP31 warned that most of the money promised to help Africa make the switch is yet to arrive. The countries presented their progress at a Leaders’ Roundtable on Clean Cooking in Africa in Antalya, Türkiye, on 12 November, co-hosted by the COP31 Presidency of Türkiye, Tanzania, the International Energy Agency (IEA) and the Clean Cooking Alliance. Tanzania: from 16 to 35 per cent “I’m pleased to report that clean cooking access in Tanzania has increased from 16% in 2022,” President Samia Suluhu Hassan told the roundtable. She said access reached 28.6 per cent in March 2024 and is expected to hit 35 per cent by the end of 2026 (more than double in four years). She credited rural electrification, lower electricity tariffs for cooking, subsidies for LPG equipment and tax incentives. “As of March 2026, the government has facilitated distribution of more than 346,000 subsidized LPG cylinders alongside over 49,000 induction stoves and 7,000 electric cookers,” she said. Through the Cook Fund programme, “more than 413,000 household benefiting nearly 2 million people have gained access to clean cooking solutions,” she said, adding that the programme has reached 45 public institutions, including schools with more than 62,000 students, and cut an estimated 3.8 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. “We are also extending clean cooking solutions beyond households to schools, hospitals, and other public institutions like prisons,” President Samia said. Lesotho: cooking and heating For Lesotho, the challenge goes beyond the kitchen. “Our household energy requirements extend beyond cooking to include space heating,” said Deputy Prime Minister Justice Nthomeng Majara. She said Lesotho piloted electric pressure cookers in five schools in 2022 with the World Food Programme and the Modern Energy Cooking Services programme, and that improved cookstoves are now being made locally. A renewable energy initiative, she said, “envisages the development of 9,194 improved cook stoves by the year 2028 with 60% earmarked for female headed households.” “This is an important demonstration of how targeted financing can address both energy poverty and gender inequalities,” she said. Uganda: 50 per cent by 2030 “Uganda recognizes that access to clean cooking is not merely an energy issue,” said Uganda President Yoweri Museveni’s representative. Uganda’s strategy aims for universal access to clean cooking “by 2040 with an intermediate target of 50% access by 2030,” she said. She said Uganda has introduced a dedicated electric cooking tariff, is piloting electric cooking in schools, and that President Museveni has issued Executive Order No. 3 banning charcoal. The availability and cost of alternatives, she said, remain a challenge. The money question Uganda and Lesotho called for more finance. “We particularly recognize the importance of concessional financing, private sector investment, and targeted support to make clean cooking solutions affordable and accessible,” the Ugandan representative said. Justice Majara said: “We need concessional financing grants, innovative financing instruments and results-based financing to make clean cooking technologies affordable, particularly for low-income and rural households.” At the first Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa in Paris in 2024, leaders pledged US$2.2 billion. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol told the roundtable that about a third of it, some US$740 million, has been disbursed, leaving about US$1.46 billion (two-thirds) still to come. “Where did this money go? It went to 28 African countries supporting concrete projects. To give you a few example, LPG, infrastructure and electric cooking in Kenya, new stove factories in Nigeria …,” Birol said. President Samia said “approximately US dollar 740 million of the commitment made in Paris has been deployed across 22 African countries,” and that a further US$900 million had since been mobilised, bringing total commitments to about US$3.1 billion. Kenya’s special envoy, Ambassador Ali Mohamed, speaking for President William Ruto, said Africa’s clean cooking challenge “requires at least $2 billion every year.” The President of the OPEC Fund for International Development, Abdulhamid Alkhalifa, said: “The IEA estimates that Africa needs $4 billion a year for clean cooking issue.” Alkhalifa said that is “less than … what the world invest in energy in a single day.” He said the OPEC Fund supports clean cooking in Madagascar, Somalia, Sierra Leone and Tanzania, with more than 10 more African countries in its pipeline. The European Commission said more than 400 million had been mobilised under the Team Europe approach to accelerate access to clean cooking in Africa. “Why I say it’s a big injustice … because it is a easily solve problem if we have the finance for that,” Birol said. Leaders will meet again at the second Summit on Clean Cooking in Africa in Nairobi, Kenya, on 27–28 January 2027, co-chaired by Birol and President Ruto. “Clean cooking is not simply an energy issue but an investment in human development, women’s empowerment, economic opportunity, and climate resilience,” President Samia said. END.

items.title: Troisième édition de la semaine du Maroc à Nouakchott du 16 au 22 novembre
items.description: Nouakchott va accueillir du 16 au 22 novembre prochain la troisième édition de la « Semaine du Maroc », à laquelle participent des institutions gouvernementales et des organismes économiques des deux pays, dans le but de faire connaître les opportunités d'échanges commerciaux et d'investissement entre la Mauritanie et le Maroc. Selon un communiqué de presse publié par les organisateurs de l’événement, celui-ci est organisé en collaboration avec l’ambassade du Maroc et l’association « Forum du Sud », en partenariat avec le ministère mauritanien du Commerce et du Tourisme et le ministère marocain de l’Industrie, de l’Investissement et de l’Économie numérique, ainsi qu’avec un certain nombre d’organismes et d’institutions économiques des deux pays. Le communiqué ajoute que le programme de la manifestation comprend des rencontres bilatérales entre hommes d’affaires et entreprises, mais aussi entre entreprises et organismes gouvernementaux, sans oublier des tables rondes consacrées aux perspectives de coopération économique entre les deux pays et aux grands projets qui renforcent leur partenariat. Cette semaine a pour objectif d’explorer les opportunités d’échanges commerciaux et d’investissement dans les secteurs de l’industrie, de la construction, des travaux publics, de l’énergie, de l’agroalimentaire, de l’agriculture, du secteur bancaire et des télécommunications. Le programme comprend également des présentations consacrées à la culture marocaine, à l’artisanat, à la gastronomie et aux produits locaux, ainsi que des soirées artistiques, musicales et poétiques tout au long de l’événement.

items.title: Enseignement supérieur en Afrique : l'UM6P, un modèle d'excellence à suivre ?
items.description: L'Afrique peut-elle former ses propres élites sans les envoyer étudier à l'étranger ? Au Maroc, l'Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) s'impose parmi les établissements africains les mieux classés à l'international. Recherche, intelligence artificielle, robotique, agriculture : l'université mise sur des formations de pointe pour répondre aux défis du continent. Mais cette excellence est-elle accessible à tous ? Et ce modèle peut-il être reproduit ailleurs en Afrique ? Sa Benjamin Traoré, professeur de droit public et directeur du programme Droit et Gouvernance à l'UM6P, est l'invité de Fatimata Wane dans le Journal de l'Afrique sur France 24.

items.title: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai elected NDC Greater Accra Deputy Youth Organiser
items.description: Daniel Niibi Afotey Odai has been elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Greater Accra Region after narrowly defeating three other contenders in the party’s regional executive elections. Niibi secured 45 votes in the election held on Saturday, November 14, 2026, edging his closest challenger, Atsu Eric Afeme, who polled 44 votes. Jones Klutse obtained 32 votes, while Rashid Isah secured eight. The result gives Niibi a new role in the party’s regional youth leadership as the NDC continues its internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections. Niibi’s political career began at the branch level. He served for eight years as Deputy Youth Organiser for the Krowor Constituency, where he was involved in youth mobilisation and organising party structures. He holds a degree in Political Science from the University of Ghana and is a Chartered Manager. He is also the District Director of the Youth Employment Agency (YEA) in Krowor, where his work involves connecting young people to employment, skills development and other opportunities. Outside politics and public service, Niibi manages Nungua Royals FC and works as a media consultant with the Multimedia Group. Niibi campaigned under the message, “Youth in Politics: From Spectators to Decision Makers”. His proposed agenda included establishing a functional Greater Accra Youth Secretariat, creating a database of young party members across the region’s 34 constituencies and setting up a 24-hour youth hotline. He also proposed appointing a youth desk officer in every constituency and introducing a welfare scheme for young party members. The NDC’s regional executive elections form part of the party’s internal reorganisation, with the outcome expected to shape its leadership structures and mobilisation efforts across the country. As Deputy Regional Youth Organiser, Niibi will work with the regional leadership on youth mobilisation and strengthening the party’s structures in Greater Accra.

items.title: L’armée américaine teste au Maroc des avions autonomes pour évacuer les blessés
items.description: Les États-Unis ont choisi le Maroc pour expérimenter une nouvelle technologie d’évacuation médicale militaire reposant sur un avion capable de transporter des blessés de manière autonome, sans pilote à bord ni recours à une station de contrôle au sol. Cette expérimentation s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme « Autonomous Casualty Evacuation », piloté par le commandement américain pour l’Afrique (AFRICOM). Dans ce cadre, un contrat de 500.000 dollars a été attribué à la société américaine Merlin, spécialisée dans les technologies d’autonomie aérienne, afin de réaliser une démonstration de cette technologie au Maroc. L’essai, prévu durant l’exercice budgétaire américain 2027, qui a débuté le 1er octobre, reposera sur un Cessna 208B Grand Caravan équipé du système de pilotage autonome Merlin Pilot. Une évacuation médicale sans pilote Le scénario prévu doit reproduire les différentes étapes d’une évacuation médicale, depuis la réception de la mission et la préparation automatique de l’itinéraire jusqu’au transport d’un blessé vers un établissement médical. L’appareil devra ainsi rejoindre une zone isolée, dépourvue d’infrastructures adaptées, pour récupérer un blessé simulé avant de regagner une destination médicale. Une civière sera chargée à bord afin de reproduire les conditions d’une véritable mission d’évacuation. L’objectif est notamment d’évaluer la capacité de l’avion à accomplir l’ensemble de la mission sans intervention humaine directe dans le pilotage. Le système Merlin Pilot intègre directement à bord les fonctions de navigation et de gestion du vol. Il est ainsi conçu pour permettre à l’appareil de recevoir les instructions de mission, de calculer son itinéraire, de modifier sa trajectoire en cas d’obstacle ou de menace et de poursuivre son vol de manière autonome. Autre capacité qui doit être évaluée : la possibilité de poursuivre la mission en cas de perte de communication avec une station au sol. Une caractéristique particulièrement importante pour AFRICOM, alors que les drones conventionnels reposent généralement sur une liaison continue avec leurs opérateurs. Le Cessna Grand Caravan transformé en ambulance volante Le choix du Cessna 208B Grand Caravan tient notamment à ses caractéristiques. Cet appareil monomoteur à turbopropulseur dispose d’une large porte cargo et d’un plancher plat permettant de charger une civière directement depuis le sol, sans recourir à des équipements de levage spécifiques. Pour la démonstration, Merlin devrait également équiper l’avion d’un module dédié à l’évacuation médicale aérienne, avec notamment des équipements d’oxygène, des sources d’alimentation électrique et des supports destinés aux dispositifs de surveillance de l’état du patient. Selon Matt George, fondateur et directeur général de Merlin, l’évacuation des blessés impose de pouvoir acheminer rapidement les patients vers des structures chirurgicales. Une mission qui devient particulièrement complexe dans les zones reculées, où les distances sont importantes et les communications parfois difficiles. Le dirigeant estime que l’intégration de systèmes autonomes directement dans les appareils pourrait permettre de maintenir ces missions même lorsque la liaison avec les stations de contrôle terrestres est interrompue. Un enjeu logistique pour les opérations américaines en Afrique Cette expérimentation répond plus largement aux défis logistiques auxquels est confronté AFRICOM, dont la zone de responsabilité couvre 53 pays africains. Les longues distances, l’éloignement de certaines infrastructures médicales et les contraintes sécuritaires peuvent compliquer l’évacuation rapide des militaires blessés. L’autonomie aérienne est ainsi envisagée comme une piste permettant de réduire les délais d’intervention et de faciliter l’accès aux zones difficiles. Le test réalisé au Maroc doit permettre aux autorités américaines d’évaluer, dans des conditions opérationnelles, le potentiel de cette technologie pour les missions d’évacuation médicale dans des environnements où les infrastructures et les communications sont limitées. The post L’armée américaine teste au Maroc des avions autonomes pour évacuer les blessés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Incivilité vs Téranga (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Un extrait de vidéo postée sur la page facebook du journaliste gabonais Freddy Koula Moussavou, a généré, mercredi, un vif échange d’incivilités entre internautes sénégalais. Des injures et des propos discourtois sont venus polluer le contenu de ce post du journaliste qui s’adressait à l’ancien président Macky Sall sur la télévision togolaise New World, en ces termes : « En parlant de double nationalité, mon père est à Matam, donc je viendrai chercher mon passeport sénégalais… » En quoi le président Sall avait répondu : « Ha oui ? Je suis également originaire de la région de Matam… ». Bref, actuellement en séjour à Dakar où se déroulent les Joj 2026, Freddy Koula Moussavou, voulait juste faire un clin d’œil en postant : « Ça tombe bien, j’y suis… au pays de la Téranga ». Mais le flot d’incivilités échangées entre internautes sénégalais, a fini par étaler toute la grossièreté affichée par certains de nos compatriotes sur les réseaux sociaux, sur tous les sujets, même le plus banal. La belle « Téranga » dont nous nous gargarisons ne se reflète plus dans nos relations entre concitoyens. La partisannerie est venue bafouer toutes ces valeurs que nos ancêtres ont forgées jusque-là. Notre Boîte de Pandore est bien ouverte. omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Sam Jonah credits Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian ownership of mineral wealth
items.description: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has credited former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong with advancing Ghanaian participation and ownership in the country’s mining and timber industries. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government introduced policies in 1972 that gave the state controlling interests in major companies, including Ashanti Goldfields and the Consolidated African Selection Trust. He said the measures were intended to increase Ghanaian control over the country’s natural resources while retaining foreign partners, their capital and technical expertise. “For the first time since the Portuguese landed at Elmina, the majority of the wealth beneath Ghanaian soil belonged to Ghanaians,” he said. Sir Jonah said Acheampong’s government did not rely on force to take control of the mining operations but retained foreign partners under management agreements. He said the government required the companies to locate their head offices in Accra, give the state a controlling role and train Ghanaians for senior management positions. “But he insisted on three things: that the head office be in Accra, so that the decisions that mattered were taken by people who had to look Ghanaians in the eye; that the state hold the controlling voice; and that a Ghanaian be trained and placed in the deputy managing director’s chair, with the clear expectation that the top chair would follow,” he said. Sir Sam Jonah said the policy helped create opportunities for Ghanaian professionals in the mining industry. The University of Cape Coast Chancellor said he was among those who benefited from the policy. “In due course, I was that Ghanaian. So were many others, in many companies. A whole generation of Ghanaian engineers, geologists and accountants came up through the door that decree opened,” he said. Sir Jonah had earlier disclosed that he joined Ashanti Goldfields in 1969 as an underground miner at Obuasi, before the government took control of the company in 1972. He later rose to become its chief executive. His remarks formed part of a broader assessment of Acheampong’s leadership and the former military government’s approach to Ghanaian participation in strategic industries.

items.title: Coyah-Kindia : les trafics sur la RN1 paralysés après le renversement d’un camion-remorque à Labota
items.description: La circulation est fortement perturbée sur la Route nationale numéro 1 (RN1), au niveau de Labota, au PK 40, dans la sous-préfecture de Mambia, préfecture de Kindia, à la suite du renversement d’un camion-remorque en pleine chaussée. Survenu aux environs de 17 heures, l’accident a provoqué un blocage presque total du trafic sur cet axe stratégique reliant Conakry à l’intérieur du pays. Des dizaines, voire des centaines de véhicules sont immobilisés de part et d’autre du lieu de l’accident, occasionnant un embouteillage particulièrement impressionnant. Après plusieurs heures d’attente, la situation reste toujours difficile pour les usagers. Depuis près de cinq heures, automobilistes, transporteurs et voyageurs sont contraints de patienter, dans l’espoir d’une reprise normale de la circulation. Sur les lieux, les éléments de la gendarmerie routière sont mobilisés pour tenter de fluidifier le trafic et trouver une issue à cette situation qui pénalise fortement les usagers de la route. Pour l’heure, les circonstances exactes de l’accident et le bilan d’éventuels blessés ne sont pas encore connus. Ce nouvel incident remet en lumière la vulnérabilité de la RN1, un axe routier stratégique où le renversement d’un poids lourd suffit à provoquer une paralysie majeure de la circulation, avec des conséquences importantes pour les milliers d’usagers qui l’empruntent quotidiennement.

items.title: ArchXenus marks 15 years with more than 140 projects, launches GeneXus
items.description: Architecture firm ArchXenus has marked 15 years in practice with more than 140 projects, using its anniversary celebration to launch GeneXus, a book documenting 12 of its selected works, and to introduce initiatives aimed at strengthening its contribution to Ghana’s built environment. The two-day celebration, held on 10 and 11 November 2026 at Christ Temple East in Accra, a building ArchXenus designed and whose construction it managed, featured the launch of the GeneXus book, the Xenus Impact Foundation and the African Urban Futures Conclave. It also brought architects and other stakeholders together to examine the future of cities, climate-responsive buildings, housing and investment in the built environment. The firm is led by Nana Akua Oppong-Birmeh and Agnes Ofosu-Appiah, both Partners and Principal Architects at ArchXenus E and Co-Directors of the Xenus Impact Foundation. Both said the firm’s most significant achievement over the past 15 years was not simply the number of projects it had completed, but the people it had helped develop, and the model of partnership it offered, particularly to women building careers while managing family responsibilities. “Just by virtue of our existence, so many people have found their feet, especially women. They have found the confidence to pursue their passion, to proceed into family life, and not worry about so many things, because we are modelling this and creating an opportunity for us to grow,” Nana Akua said. “Being partners and running the firm together has taught us that there’s strength in numbers. We are both married women with children, so we have life happening as well as work that is ongoing. When one person is down or out, the other steps in. We complement each other, which allows us to work, see where the gaps are in the built industry, and provide solutions for them,” Agnes said. The GeneXus book brings together 12 selected ArchXenus projects. Nana Akua said the publication was intended to strengthen the documentation of Ghanaian architecture and give students and practitioners local examples from which to draw inspiration, noting that many still relied on foreign publications despite the availability of projects designed and led by Ghanaians. “This is an opportunity for people to gather inspiration right here, in our cities, in Ghana, designed and led by Ghanaians, with familiar names. In places where you can actually pick a cab, go and experience them, and get inspired,” she said. Agnes said the African Urban Futures Conclave was conceived to address the fragmented nature of conversations in the built environment, where architects, engineers and other professionals often discussed issues within their own disciplines although the challenges facing cities required collaboration across sectors. The full Conclave will take place in April 2027 and is intended to be held biennially, bringing stakeholders from Ghana and across West Africa together to exchange ideas, plan, make business connections and agree on practical actions. Ahead of it, ArchXenus has agreed a challenge with the Ghana Institute of Architects inviting architects to showcase solutions to the problems facing cities. The Conclave is one strand of the newly launched Xenus Impact Foundation, which the partners established to give ideas room to grow beyond the firm’s commercial work and to serve communities through impact projects and corporate social responsibility. The Foundation works in four ways: publishing, through AX Press, which includes GeneXus; building, through impact projects; convening, through gatherings such as the Conclave; and showing, through exhibitions, including Time Space and Essence in Venice in 2027. Nana Akua called for stronger coordination in the planning of Ghanaian cities, arguing that architects are commonly commissioned to work within defined plots even when the impact of a building extends beyond its boundaries. “For an architect, you are usually given a defined plot of land to work with. You can think beyond it, but you can only work on that plot. Most cities that have developed have a vision for what they want to be, and that makes it easier for everyone to plug into that vision and let us have the kind of city that we all dream of,” she said. Agnes raised concerns about the gap in housing provision for middle-income earners, saying Ghana’s housing deficit, commonly put at about 1.8 million units, persisted despite a visible construction boom that did not translate into options for people in that bracket. “When you see a construction boom, it’s not for middle income. There’s a lot of luxury, and there are a lot of affordable housing schemes. But somewhere in the middle, there’s a gap. And the kayayei: when they arrive in Accra or whichever big city they go to, what buildings and what systems have we put in place for them?” she said. The Foundation’s pilot impact project, CoSpace, responds to that gap, exploring how middle-income earners can afford dignified homes in established neighbourhoods closer to work and school rather than living far from both. These concerns were among the issues explored on the second day of the celebration, 11 November, under the theme “Conversations & Connections”, a foretaste of the full Conclave. The discussions connected the role of architecture to wider questions about the kind of cities people want to live in, including lessons from architectural practice in Ethiopia and the need to move beyond plans towards implementation. Climate-responsive construction also featured prominently, with discussions on why green buildings matter and how they could be delivered at scale. A virtual address and moderated discussion on “Designing for Dignity” considered the human needs that should inform design, while conversations on moving from vision to delivery examined what is required to turn urban plans into practical outcomes. The gathering also considered what makes urban projects investable, bringing questions of capital, business connections and collaboration into discussions about the future of cities.

items.title: CAN 2027, Algérie – Togo : les Fennecs s’imposent sans briller
items.description: Pour son quatrième match de l’ère Brahim Hemdani, l’équipe d’Algérie n’a pas brillé. Face au Togo ce vendredi soir à Tizi-Ouzou lors de la 3 e journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, elle s’est contentée de l’essentiel : une courte victoire par un but à zéro grâce à une tête imparable de Ramy Bensebaini à un quart d’heure de la fin du match. A la suite d’un corner renvoyée par la défense togolaise, Anis Hadj Moussa récupère le ballon pour le mettre sur la tête du défenseur central de Dortmund. Bien élancé, Bensebaini catapulte le ballon dans les bois du gardien adverse et ouvre le score pour des Fennecs, amorphes et mal inspirés. Algérie – Togo : les Verts mal inspirés Une victoire qui permet aux hommes de Brahim Hemdani de s’emparer, seuls, de la tête de leur groupe avec sept points, devant la Zambie (2 e , 4 pts), le Togo (3 e , 3 pts) et le Burundi (4 e , 2 pt). Au-delà du résultat positif, les camardes de Bensebaini n’ont pas fourni une prestation convaincante, face à un adversaire modeste. Amorphes et sans inspiration, ils ont eu du mal à se créer des occasions de buts, avec seulement 5 tirs cadrés et deux occasions manquées. C’est très peu de la part d’une équipe nationale qui joue sur son terrain, devant son club et qui aspire à aller au moins jusqu’aux demi-finales de la CAN 2027. Le sélectionneur national a encore du travail pour redresser la barre et corriger les erreurs. Ni Ibrahim Maza et encore moins Nabil Bentaleb et Amine Gouiri n’ont produit le jeu nécessaire pour déstabiliser la défense adverse. Le Togo a même failli égalise dans les dernières secondes de la partie par Kodjo Laba. L’article CAN 2027, Algérie – Togo : les Fennecs s’imposent sans briller est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Sam Jonah calls for renewed agricultural investment, recalls Operation Feed Yourself achievements
items.description: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has criticised successive governments for abandoning the agricultural gains of General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s Operation Feed Yourself campaign, arguing that Ghana allowed a successful food production initiative to collapse. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Sir Jonah said the programme, launched in 1972, was a nationwide mobilisation effort that brought traditional authorities and communities into the drive for food self-sufficiency. He said the campaign used radio broadcasts and information vans to encourage people across the country to participate in agricultural production. “Cutlasses, hoes, fertiliser and seed were sold at heavily subsidised prices. Feeder roads carried produce to market. Above all, the government invested in water, from Dawenya and Asutsuare to the great Tono dam in the north,” he said. Sir Jonah said the campaign produced significant results, particularly in rice production. “Rice imports fell to zero in 1975, and again in 1976. Zero. Farmers in the North exported rice and tomatoes to Upper Volta, and Tamale earned a nickname, The Rice City,” he said. He argued that the programme demonstrated Ghana’s capacity to achieve substantial improvements in domestic food production when agricultural policies were supported by sustained investment and nationwide participation. Sir Sam Jonah said the programme’s decline represented a missed opportunity for the country. “The tragedy of Operation Feed Yourself is not that it failed. It is that it worked, and we let it go,” he said. He contrasted the campaign’s reported achievements with Ghana’s current food import bill, which he put at about US$2 billion annually, with rice and chicken accounting for a significant share. Operation Feed Yourself was introduced under Acheampong’s military government in 1972 to promote domestic food production and reduce dependence on imports. Colonel Frank Bernasko played a leading role in the campaign, helping mobilise traditional authorities and communities. Sir Jonah’s remarks formed part of a broader argument for renewed investment in agriculture and a stronger national commitment to food security.

items.title: Sénégal : les budgets de 19 ministères rejetés en commission parlementaire
items.description: Le Sénégal s’enfonce davantage dans l’impasse budgétaire. Les projets de budget de 19 ministères ont été rejetés par la Commission des Finances et du Contrôle budgétaire de l’Assemblée nationale, alors que l’examen du projet de loi de finances pour 2027 se poursuit sur fond de tensions entre le gouvernement et un Parlement dominé par l’opposition. Parmi les départements concernés figurent notamment les ministères de l’Intégration africaine et des Affaires étrangères, de l’Intérieur et de la Sécurité publique ainsi que de la Justice. Les commissions parlementaires ont également rejeté les projets de budget de plusieurs secteurs clés, notamment l’Éducation nationale, la Santé, l’Enseignement supérieur ainsi que l’Industrie et le Commerce. Des réserves sur les prévisions financières Les parlementaires ont notamment mis en doute la sincérité des prévisions de recettes et de dépenses, la fiabilité de certaines données financières ainsi que la cohérence des crédits proposés pour différents départements. Les discussions ont également porté sur l’insuffisance des moyens affectés à certains programmes sectoriels et sur les écarts constatés entre les prévisions de la loi de finances initiale et celles de la loi de finances rectificative pour 2026. Cette série de votes défavorables intervient quelques jours après le rejet, le 7 novembre, des projets relatifs aux recettes et à la dette publique, ainsi que des budgets de plusieurs institutions de la République, dont la Présidence, la Primature et l’Assemblée nationale. Pas encore de rejet définitif du budget 2027 Ces votes en commission ne signifient toutefois pas que la loi de finances pour 2027 est définitivement rejetée. Ils interviennent dans le cadre de l’examen parlementaire des crédits et la procédure d’adoption du texte doit encore se poursuivre conformément aux règles en vigueur. Le Sénégal traverse néanmoins une crise politique et budgétaire majeure, marquée par un bras de fer entre le gouvernement et une Assemblée nationale dominée par le parti d’opposition Pastef. Depuis la fin du mois d’octobre, les députés de la majorité parlementaire opposée au gouvernement rejettent successivement plusieurs textes liés au budget, accentuant les incertitudes autour de l’adoption du projet de loi de finances 2027. Cette crise intervient alors que Dakar poursuit ses discussions avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) autour d’un nouveau programme d’appui financier et de réformes destinées à renforcer la soutenabilité des finances publiques. L’issue du bras de fer parlementaire apparaît ainsi déterminante pour le gouvernement, alors que le pays cherche à rétablir la confiance autour de ses comptes publics et à avancer dans ses discussions avec ses partenaires financiers internationaux. The post Sénégal : les budgets de 19 ministères rejetés en commission parlementaire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Benjamin Danso defeats NDC Greater Accra chair Ashie Moore by a margin of over 500 votes
items.description: Benjamin Danso has emerged as the new Greater Accra Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), defeating incumbent Emmanuel Nii Ashie Moore in the party’s regional executive election by a margin of over 500 votes. Mr Danso’s victory brings an end to Mr Ashie Moore’s tenure, which began in November 2022 when he defeated then-incumbent Joseph Ade Coker to take over the regional chairmanship. Mr Ashie Moore had served in the position for almost four years and was seeking another term. Ahead of Saturday’s, November 14, 2026, polls, he expressed confidence that delegates would retain him, citing his work and leadership of the party in the region. In an interview ahead of the election, he said he was confident delegates would reward his efforts. “I’m very confident the delegates today will reward hard work,” he said. However, the delegates voted for Mr Danso, giving him the responsibility of leading the party in the Greater Accra Region for the next four years. Mr Danso had, during his campaign, pledged to lead with service, integrity and commitment to the party’s grassroots. He also outlined plans to strengthen party structures across all 34 constituencies in the region and build a united front capable of securing victory for the NDC in the 2028 general elections. Benjamin Danso served as the NDC Constituency Chairman for Krowor in Greater Accra. In June 2023, he was elected chairman of the Greater Accra NDC Constituency Chairmen’s Association, a caucus that brings together constituency chairpersons across the region. That role gave him experience coordinating and engaging party leaders beyond his own constituency.

items.title: Owusu Nkrumah Ababio elected Ahafo NDC Regional Chairman
items.description: Owusu Nkrumah Ababio has been elected Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Ahafo Region following the party’s 2026 Regional Executives Elections. The keenly contested polls, held at Nana Bosomprah Park in Goaso, saw Mr Ababio secure 106 votes to defeat his closest contender, Joseph Baradoe, who polled 94 votes. The third candidate, Ahmed Ali Awinbila, obtained three votes. The results were certified and signed by the Ahafo Regional Director of the Electoral Commission (EC), Emmanuel Kyei, bringing the electoral process to a close. In the contest for Regional Vice Chairman, Abdul Mumin Sadick emerged victorious with 85 votes, defeating Prince Ahmed Mohammed, who secured 59 votes. Salamatu Braima polled 43 votes, while Joseph Asako Azumyarn obtained 12 votes. Awudu Razak won the Regional Secretary position with 114 votes, beating George Mawuli, who polled 89 votes. For Deputy Regional Secretary, Gbene Mohammed Sidiki secured 85 votes to emerge as winner ahead of Patricia Oteng Agyemang (65 votes), Richard Adampoah Kowoji (41 votes) and Haruna Alhassan (11 votes). Masawudu Sulemana was elected Regional Organiser after polling 109 votes against Iddrisu Loaman Dauda’s 94 votes. Shilla Yahaya won the Deputy Regional Organiser position with 77 votes, defeating Ibrahim Anyas Muniru, who obtained 66 votes, and Peter Bonsu, who polled 59 votes. In the financial portfolios, Smartwilliam Kwasi Aziblame won the Regional Treasurer position with 112 votes, beating Ibrahim Musah, who secured 88 votes. Abdulai Hamidu was elected Deputy Regional Treasurer with 129 votes, defeating Abdul-Kadri Yahaya, who polled 73 votes. Apraku Lartey emerged as Regional Communication Officer after securing 117 votes against Issaka Azumah’s 86 votes. Alfred Aboagye won the Deputy Regional Communication Officer position with 127 votes, beating Misiagbetor Etse JohnChris, who obtained 75 votes. Abdallah Ibn Chambas recorded the highest individual vote tally in the elections, securing 136 votes to win the Regional Zongo Caucus Coordinator position. His opponent, Abdulai Mamoudou Sana, polled 67 votes. In the youth wing elections, Abdul Razak Ahmed won the Regional Youth Organiser position with 18 votes against Ibrahim Issifu’s 11 votes. Dufie Jennifer was elected Deputy Regional Youth Organiser after polling 10 votes, narrowly beating Paul Mensah Quainoo, who obtained seven votes. Dauda Karim secured six votes, Kwame Qyabaah four, while Yussif Issah polled two votes. For the women’s wing, Gawusu Pooley Mamuna won the Regional Women Organiser position with 13 votes, defeating Hajia Safia Iddrisu, who polled 11 votes. Mary Louisa Owusu was elected Deputy Regional Women Organiser with nine votes, narrowly beating Lucy Amoah, who obtained eight votes. Bernice Agyei secured seven votes, while Augustina Akua Abrafi polled one vote. The newly elected regional executives are expected to focus on strengthening the party’s grassroots structures, consolidating internal cohesion and mobilising supporters ahead of the 2028 general elections and other political activities in the region.

items.title: ‘Yentua’ was negotiation, not recklessness – Sam Jonah on Acheampong’s debt decision
items.description: Business leader Sir Sam Jonah has praised former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong’s 1972 decision to repudiate some of Ghana’s external debt, describing it as an act of courage and a demonstration of negotiation skill. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Mr Jonah said Acheampong’s government announced on February 5, 1972, that Ghana would not honour about US$90 million in suppliers’ credits it considered tainted by corruption, fraud or inflated contracts. He said the decision became known through the Akan expression “Yentua”, meaning “we will not pay”. “The Daily Graphic put it in one Akan word, in a headline this country has never forgotten: Yentua. We will not pay,” he said. Sir Jonah argued that Acheampong’s decision reflected a willingness to withstand immediate economic pressure in pursuit of what he described as long-term national dignity. “He was prepared to absorb short-term pain for long-term dignity. That is not recklessness. That is negotiation,” he said. According to Mr Jonah, the debt repudiation compelled creditors to return to negotiations, eventually leading to a rescheduling agreement in Rome in 1974. Under the arrangement, he said, the debt was rescheduled at an interest rate of 2.5 per cent, with an extended grace period. Sir Jonah contrasted the 1972 decision with Ghana’s suspension of payments on much of its external debt in December 2022, which preceded the country’s debt restructuring programme. He said the two episodes reflected different circumstances, arguing that Acheampong’s decision was presented as a deliberate negotiating position, while the 2022 default was driven by the country’s inability to meet its debt obligations. “In December 2022, fifty years after Yentua, our government again announced that it would stop paying most of its external debt. But this was no choice made from strength, to the applause of the nation. It was a default forced upon us, and it reached into the savings of pensioners and ordinary depositors,” he said. “In 1972 the slogan was Yentua: we will not pay. In 2022 the honest slogan would have been Yentumi: we cannot,” he added. The lecture formed part of a broader call for renewed discussion about Ghana’s debt management, economic sovereignty and the lessons that can be drawn from the country’s past dealings with creditors.

items.title: Sam Jonah calls for honest reassessment of General I.K. Acheampong’s leadership
items.description: Business leader and University of Cape Coast Chancellor Sir Sam Jonah has called for a fresh and balanced examination of the leadership of former Head of State General Ignatius Kutu Acheampong, urging Ghanaians to confront the complexities of his time in office. Delivering the Second General I.K. Acheampong Memorial Lecture at the Marriott Hotel in Accra on Friday, November 13, 2026, Sir Jonah said the country needed to move beyond the silence and polarised narratives surrounding the former military leader. He said the lecture offered an opportunity to examine Acheampong’s record, including his policies, achievements and shortcomings. “Our forebears left us a saying for an evening such as this: Se wo were fi na wosankofa a yenkyi . It is not wrong to go back for what you have forgotten. That is what we shall do tonight. We shall break the silence,” he said. Sir Jonah disclosed that he had personally benefited from policies introduced under Acheampong’s government, particularly those that expanded opportunities for Ghanaians in the management of the Ashanti Goldfields Corporation. He said he joined the mining company in 1969 as an underground miner at Obuasi, three years before the government took control of the company in 1972. “I am a beneficiary of this man. In 1972 his government took control of the Ashanti Goldfields Corporation and opened its senior management to Ghanaians. I had joined Ashanti three years earlier as an underground miner at Obuasi. The chairs I would one day occupy were built on policies General Acheampong signed into law,” he said. He, however, clarified that he had never met the former Head of State personally. “I never knew him. I never sat across a table from him. But my life bears his fingerprints, and I would be a fraud to pretend otherwise,” he added. Sir Sam Jonah said his intention was neither to glorify Acheampong nor to condemn him without examining the full record of his leadership. “Ghana has already done both to this man, and neither has served us well. Tonight, I intend to examine the leadership of General Acheampong, the vision and the blindness, the triumph and the disappointment, the man and the system he led, and to let you judge it whole,” he said. General Acheampong came to power in January 1972 after leading a military coup that overthrew the government of Dr Kofi Abrefa Busia. His government introduced policies and initiatives including Operation Feed Yourself, which sought to boost domestic food production, and the Yentua policy, under which Ghana repudiated certain external debt obligations. It also advanced the Union Government proposal, which sought a political arrangement involving civilian and military participation. Acheampong was removed from power in July 1978 and later executed by the Armed Forces Revolutionary Council in June 1979.

items.title: Claude : quand créer une application devient un jeu d’enfant (Par Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE)
items.description: Il fut un temps où créer une application mobile ou une plateforme web relevait presque d'un parcours du combattant. Il fallait apprendre des langages de programmation, maîtriser des lignes de code, comprendre le fonctionnement des bases de données et, souvent, disposer de moyens financiers pour solliciter les services d'un développeur. Aujourd'hui, l'intelligence artificielle bouscule cette réalité. Avec « Claude », développé par Anthropic, créer une application peut désormais commencer par une simple conversation.Imaginez un entrepreneur qui souhaite lancer une plateforme de lecture en ligne, un journaliste qui rêve d'un outil pour organiser ses données ou un étudiant qui veut développer une application pour résoudre un problème rencontré dans son université. Hier, ces idées nécessitaient des compétences techniques parfois difficiles à acquérir. Aujourd'hui, il suffit de les expliquer à « Claude », de préciser les fonctionnalités attendues et de laisser l'intelligence artificielle proposer une première réalisation. Elle peut générer le code, concevoir une interface, organiser les différentes fonctionnalités et accompagner l'utilisateur dans les corrections. C'est l'une des évolutions les plus intéressantes de « Claude » : sa capacité à transformer des instructions formulées en langage naturel en véritables projets numériques. Avec ses fonctionnalités de programmation et de création interactive, notamment Artifacts, l'outil permet de concevoir des prototypes, des interfaces et de petites applications directement à partir d'un échange conversationnel. Avec « Claude Code », Anthropic va encore plus loin en proposant un assistant capable d'intervenir sur des projets informatiques, d'examiner des fichiers, de modifier des codes et d'aider à corriger des erreurs. Cette nouvelle manière de développer s'inscrit dans une tendance baptisée « vibe coding ». Le principe est simple : plutôt que de commencer par écrire soi-même des centaines de lignes de code, l'utilisateur décrit ce qu'il souhaite obtenir. L'Ia traduit cette intention en instructions techniques. Le créateur teste, observe le résultat, signale ce qui ne fonctionne pas et demande des améliorations. Le développement devient ainsi un dialogue permanent entre l'humain et la machine. La révolution est particulièrement intéressante pour les pays comme le Sénégal, où les talents ne manquent pas, mais où l'accès aux ressources techniques et financières peut constituer un obstacle à la concrétisation de certaines idées. Un jeune entrepreneur peut désormais expérimenter une plateforme de commerce, un étudiant concevoir un outil éducatif ou un journaliste imaginer une application de traitement de données sans nécessairement disposer, dès le départ, d'une équipe de développeurs. L'intelligence artificielle réduit ainsi la distance entre l'idée et le premier prototype. Mais cette facilité apparente ne doit pas faire oublier une réalité : créer une application et concevoir un logiciel professionnel sont deux choses différentes. Une interface séduisante ne garantit ni la sécurité des données, ni la fiabilité du système, ni sa capacité à supporter des milliers d'utilisateurs. Un code généré par l'Ia peut contenir des erreurs, des failles de sécurité ou des fonctionnalités mal conçues. Il faut donc savoir tester, vérifier et comprendre, au moins dans ses grandes lignes, ce que la machine produit. Le risque serait de confondre la capacité à obtenir un résultat avec la maîtrise du métier. Le développeur ne disparaît pas. Son rôle évolue. Il devient aussi celui qui supervise, contrôle, optimise et sécurise les solutions produites avec l'intelligence artificielle. Les connaissances en programmation restent précieuses pour identifier les erreurs et construire des applications robustes. Au fond, « Claude » ne transforme pas chaque utilisateur en ingénieur informatique du jour au lendemain. Il rend simplement possible ce qui semblait autrefois réservé à une catégorie de professionnels. La barrière technique s'abaisse, laissant davantage de place à la créativité, à l'expérimentation et à l'innovation. Pour le Sénégal, l'enjeu est désormais de ne pas être seulement consommateur de ces technologies, mais de s'en servir pour produire des solutions adaptées à ses réalités. Car si demain tout le monde peut demander à une Ia de créer une application, l'avantage appartiendra surtout à ceux qui sauront identifier les bons problèmes, à résoudre et transformer leurs idées en outils réellement utiles. cheikh.tidiane.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Accra | Le ministre des Affaires étrangères s’entretient avec les Tunisiens établis au Ghana
items.description: En marge de sa participation aux travaux de la vingt-septième session extraordinaire du Conseil Exécutif de l'Union Africaine, tenue dans la Capitale ghanéenne Accra, M. Mohamed Ali Nafti, Ministre des Affaires Étrangères, de la Migration et des Tunisiens à l'Étranger, a eu une rencontre, samedi 14 novembre 2026, avec des membres de la communauté tunisienne résidant au Ghana, et ce en présence de l'Ambassadeur de Tunisie accrédité auprès du Ghana, M. Mohsen Antit. À cette occasion, le Ministre a confirmé la haute sollicitude qu'accorde Son Excellence le Président de la République, Monsieur Kaïs Saïed, aux compatriotes tunisiens à l'étranger, ainsi que son souci de les entourer d'attention, d'assurer le suivi de leurs préoccupations et d'aplanir les difficultés qu'ils pourraient rencontrer. Il a précisé que le Ministère œuvre assidûment à améliorer davantage les services consulaires et à développer les mécanismes de communication avec eux. Cette rencontre a été l'occasion d'évoquer les relations historiques qui unissent la Tunisie au Ghana, leur engagement dans la bataille de libération et d'indépendance ainsi que leur attachement à l'édification de l'Afrique et de son unité. Il a souligné, par ailleurs, le rôle qui leur incombe pour contribuer à veiller sur l'image de la Tunisie auprès du Pays de résidence, les exhortant, chacun depuis sa position, à soutenir les efforts nationaux de développement et à consolider les relations de coopération existantes avec le Ghana dans les divers domaines. De leur côté, les membres de la communauté tunisienne au Ghana ont exprimé leur fierté quant à leur appartenance à la Patrie et leur considération pour cette initiative qui reflète la solidité du lien entre la Tunisie et ses compatriotes à l'étranger, confirmant leur disposition à continuer d'assumer leur rôle en tant que pont de communication et de rapprochement entre les deux Pays frères. MAE L’article Accra | Le ministre des Affaires étrangères s'entretient avec les Tunisiens établis au Ghana est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Nana Toku defeats Borlu to retain NDC Western Regional chairmanship
items.description: Nana Kojo Toku has retained his position as Western Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) after defeating two challengers in the party’s regional executive election. Mr Toku polled 225 votes to secure another term, beating Samuel Kwame Borlu, who obtained 209 votes, while George Arthur placed third with 114 votes. In other key positions, George Dadzie Junior was elected Regional Secretary with 324 votes, while Alhaji Iddrisu Mustapha secured 217 votes to become First Vice Chairman. Daniel K. B. Eshun, who polled 119 votes, was elected Second Vice Chairman. Suleman Yahaya Anafo won the Deputy Secretary position with 165 votes, while Richard Ernest Kirk-Mensah emerged as Communications Officer after polling 306 votes against Eric Kwaku Kyeremah’s 231. Daniel Nketsiah also secured the Deputy Communications Officer position with 238 votes. Charles Adu-Fordjour was elected Regional Organiser with 312 votes, defeating Haruna Moro Azika, who polled 191, while Clifford Ayirebi Acquah won the Deputy Organiser position with 256 votes against George Bamfo’s 234. Abdul Hakeem Mahama was elected Youth Organiser with 51 votes, while Jones Adom won the Deputy Youth Organiser position. Hafiz Alasco also emerged as the winner of the Zongo Caucus position with 311 votes, defeating Alhaji Abubakari Kamal, who secured 237 votes. Meanwhile, Daniel Darlington Atitso was elected Treasurer unopposed, with Marian Plange-Kwofie also going unopposed as Deputy Treasurer. Gladys Egyin was elected Women Organiser unopposed, while Hajia Sadika Yakubu and Charlotte Cobbinah secured the positions of Deputy Women Organiser and Second Deputy Women Organiser, respectively. The elections also saw other candidates contesting positions across the regional executive structure as the party elected officers to oversee its affairs in the Western Region.

items.title: Nana Kwasi retains Ashanti NDC chairmanship with 814 votes
items.description: Augustus Andrews Nana Kwasi has retained his position as Ashanti Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) after defeating his challenger, Isham Alhassan Yaw Bonsu, in the party’s regional executive election. Nana Kwasi secured 814 votes against the 622 obtained by former Ashanti Regional Organiser, Isham Alhassan Yaw Bonsu, out of the 1,436 votes cast. His victory extends his leadership of the party in the region after eight years in office, following a keenly contested election that attracted considerable interest among party faithful. Shortly after the results were announced, the incumbent chairman was overcome with emotion and broke down in tears as supporters and sympathisers gathered around him to celebrate his victory. The emotional scene drew the attention of delegates and party supporters, with the chairman visibly struggling to contain his tears as he received congratulations. Ahead of the election, Nana Kwasi had expressed confidence in securing another mandate, pointing to what he considered significant gains made by the party in the Ashanti Region during his tenure. He cited the NDC’s improved presidential election performance in the region, saying the party had increased its votes from about 300,000 when he assumed office to approximately 450,000 in the 2020 general elections and 800,000 in the 2024 polls. His re-election is expected to reinforce his influence within the party in a region widely regarded as a stronghold of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP). The outcome also comes at a crucial time as the NDC seeks to consolidate its support base, strengthen its grassroots structures and improve its electoral performance ahead of the 2028 general elections. Nana Kwasi is expected to work with the newly elected regional executives, constituency officers and other party stakeholders to address internal divisions and build a united front following the contest.

items.title: Lali X Lola, King Jerry energise vendors at Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair as they turn to the dance floor
items.description: The second day of the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 ended amid music, dancing and excitement as Ghanaian music acts Lali X Lola and King Jerry treated patrons to lively performances, transforming the business exhibition into a vibrant celebration of entrepreneurship and entertainment. What began as a platform for businesses to showcase their products, connect with customers and attract new markets gradually took on a carnival atmosphere, with music drawing exhibitors and shoppers away from their stalls to join the celebrations. The energy at Ghud Park, Accra Mall, was infectious, as patrons responded enthusiastically to the performances, singing along, dancing and capturing moments on their phones. Vendors, who had spent the day engaging customers and displaying their products, also joined the fun. Some carried their merchandise as they danced, creating colourful scenes that brought together business promotion and entertainment in an atmosphere of shared excitement. The performances by Lali X Lola and King Jerry provided a lively soundtrack to the fair’s activities, keeping the crowd entertained and adding a memorable dimension to the second day. The excitement was not confined to the performance area. Exhibitors and patrons interacted across the venue, with shoppers moving between stalls to explore the range of products and services on display while enjoying the music. The fair’s blend of business and entertainment offered exhibitors another opportunity to draw attention to their brands, engage potential customers and create memorable experiences around their products. A marketplace of Ghanaian enterprise The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026, organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank, has brought together more than 80 businesses and brands at Ghud Park, Accra Mall. The three-day event, running from November 13 to 15, provides a platform for small and medium-sized enterprises to showcase locally made products, promote their services, network and build relationships with consumers and potential business partners. The exhibition features a broad range of sectors, including food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, finance, household products and real estate. Participating businesses have been using the fair to introduce shoppers to their products, offer attractive deals and demonstrate the creativity and innovation driving Ghanaian entrepreneurship. The event has also featured appearances by Joy Prime’s KMJ and Hitz FM’s Mercury Quaye, who have engaged exhibitors and patrons, adding to the lively atmosphere. Final day beckons Although the second day has wrapped up with music and dancing, the fair is not over. Sunday, November 15, marks the final day of the exhibition, offering patrons another opportunity to visit the stalls, discover products, take advantage of shopping deals and support local businesses. With its combination of business opportunities, product displays, networking and live entertainment, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair continues to provide a meeting point for entrepreneurs and consumers. The scenes of vendors dancing with their products and patrons enthusiastically joining the celebrations captured the spirit of the second day: a marketplace where business, creativity and entertainment came together in an atmosphere of excitement.

items.title: Obeng Inkoom unseats Richard Asiedu to become NDC Central Regional Chair with an 8-vote difference
items.description: Private legal practitioner Obeng Inkoom has been elected Central Regional Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), ending Dr Richard Asiedu’s tenure after a closely contested regional executive election at Dunkwa-on-Offin. Mr Inkoom secured 372 votes to defeat the incumbent, who polled 364. A third contender, Ibrahim Mohammed, obtained 16 votes. The newly elected chairman has pledged to bring the party’s factions together and strengthen its structures, saying unity and adherence to the NDC’s founding values would guide his leadership. He said his policy agenda was centred on building a united party grounded in honesty, integrity, probity and accountability. “I issued a policy statement, and it is to the effect that I will build a united party and that united party will be based on the principles of the formation of the NDC, which we call the value proposition and that is honesty, integrity, probity and accountability,” he said. Mr Inkoom added that he intended to train party members to improve their ability to communicate the NDC’s message effectively. His victory follows a competitive race in which he edged Dr Asiedu by just eight votes, making the Central Regional chairmanship one of the closely fought contests in the party’s regional elections.

items.title: Air Algérie : avec Domestic Airlines, la flotte va bientôt atteindre 100 avions
items.description: La flotte globale d’Air Algérie y compris celle de sa filiale Domestic Airlines atteindra bientôt près de 100 avions après la réception des appareils neufs commandés par la compagnie aérienne nationale auprès d’Airbus, Boeing et ATR. « Le président de la République a donné son accord pour d’importants investissements de la part d’Air Algérie. Il a initié la création de Domestic Airlines. Cette compagnie accomplit un service qui permet de répondre à la demande de plusieurs de nos concitoyens notamment dans l’extrême sud du pays. Nous travaillons à augmenter le nombre de vols domestiques », a déclaré le ministre des Transports, Saïd Sayoud, jeudi à l’APN en réponse à une question orale d’un député d’El Oued. Saïd Sayoud : « Les avions d’Air Algérie ne s’arrêtent presque pas » Air Algérie a renforcé la flotte de Domestic Airlines avec l’acquisition de nouveaux 16 ATR 72-600. « Nous avons déjà reçu un appareil ATR 72-600. Deux autres avions du même type seront livrés avant la fin de l’année, et le reste sera réceptionné en 2027 », a ajouté le ministre, en soulignant l’ampleur de la demande sur les vols d’Air Algérie et de Domestic Airlines dont les avions « ne s’arrêtent presque pas ». « Ils sont exploités d’une façon continue, sans interruption », a-t-il dit. Saïd Sayoud a ensuite évoqué le programme de renouvellement de la flotte d’Air Algérie qui passera à près de 100 avions, une fois tous les appareils commandés livrés. « Avec la réception des 16 ATR, des avions Airbus A330-900Neo (10) et Boeing (18), nous allons arriver à une flotte totale de près de 100 avions. Nous étions à 54 appareils », a-t-il dit. Dans le détail, ; Air Algérie va réceptionner, ce mois de novembre, un 7 e Airbus A330-900Neo sur une commande de 10 appareils, a indiqué le ministre. items.title: 21-year-old Ghanaian Thomas Oduro stabbed to death in North London
items.description: A 21-year-old Ghanaian identified as Thomas Oduro has died after being stabbed in north London, prompting a murder investigation by the Metropolitan Police. The incident occurred on Friday, November 13, along Lordship Lane in Haringey, where emergency services were called shortly after 6 pm following reports that a man had been attacked. According to the BBC, paramedics attended the scene but were unable to save the victim, who was pronounced dead at the scene. The Metropolitan Police subsequently identified him as Thomas Oduro, from Tottenham, and confirmed that his next of kin had been informed. Detective Chief Inspector Phil Clarke, who is leading the investigation, expressed condolences to the bereaved family, saying they had suffered a devastating loss and were receiving support from specialist officers. He added that investigations were continuing at the scene, with an increased police presence expected in the area over the coming days. The detective also appealed to anyone who was around Lordship Recreation Ground at about 6 pm on Friday, or who might have information relevant to the incident, to assist investigators. The police have urged witnesses to contact them through 101 or provide information anonymously to Crimestoppers. Recent deaths of young Ghanaians abroad The London killing comes amid growing concern among Ghanaians following several recent deaths involving young nationals in North America. In the United States, 15-year-old Ghanaian Javits Frimpong was fatally shot on October 29 while walking to school in the Bronx, New York. A 17-year-old suspect was arrested and charged with murder and other offences in connection with the incident. Another Ghanaian, 24-year-old Joseph Owusu, was found dead at a dumpsite in the Bronx after reportedly going missing for about two weeks. Surveillance footage later emerged showing two individuals removing a large bag believed to contain his body from a car and leaving it on a pavement. His family has called for justice as investigations continue. In Canada, 18-year-old Ghanaian Prince Abdul Malik was shot dead in Toronto on November 7. Toronto Police identified the victim as Malik Abass, of Mississauga, while his family identified him as Prince Abdul Malik. The killing has been classified as a homicide, with investigations ongoing. The circumstances surrounding the death of Thomas Oduro in London are still being investigated.

items.title: Alhaji Bolnaba wins another term as NDC Upper East Regional Chairman
items.description: Alhaji Abdulai Mumuni Bolnaba has won another term as Upper East Regional Chairman of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), beating challenger Duncan Nsoh Ghaneba by 220 votes. Mr Bolnaba polled 371 votes to Mr Ghaneba’s 151 in the party’s regional executive elections, held on Saturday, November 14, at the GNAT Hall in Bolgatanga. A total of 570 delegates were eligible to vote. The poll was part of the NDC’s nationwide regional elections ahead of its national executive elections. Mr Bolnaba first became chairman in December 2005, after defeating the then-incumbent, Alhaji Patience Abubakari, and has held the post in later regional elections.
