items.title: Here’s the latest.
Déjà sorcier à… 23 ans (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Sacrés Navétanes. On voit du tout dans ces championnats de football amateurs joués dans nos villes et villages durant les vacances scolaires, souvent de juillet à octobre ou novembre. Leur charme, comme à la lutte traditionnelle, le côté mystique et folklorique. Toute une armada de charlatans y est souvent déployée pour terrasser l’équipe adverse. C’est dans cette aventure mystique qu’un soi-disant « marabout », âgé juste de 23 ans, s’est embarqué avec l’équipe Asc Avenir pour vaincre leurs adversaires de l’Asc Relais, lors d’une finale zonale. Payé 100.000 FCfa pour sa prestidigitation, le jeune sorcier aurait débarqué au stade Caroline Faye de Mbour avec un linceul, en réalité un mannequin féminin en silicone enroulé dans du tissu, porté par trois quidams tous vêtus de rouge. Au finish, leur équipe a été bien corrigée par l’adversaire sur le score sans appel de 2 buts à 0. Et un malheur ne venant jamais seul, le magicien et ses trois acolytes ont été embarqués par la police et présentés à un juge. Curieux de savoir si le jeune parviendra à « envoûter » tout ce monde et sauver sa réputation. Une affaire à suivre… omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Le sport et la santé, ces nouveaux outils du soft power chinois (Par Oumar NDIAYE)
items.description: Même si elle est en avance par rapport aux autres concurrents sur la course à la coopération avec l’Afrique, la Chine n’entend pas laisser aussi le terrain de soft power. Premier partenaire économique de l’Afrique, les échanges commerciaux entre la Chine et le continent africain ont atteints, en 2025, plus de 300 milliards de dollars. Sur le plan politique, les connexions institutionnelles sont de haut niveau de la par le Forum de coopération sino-africaine (Focac) qui est la rencontre de ce genre à enregistrer la plus grande présence de chefs d’État et de gouvernement. En parallèle, la Chine est en train de développer un soft power, une politique d’influence douce pour asseoir son influence. Popularisé le politologue américain Joseph Nye, le concept de soft power est définit comme l’habileté d’obtenir ce que l’on désire par l’attraction et la séduction plutôt que par la coercition ou les paiements. Dans son ouvrage « Soft Power : The means to success in word politics » (Soft Power : les moyens deréussir en politique étrangère, PublicAffairs Edition), publié en 2004, Joseph Nye détaillait ainsi les éléments qui fondent la politique de persuasion des États-Unis, qui n’ont rien à voir avec la puissance militaire ou économique. La Chine, avec sa puissance économique et même militaire, utilise ainsi ces outils de persuasion pour davantage se rapprocher des populations des zones avec qui elle développe une coopération historique et dynamique. Parmi ces outils, le sport est l’un des meneurs de jeu. La dernière polémique de Kylian Mbappé avec ce que les Chinois considèrent comme un dérapage a révélé plusieurs choses à la fois. D'abord, la diplomatie du loup guerrier (wolf warrior) est toujours active en Chine avec un esprit conquérant et surtout décomplexé. Ensuite, depuis quelques années, les entreprises chinoises sont de plus en plus présentes dans le sponsoring des compétitions sportives continentales et internationales, et aussi dans plusieurs grands championnats dont la « Liga » espagnole et la « Premier League » anglaise. Il y a aussi l'énorme marché chinois, véritable niche pour les diffusions des compétitions sportives. Sans être une puissance sportive de grande envergure, malgré que sa capitale Beijing ait une particularité rare dans le monde du sport et de l’olympisme en organisant les Jeux Olympiques d’été en 2008 et d’hiver en 2022, la Chine a déployé ses ailes dans le sponsoring des grands événements sportifs. À la dernière Coupe d’Europe des nations 2024, sur les 13 sponsors mondiaux, 5 sont des compagnies chinoises dont le géant de l’automobile électrique BYD ou le service de paiement AliPay. L’ampleur de « l’affaire Kylian Mbappé » et ses développements avec l’avalanche d’excuses présentées par l’international français, son club le Real de Madrid, et l’instance dirigeante du championnat espagnol, la « Liga », démontre ainsi la place et le poids occupés par le marché chinois sur le « merchandising » dans le domaine du sport, principalement le football. Sans compter que ce pays est devenu incontournable en devenant constructeur de stades dans beaucoup régions du monde, surtout en Afrique. Selon des estimations relayées par plusieurs médias chinois, les revenus publicitaires de Kylian Mbappé en Chine sont de 22 millions d’euros (plus de 14 milliards de Fcfa) par an, soit 38 % de ses revenus commerciaux mondiaux. Ce n’est pas seulement dans le sport que la Chine entend dérouler sa politique d’influence douce. Dans le domaine de la santé aussi, même si ces missions médicales ont lontemps sillonné l’Afrique des profondeurs, la Chine envoie aussi des navires-hopitaux faire des consultations dans beaucoup de pays africains. Le navire-hôpital « Arche du bonheur » a accosté en Mauritanie, au Sénégal, en Guinée, en Côte d’Ivoire, au Togo et au Ghana entre les mois d’octobre et novembre. Lors de son passage à Dakar, du 25 septembre au 1er octobre, ce bâtiment a effectué plus 6000 consultations et aussi 29 chirurgies. Ainsi avec ces outils que sont le sport et la santé, la Chine est en train d’étendre son influence en répondant aux besoins des populations locales, tout en gardant son avance sur la coopération dans plusieurs zones géographiques telles que l’Afrique… oumar.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Le parti Tewassoul appelle le gouvernement à corriger les déséquilibres des accords de pêche antérieurs avec l’UE
items.description: Le Parti du rassemblement national pour la réforme et le développement (Tewassoul) a estimé que la contribution financière offerte à la Mauritanie au titre de l'accord de pêche avec l'Union européenne est limitée et ne correspond ni à la valeur réelle de ses richesses marines, ni au volume des recettes tirées par les bénéficiaires de leur exploitation. Dans un communiqué publié ce samedi, le parti a déclaré que l’expiration du protocole d’application de l’accord constituait une occasion de réévaluer la politique d’exploitation des ressources halieutiques et de corriger les déséquilibres qui ont caractérisé les accords précédents. Il a appelé le gouvernement à aborder les négociations en cours de préparation dans un esprit de responsabilité nationale, à ne faire aucune concession portant atteinte aux droits souverains du pays, et à faire des garanties environnementales et des conditions d’exploitation durable des lignes rouges non négociables. Il a également demandé que les Mauritaniens puissent bénéficier davantage des richesses marines, en renforçant l’approvisionnement des marchés locaux en produits de la mer, en favorisant l’emploi national, en modernisant la flotte nationale et en développant les installations et les infrastructures liées au secteur de la pêche. Le parti a appelé les forces politiques, les organisations de la société civile, les experts et les chercheurs à se mobiliser autour de ce dossier, en exigeant que l’exploitation des richesses nationales fasse l’objet d’un débat national large et transparent, permettant à l’opinion publique de prendre connaissance de la réalité des accords, de leurs conditions, de leur efficacité et des retombées qu’ils génèrent pour le pays. C’est ce samedi soir que prend fin la validité du protocole d’application de l’accord de partenariat dans le domaine de la pêche entre la Mauritanie et l’Union européenne, qui remonte à 1987, alors que les deux parties ne sont pas parvenues à s’entendre sur un nouveau protocole, malgré plusieurs cycles de négociations menés ces derniers mois en vue de sa mise à jour.

items.title: Et si on s’intéressait à la souffrance des hommes ? (Par Matel BOCOUM)
items.description: La communauté internationale s’apprête à célébrer, du 25 novembre au 10 décembre, les 16 jours d’activisme contre les Violences basées sur le genre (Vbg). Une nouvelle occasion de tirer la sonnette d’alarme face aux violences dont les femmes et les enfants sont généralement les principales victimes. Cette campagne invite à rendre visible ce qui demeure invisible. Pour autant, les projecteurs se braquent rarement sur ces hommes qui souffrent en silence, contraints à la résignation par le poids des étiquettes sociales et des exigences qui les poussent à tout endurer sans jamais se plaindre.Dire qu’ils sont de plus en plus nombreux à oser sortir de leur mutisme dans un cadre informel. Ils expriment les souffrances qu’ils disent vivre au sein de leur foyer, parfois du fait de leur épouse. Sur les réseaux sociaux, certaines publications révèlent ainsi une réalité souvent occultée. Derrière l’image de l’homme fort, protecteur et responsable de famille se cache parfois un être humain épuisé. Lui aussi a besoin d’écoute, de reconnaissance, de repos et de soutien au sein de son couple et de sa famille. Dans une publication sur Facebook, un auteur, sous le sceau de l’anonymat, attire l’attention sur le stress auquel est confrontée la gent masculine. Mais des hommes n’osent pas en parler, comme si la société les privait de ce droit. Leur quotidien est souvent marqué par des tensions conjugales, un manque de reconnaissance et une absence de soutien, autant de facteurs susceptibles d’accentuer leur mal-être. Dans ce sillage, l’expérience vécue en 2003 par la journaliste américaine Norah Vincent continue de susciter des réflexions. Elle avait fait une immersion dans le monde masculin sous l’identité fictive de « Ned ». Elle avait choisi de se faire passer pour un homme en modifiant son apparence physique. Alors qu’elle s’attendait à découvrir les privilèges masculins, la journaliste a été confrontée à une réalité qui l’a profondément bouleversée. Au terme de cette expérience de 18 mois, elle a traversé une grave dépression qui a nécessité une hospitalisation. Elle a ensuite relaté cette immersion dans un ouvrage intitulé Self-Made Man, publié en 2006. Il faut rappeler que cette journaliste, chroniqueuse reconnue notamment au Los Angeles Times et au Village Voice, avait l’habitude de bousculer les idées reçues. « Elle découvre une pression constante, invisible, que la société exerce sur les hommes. L’obligation d’être forts en permanence. L’interdiction tacite de montrer leur vulnérabilité. L’isolement émotionnel que beaucoup d’hommes vivent comme une fatalité. Ce que des chercheurs en psychologie documentent depuis des années sur la solitude masculine, Norah le vit dans sa chair », souligne un article en ligne attribué à TDN et daté du 15 avril 2026. Dans son livre Self-Made Man, publié en 2006, elle ne dresse pas un réquisitoire contre les hommes. Elle raconte avoir découvert que la vie masculine est bien plus dure qu’elle ne l’imaginait. Par ailleurs, si certains estiment que les difficultés rencontrées par les hommes dans leur vie quotidienne et conjugale pourraient expliquer leur espérance de vie plus faible que celle des femmes, les travaux scientifiques mettent en évidence plusieurs facteurs, notamment biologiques, génétiques, comportementaux et sociaux. Un article publié en mars 2020 sur le site Sciences et Avenir, suggère d’aborder la question de la différence d’espérance de vie entre les hommes et les femmes sous l’angle génétique. Il cite le bilan démographique de l’Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (Insee) pour l’année 2019, les enfants nés cette année-là pouvaient espérer vivre en moyenne 85,6 ans pour les filles et 79,7 ans pour les garçons. L’article souligne que cet écart pourrait notamment s’expliquer par les comportements masculins : « les hommes prennent davantage de risques, exercent plus souvent certains métiers dangereux et adoptent parfois des habitudes de vie moins favorables à leur santé, ce qui peut augmenter leurs risques de développer des maladies cardiovasculaires ». Toutefois, ces écrits renseignent une souffrance masculine qui mérite, elle aussi, d’être entendue et prise en considération. matel.bocoum@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Les « Jakaarta », pourvoyeurs d’emploi et de mort (Par Ibrahima Khaliloullah NDIAYE)
items.description: J’assistais, lundi dernier, à quelques encablures de mon bureau, à la mise sous terre d’un jeune homme, mécano de son état, dans le cimetière contigu au journal «Le Soleil» où reposent d’ailleurs de nombreux collègues et confrères. C’était après le crépuscule. Dans la pénombre, les lampes des téléphones portables furent allumées. Je pus apercevoir aisément les nombreuses silhouettes qui tinrent à accompagner le jeune homme à sa dernière demeure. Décédé la veille, le défunt, la quarantaine, était connu dans la zone où il habitait et faisait valoir son savoir-faire de mécano. Il a perdu la vie suite à un accident de moto dont la personne rescapée qui était avec lui, garde de sérieuses blessures.La moto ? Les « Jakarta » ? Une véritable hécatombe qui n’en finit pas. Pas un jour sans accident sur nos routes. Ces engins de la mort se faufilent, bifurquent, doublent sans prévenir. Sans aucun respect du Code de la route. La plupart de ceux qui les conduisent, des jeunes à la fleur de l’âge, ne connaissent d’ailleurs rien à la réglementation routière. Ils n’en ont cure. Ce qui les intéresse, c’est d’arriver à destination. Souvent, montrer leur aptitude à conduire par différentes girouettes ces motos qui ne cessent d’augmenter dans la circulation routière. C’est donc dans une totale irresponsabilité que voguent certains de ces jeunes, pris par l’allégresse de la vitesse et s’en donnant à cœur joie. L’évidence est qu’une éducation à la conduite s’impose à tous les usagers de la route, au-delà des « Jakartamen » aujourd’hui. Au moment où le job de conducteur de « Jakarta » est au hit-parade des pourvoyeurs d’emploi, l’État devrait organiser davantage le secteur. La première chose étant d’assurer la sécurité des usagers, des passagers et des piétons. Les tentatives d’immatriculation et de dotation de cartes grises, prolongées de paiement de taxes, n’ont pas trop arrangé les choses. Même le port de casque n’est pas systématique malgré de régulières opérations des forces de l’ordre affectées à la circulation sur cette défaillance particulière. Au Rwanda ou encore au Bénin, entre autres exemples en Afrique, le réflexe premier du transporteur est de donner le casque au transporté. Inutile de préciser que lui-même est le premier à en porter. Pour en revenir à l’accident évoqué ci-dessus, je me suis toujours étonné de la conduite irraisonnée des jeunes de Yarakh qui, au-delà de la maîtrise de la moto, versent, depuis des années, dans le spectacle au prix de leur vie. Sous les acclamations et ovations de leurs camarades. En attendant qu’un autre prenne le tour pour montrer ses talents de « cabreur » ou procède à un « laisser-deux » (les deux mains hors du guidon et ne tenant plus la moto). Les piétons font aussi les frais des conducteurs qui se prennent pour les « rois de la route ». Jusque sur les trottoirs ou les passages cloutés qu’ils sont supposés traverser en toute sécurité… Tel ce jeune homme victime d’un motocycliste pilotant une grosse cylindrée. La jeune fille que le chauffard transportait s’écria au moment du choc : « Oh, tu as tué le fils d’autrui ». Le conducteur n’eut rien d’autre à faire que de prendre la poudre d’escampette avant l’arrivée des passants qui se mirent à affluer. Le jeune blessé traîne encore les séquelles de l’accident et le plâtre enlevé de sa jambe ne signifie pas encore une guérison totale. Trois mois après l’accident, il marche encore difficilement et sa jambe droite tient grâce à un fer qui y est introduit. Le chauffard-fuyard, lui, vit certainement libre, mais avec un éternel remords en guise de tourment. À Thiès, c’est un enseignant, brillant prof de maths de son état, qui a été victime de la furie d’une moto alors qu’il était sur un trottoir. Les remords du motard et sa tentative de participer aux frais d’hospitalisation, refusée du reste, n’y changent rien. Malgré sa fracture de la hanche, notre prof n’a pas manqué de faire des remontrances à son « assassin de la mobilité » à qui il reprochait de priver ses potaches de leur enseignant, alors que certains d’entre eux sont en classe d’examen. Le mal est devenu tellement endémique que dans chaque grand hôpital, il existe une « salle Jakarta » où sont hospitalisées les nombreuses victimes d’accidents de deux-roues. Quant aux vieilles personnes, s’il y a un cauchemar qu’elle redoute quand elles sortent de leur maison, ce sont bien les « Jakarta », en raison de leur vitesse excessive et leur propension à les heurter n’importe où. Les motos se révèlent donc aujourd’hui un problème de santé et de sécurité publiques. Pas que. D’esthétique également. La ville de Saint-Louis, qui avait refusé les « Jakarta » jusqu’à récemment, a fini par accepter leur envahissement avec tout le lot de désordre qu’induisent ces engins de la mort. Et de pollution. Qu’elles puent les fumées de motos ! Parfois jusque dans nos maisons quand une en traverse à côté de nos fenêtres… À la décharge de ces jeunes, dont certains sont diplômés, les motos constituent aujourd’hui le secteur le plus grand pourvoyeur d’emplois pour eux. Cependant, ils restent, pour la plupart, piégés par la facilité du gain qu’elles offrent. L’émigration irrégulière par voie maritime se conjugue quelquefois avec la mort. Les motos, elles, donnent parfois la mort mais pas seulement à ceux qui choisissent de les conduire. Elles tuent et blessent aussi — et c’est là que le bât blesse — d’innocentes personnes qui n’ont eu que le tort de se retrouver sur leur chemin. L’équation qu’elles posent est très délicate. Comment concilier l’exigence de la débrouille urbaine pour ces innombrables jeunes qui en vivent et celle de sécurité pour les paisibles citoyens ? Une chose est sûre : il faudra bien attaquer, un jour, le mal par la racine. Et pourquoi ne pas commencer par tarir progressivement la source ? Faire en sorte que ces motos, pour l’essentiel de seconde main, entrent en bien moindres quantités sur le territoire national… ibrahimakhalil.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: RFK Jr. Failed America on Measles
items.description: Measles is undeniably back. The disease, which was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000, is once again endemic, the Pan American Health Organization reportedly decided at a meeting this week. PAHO made that determination based on a set of technical standards, and its official declaration is expected early next week. Those criteria say that measles is endemic when the same strain of the virus causes continuous infections for a year straight; even before this week’s meeting, publicly available data indicated that this was likely the case. But really, the evidence has been clear for some time now: The U.S. is in the midst of a measles crisis unlike any it’s faced in decades. More than 5,000 cases in 45 states have been confirmed this year. Pennsylvania started reporting measles deaths this August; its count is now up to seven. New York has had one death. Wisconsin reported its second yesterday. This is already America’s worst year for measles since 1991, which marked the end of a three-year epidemic in which 123 people died. That surge helped spur a national vaccination push. This time, the outbreak has unfolded on the watch of a health secretary who has declined to accept responsibility for its ongoing spread. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has dismissed Democrats’ attempts to blame him for measles’ return. In April, he told a Senate committee that “the measles epidemic began before I came into office.” That’s true: Measles had already begun to spread in West Texas by January 2025, before Kennedy became health secretary. And routine childhood-vaccination rates, including the measles immunization, have declined since the coronavirus pandemic, which disrupted doctor appointments around the country. The U.S. isn’t alone in seeing cases rise. In January, six other countries—including Austria, Spain, and the United Kingdom—lost their elimination status. Measles was declared endemic in Canada again last year. But this is Kennedy’s crisis now. He’s been the nation’s top public-health official for nearly two years, and the country’s predicament has only deepened under his leadership. The number of measles cases in the U.S. in the first 10 months of the year is more than double the total for 2025. Meanwhile, Kennedy and the Department of Health and Human Services have failed to send a clear message to Americans about the importance of curbing the virus’s spread. As one CDC official, whose name I’m withholding to protect them from professional repercussions, recently told me, “The response has lacked a clear strategy and support from the top.” Kennedy’s CDC has offered help to states dealing with outbreaks. Recently, it’s sent staff to Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin to assist with tasks such as contact tracing and surveillance. (In an emailed statement earlier this week, an HHS spokesperson cited that assistance and $100 million the CDC recently sent to states as evidence of the department’s “aggressive” response to measles.) But under Kennedy, the CDC’s response has also at times appeared constrained. The Washington Post reported that an alert that CDC scientists wanted to send regarding the risks of measles during pregnancy was not approved for unclear reasons. Meanwhile, at least some of the assistance the CDC has offered hasn’t been welcome. As Nicholas Florko reported in The Atlantic last year, Kennedy planned to send vitamin A to Texas, but health officials in the state had never requested any. (Vitamin A can help treat measles in children who have a severe deficiency but has not been shown to be effective for most Americans.) Perhaps most dramatically, Kennedy and his HHS have fought with states over the precise toll that measles has taken. In August, after two infants died in Pennsylvania, Kennedy and Governor Josh Shapiro got into a public dispute over whether measles contributed to those children’s deaths. As the number of deaths reported by states has continued to rise, the CDC has so far declined to attribute some of them to measles; its dashboard currently lists only six fatalities. Kennedy doesn’t talk about measles often. When he does, he tends to offer a tepid endorsement of the vaccine or downplay the seriousness of the disease. In 2024, during his failed presidential run, Kennedy—a longtime anti-vaccine activist—told an interviewer that he wouldn’t give his children the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine if they were born today. (Last year, he said he would “probably” do so.) He also claimed at the time that “kids who get the measles as a child are much healthier when they grow up,” which is not true. Last year, during an outbreak in Texas in which two young girls died, he offered only half-hearted support for vaccination while pushing vitamin A. As I reported at the time , Kennedy privately told the father of one young girl who had died of measles, “You don’t know what’s in the vaccine anymore.” This August, in the midst of a rapidly growing outbreak in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, Kennedy said on CNN that “parents should get their children vaccinated for measles”—but only after the host, Dana Bash, asked him to encourage parents to vaccinate their children. (The HHS spokesperson wrote that Kennedy and CDC Director Erica Schwartz “continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles.”) Such a statement would be entirely unremarkable for any previous health secretary, but it felt notable coming from Kennedy. Since that CNN interview, Kennedy has devoted few words to measles and far more to mocking Shapiro and promoting other projects, such as his cooking show. One recent episode explored how to make a chickpea salad. Kennedy has also kept mum on the many false statements about measles and vaccination from his allies and supporters. The anti-vaccine nonprofit Kennedy founded, Children’s Health Defense, published an article in September saying that “parents don’t need to be afraid of the measles” and asserting incorrectly that the virus can make children stronger. A week later, after four people had died in Pennsylvania, Kennedy told attendees at a Children’s Health Defense conference, “You have a strong and steadfast friend at the White House.” None of this reflects well on the health secretary, but he has shown no sign that he’ll change course. (HHS did not immediately respond this morning to a request for comment on PAHO’s reported decision.) President Trump has been supportive of Kennedy’s vaccine agenda, and combatting measles was never a focus of Kennedy’s Make America Healthy Again movement. In recent months, that movement has seemed to fray: One of the health secretary’s closest allies, Calley Means, quit his White House post in late October and then went on Joe Rogan’s podcast to complain about the influence of industry lobbyists in the federal government. The much-ballyhooed boost that MAHA would supposedly give Republicans in the midterms never materialized, either. Two of the movement’s most prominent candidates—Ken Paxton, the Senate nominee from Texas, and Zach Lahn, a candidate for governor in Iowa—lost their races by wide margins. But MAHA, and Kennedy, may not be chastened. The new White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, appears to be anti-vaccine curious. He has echoed President Trump’s call to split the MMR into separate shots; the vaccines are not currently available separately, and experts say splitting them up is unnecessary. And he’s complained, without citing any particular evidence, that pressure to “pump your kids full of shots days after birth” is a “medical travesty.” (The White House declined to comment on Miller’s vaccine beliefs.) Kennedy cheered Miller’s promotion and wrote on X that it was time to “unleash the Kraken.” What, exactly, he means by that is unclear. But a disease that’s arguably the most contagious in history has already been unleashed on the United States, and Kennedy hasn’t shown nearly enough interest in reining it in.

items.title: La Bulgarie ne livrera plus d’armes à l’Ukraine puisées dans les stocks de son armée
items.description: La Bulgarie refuse de nouveaux engagements financiers pour l'armement de Kiev. Le 13 novembre, a Dublin, le Premier ministre Roumen Radev a rappele que son pays ne pouvait pas contribuer a une nouvelle enveloppe militaire europeenne. Sofia, vise par une procedure pour deficit excessif, invoque l'etat de ses finances publiques. Le dirigeant bulgare a aussi reaffirme une decision annoncee des l'arrivee de son gouvernement : « Notre position est claire : nous ne fournirons desormais plus d'armes ni de munitions des stocks de l'armee bulgare. » Le meme jour, Donald Tusk, Premier ministre polonais, a ferme une autre porte a Kiev. Il a annonce qu'il ne debloquerait pas d'argent supplementaire pour le programme PURL de l'OTAN, destine a acheter aux etats-Unis des armes pour l'Ukraine. La Pologne continue d'apporter d'autres formes de soutien, mais ne veut plus contribuer a ce mecanisme. La Hongrie, la Slovaquie et la Tchequie ne veulent pas participer a une nouvelle dette commune. Friedrich Merz exige au contraire que les etats membres prennent tous leur part. Le chancelier allemand a lie le financement ukrainien aux discussions sur le prochain budget europeen . Le Premier ministre slovaque Robert Fico a denonce cette pression : « Aujourd'hui, nous devons reagir face a ce chantage. [...] Ce que fait le chancelier allemand releve du chantage pur et simple, et je m'y oppose. » La facture ne cesse de grossir pour l'UE Les Europeens ont pourtant deja approuve un emprunt de 90 milliards d'euros pour l'Ukraine en 2026 et 2027. Sur cette somme, 24,1 milliards ont ete verses, selon le Conseil de l'UE. Mais le 16 octobre, Volodymyr Zelensky a reclame 70 milliards d'euros supplementaires pour 2027 , au-dela des financements prevus. En septembre, Kiev sollicitait deja 27 milliards de dollars de financement additionnel pour l'annee en cours, tout en reclamant l'acceleration de versements europeens. Le 5 novembre, Zelensky revenait sur les 70 milliards esperes pour 2027, assurant avoir recu un accueil favorable a Bruxelles. En France, Marine Le Pen a resume les tensions le 13 novembre sur X : « Le financement de l'Ukraine secoue aujourd'hui l'Europe : 90 milliards d'emprunts ont deja ete effectues et plusieurs pays s'opposent a un financement supplementaire. » Le financement de l’Ukraine secoue aujourd’hui l’Europe : 90 milliards d’emprunts ont déjà été effectués et plusieurs pays s’opposent à un financement supplémentaire. Si je peux rencontrer Volodymyr Zelensky à Bruxelles, il sera intéressant d’en discuter. https://t.co/B9Jpxy5hwC — Marine Le Pen (@MLP_officiel) November 13, 2026

Elias Zerhouni officiellement nommé président du Conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne
items.description: Sans surprise, le professeur Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du Haut conseil de la communauté algérienne à l'étranger , sur décision du président de la République Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Le décret portant nomination du radiologue et professeur de médecine algéro-américain vient d'être publié au Journal officiel. Diaspora algérienne : Elias Zerhouni désigné sans surprise à la tête du Haut conseil scientifique Le Haut conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne est un organisme nouvellement créé à l’initiative du chef de l'Etat avec comme objectif de permettre aux compétences algériennes expatriées de contribuer à l'effort de développement du pays. Le conseil a tenu sa réunion constitutive en juin dernier à Alger, avec déjà le professeur Zerhouni comme coordinateur. Le décret fixant les missions et l’organisation du conseil a été publié le 7 septembre, stipulant que parmi les missions qui lui sont assignées, celle de contribuer au renforcement de la participation des compétences scientifiques expatriées et de proposer “des mécanismes durables pour les relier au système national d'enseignement supérieur, de recherche scientifique et d'innovation, afin de développer le capital humain et assurer le développement économique, social, scientifique, technique et culturel du pays”. Zerhouni : “L’idée est de faire quelque chose ensemble pour le pays” Ses membres, au nombre de 39, ont été reçus fin septembre par le président Tebboune. Y figurent des éminences de la recherche scientifique en Amérique et en Europe, dont Elias Zerhouni, Yasmine Belkaid, Belkacem Haba, Karim Zaghib, Noureddine Melikechi… “Actuellement en Algérie, nous avons toutes les capacités, il y a des jeunes qui se distinguent dans des compétitions internationales. L’idée est de faire quelque chose ensemble pour le pays, nous qui connaissons l'étranger et ceux qui connaissent l’intérieur du pays”, a déclaré Zerhouni à l'issue de l’audience. Elias Zerhouni, un éminent professeur reconnu aux États-Unis Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du conseil en vertu d’un décret présidentiel daté du 4 novembre 2026, publié dans le dernier numéro du Journal officiel. “M. Adam Elias Zerhouni est nommé président du haut conseil de la communauté scientifique nationale à l'étranger”, y lit-on. Né à Nedroma (Tlemcen) en 1951, Elias Zerhouni a fait l'essentiel de sa carrière de médecin et de professeur de médecine aux États-Unis, notamment à la faculté de médecine de l'Université Johns Hopkins. Entre 2002 et 2008, il a occupé le poste prestigieux de directeur des National Institutes of Health (NIH). L'éminent radiologue avait été nommé par Georges W. Bush, alors président des États-Unis. L’article Elias Zerhouni officiellement nommé président du Conseil scientifique de la diaspora algérienne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: China's anti-poverty victory shines a light on other nations' paths
items.description: In February 2021, Chinese President Xi Jinping declared the elimination of absolute poverty, after the final 98.99 million rural Chinese residents living under the then national poverty line had all been lifted out of poverty. It marked the end of a four-decade campaign. Data from the Chinese government and the World Bank shows that approximately 800 million people were raised above the extreme-poverty threshold over the period, accounting for more than 70% of global poverty reduction. That declaration was followed by a five-year transition period intended to consolidate gains and prevent people from backsliding into poverty. It concluded at the end of 2025 with the establishment of regularized anti-relapse mechanisms. International observers were taking note. Building risk-prevention mechanisms There's no guarantee that people who emerge from poverty will stay out of it. Illness, crop failure, job loss, or a single large expense can push a household back below the threshold. China's response has been to build a follow-up system that tracks those risks. It relies on various channels: self-reporting by rural households, routine assessments by local officials, and data screening for sudden changes in income, medical spending, housing and school attendance. When a risk is flagged, a verification and assistance process kicks in, with local officials organizing support for the household. Official readouts after the 2025 central rural work conference indicate a shift toward regularized anti-relapse mechanisms, rather than temporary fixes. John Bailey, chief executive of South Africa's Sunday World media platform, has visited northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region four times. He wrote after his most recent trip that China's program is highly targeted and coordinated with rural revitalization in a way that reflects systematic planning and long-term vision. Poverty, he says, can be eliminated when leadership, policy frameworks, accountability and sustained investment in people are all present. Treating the cause, not just the symptoms China's strategy changed decisively when they recognized the rising tide of national development didn't lift all boats and started asking why some were still trapped in hardship. By 2013, the people still living in poverty were concentrated in remote areas. Kenyan commentator Eric Biegon noted after visiting southwest China's Guizhou Province that these communities faced "structural barriers" that broad economic growth simply couldn't remove. So, China developed a targeted poverty alleviation model. Rather than adopting a one-size-fits-all approach, officials collected information on millions of households, including their income, education and health conditions, as well as the specific factors contributing to their poverty. Assistance was then tailored to the needs of each household. Robert Walker, a fellow of the British Academy of Social Sciences, points out that conventional poverty-reduction programs often fail because they just hand out cash without fixing the underlying problems. China's experience offers a massive, real-world example of how this approach can work. Take Juncao, a hybrid grass developed in southeast China's Fujian Province to support mushroom cultivation. Introduced to Rwanda in 2006, it provided rural households with a low-cost, locally manageable means of generating income and improving nutrition. Citing official reports, the Chinese Embassy in Rwanda said the technology had helped lift more than 37,000 local farmers out of poverty, thanks in part to its "low cost, ease of application and short growth cycle." The technology also required neither large-scale infrastructure investment nor a complex administrative system. Approaches that empower Speaking at the 2026 Global Poverty Reduction and Development Forum in Beijing, Vongsey Vissoth, Cambodia's permanent deputy prime minister, said the real lesson from China isn't copy-pasting what they did, but understanding how they did it and adapting it to local conditions. Former Peruvian Prime Minister Javier Velásquez Quesquén agreed. He said the most important part of China's success in lifting 800 million people out of extreme poverty is designing public services with people's right to development built in. For Ayak Awer Chan Liol, who works at the Office of South Sudan's Vice President Benjamin Bol Mel, the lesson is deeply personal. After attending a training program on poverty reduction in Ningxia in 2025, Liol said it's inspiring to see that "if Ningxia can do it, Africa, South Sudan, specifically, can do it too." For other developing countries looking for their own strategies, China's experience is extremely valuable. Global progress against poverty has slowed in many regions, and solutions require flexibility. Perhaps China's most useful contribution isn't a beaten track for others to follow, but rather a light shining on what's possible through hard-won experience.

items.title: Don’t Be So Surprised That Mississippi Turned Blue
items.description: Scott Colom, the first Black U.S. senator ever elected by Mississippians, traces his lineage in the state back seven generations, to when the nation was forging its foundation on the backs of stolen Black people. He waged a campaign set on showing that “Mississippi matters,” which many registered more as a question than a declaration, doubting whether a Black man and a Democrat could win the seat. During the most expensive election cycle in U.S. history, his campaign coffers were empty compared with Democrats in other battleground races. Finally victorious on Veterans Day, he credited the state’s civil-rights titans and local people who work without an expectation of recognition for carrying on the “Mississippi faith tradition” of having hope, even—or perhaps especially—in dark chapters. Many Americans might be surprised that Colom flipped what’s long been a deeply red seat. But this win is the product of decades of uphill, incremental, thankless, and overlooked labor powered by an ancestral charge and a conviction to reclaim Mississippi. My late stepfather, Obbie Riley, a five-term Democratic county supervisor in Mississippi, was among those who undertook that fight, although he didn’t live long enough to see its results. The state’s “faith tradition” that Colom evoked is as much about prayer as it is about remembering generations of bloodshed in Mississippi, where Black voting rights were redeemed by those who could only dream of what Colom has now achieved: finally turning his home state blue. “There were times when I was tired, and I felt like I couldn’t keep going, but I kept the faith,” Colom said during his victory speech Wednesday night. “And that is another tradition of our state. There’s so many people that had faith in Mississippi at times where it seemed impossible.” That faith, and the hard work that must accompany it, was something Colom learned in his household, where he and his twin brother were reared by now-retired Judge Dorothy Colom, the first Black person to be elected to her region’s chancery court, and Wilbur Colom, an attorney who was once a Republican. Scott built on this pedigree, attending the University of Wisconsin to study law and returning home to the Columbus area, in the east-central pocket of the state, not far from the Alabama line. There he became the youngest and the first African American justice-court judge in Lowndes County, in 2011, and then Columbus’s first African American city prosecutor, in 2013. Later he took a bolder step, campaigning for district attorney in his early 30s. [ Adam Serwer: Even where MAGA won, MAGA lost ] If Columbus were anywhere else, it might be described as a natural incubator for a Democratic U.S. senator. It is a college town, home to the state’s women’s university; it’s also a vertex of a region known as “The Golden Triangle,” which is anchored by Mississippi State University and an Air Force base in Starkville. Colom ran for district attorney in 2015 as a reform candidate—and unseated a 27-year incumbent who’d defended debunked medical-examiner analyses that had led to multiple false convictions that were later overturned. Colom has been the region’s top cop for more than a decade; he instituted restorative justice and counseling for gun-violence survivors, among other reforms. In 2020, days after George Floyd was murdered, Mississippi’s attorney general suddenly dropped a police-shooting case that Colom had transferred to the state in 2016. Colom was outspoken about it, making parts of the case file public and expressing regret for handing the case over. History is never fully in the rearview in Mississippi, and that was evident throughout the Colom campaign. On the day before he delivered his victory speech, at Tougaloo College, a historically Black school with a rich civil-rights history, Colom held a press conference wearing a mocha-brown hoodie that bore a quote from the civil-rights organizer Bob Moses: When you’re in Mississippi, the rest of America doesn’t seem real. And when you’re in the rest of America, Mississippi doesn’t seem real. Moses directed Freedom Summer, the 1964 effort to recruit hundreds of white college students to Mississippi to help open Freedom Schools, or voter-registration-and-education sites meant to overcome the ridicule, violence, and other tactics the state used to keep Black voters off the rolls. At the time, the state had the lowest Black voter-registration numbers, despite being the Blackest state in the U.S. Training for the college students was under way when members of the Ku Klux Klan burned down Mt. Zion United Methodist Church in Philadelphia, Mississippi, after beating parishioners suspected of holding civil-rights meetings. Michael Schwerner and James Chaney, organizers who had done grassroots work at Mt. Zion, knew they had to leave Freedom Summer training in Ohio to check on the community. Andrew Goodman, a college student who volunteered for Freedom Summer, joined them on his first trip to Mississippi. On the afternoon of June 21, as the trio made their way through the center of Philadelphia, the deputy sheriff, a Klansman, pulled them over and arrested them. When they were released after nightfall, a group of Klansmen and law enforcement kidnapped them, killed them, and buried them in an earthen dam in Neshoba County, where an FBI search located them 44 days later. This past summer, Colom made a campaign stop at the Neshoba County Fair, where politicians frequently stump. Ronald Reagan spoke there during his 1980 presidential campaign, emphasizing his belief in states’ rights, which many interpreted as a dog whistle, given the proximity to where the three civil-rights workers had been slain. Colom’s father worked for Reagan’s transition team. In a 1981 interview with The Daily Mississippian , the University of Mississippi’s student newspaper, Wilbur Colom criticized some of Reagan’s policies and said that the GOP of the ’50s and ’60s had been deficient in its support for civil-rights legislation, but that Black voters’ commitment to the Democratic Party shouldn’t be automatic either. Wilbur’s son ran a campaign with a complementary refrain: Why should Mississippi automatically be considered a Republican stronghold, especially when Democrats have chipped away at GOP control in statewide elections over the past decade? When my stepfather died in September, he was the lone Black person and Democrat serving as a Neshoba County supervisor. And although that set him apart, he’s remembered for how he sifted through disagreements to move forward, even if the ideological overlap with his colleagues was the size of a grain of sand. Throughout his campaign, Colom likewise touted that he would work with anyone, Republican or otherwise; he even visited a Trump rally and spoke with people waiting in line. There’s a Mississippi brand of bipartisanship, one my stepdad practiced, that’s a mainstay especially in rural areas, where people of difference have found commonality even amid bitter political and racial tensions. Colom’s win was propelled by grassroots organizing to register voters, get them to the polls, and, in some cases, help them return to certify or cure provisional ballots. The senator-elect outraised his opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, in the last quarter of the campaign ( approximately $1.45 million to $864,000), but that was nothing compared with the money pouring in for other Democratic Senate candidates. Colom’s campaign had a “rich message but a poor treasury,” Representative Bennie Thompson said at the Tougaloo victory party, where he introduced the senator-elect. With seemingly nothing to lose, Colom infused a little bit of fun into his campaign, producing a series of ads that showcased his sense of humor. One, called “Sinators,” parodied the Mississippi-based movie Sinners using Colom’s identical twin brother. In it, a Hyde-Smith look-alike asks for just one more chance to keep everything in Mississippi the way it is. Hyde-Smith, whose parents sent her to a segregation academy as a child, was caught on camera in 2018 saying of a supporter standing beside her that if he “invited me to a public hanging, I’d be on the front row”—in the state where more known lynchings occurred than in any other. (She later said that the remark was an “exaggerated expression of regard.”) She conceded the race after it was called on Wednesday, and congratulated Colom on his victory. The moment had a karmic quality: After President Biden nominated Colom to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi in 2022, Hyde-Smith single-handedly blocked him from the lifetime appointment, even though other statewide Republicans supported him for the role. For a time, it looked as if the election results might face legal challenges. During the week-long vote counting, Hyde-Smith was asked about the possibility of fraud in the election and said, “There’s always irregularities .” In the summer of 2025, Mississippi shifted tens of thousands of voters to “inactive” status based on data from the credit-reporting agency Experian. DeSoto County, home to the white-flight suburbs of Memphis, inactivated more than 15,000 voters, more than anywhere else in the state . On Election Day, lines there lagged, and polling stations ran low on affidavit ballots. Colom won the county with about 53 percent of the vote; Hyde-Smith had won the county in her previous two elections. The first time the Department of Justice used the now-gutted 1965 Voting Rights Act to protect white voters happened in Colom’s district, in Noxubee County, in 2005; Wilbur Colom represented the defendant in the case . A decade later, around the time that Scott Colom was running for district attorney, a DOJ lawyer from the 2005 case filed a lawsuit alleging issues with the Noxubee voter rolls. Instead of undertaking a costly fight, the county entered a consent decree that required a period of scrutinized voter-roll management. Noxubee and Lowndes, another county in Colom’s district, also saw voter inactivations surge in the months before the 2026 midterms. This living history is another reason many doubted whether Colom, or any Black senatorial candidate, could make it to Washington. Political pundits have already compared this moment to the Barack Obama elections, which saw high Black voter turnout in Mississippi and elsewhere. Nadia Colom—the wife of the senator-elect, a real-estate agent, and former executive director of the Golden Triangle Boys and Girls Club—said in her speech on Wednesday that people have been calling her “Mississippi’s Michelle,” referring to the former first lady. “While it’s an honor, really and truly, to be seen in that light, what really means the most to me is that I get to be called Mississippi’s ,” she said. [ Read: Why Black voters abandoned Trump ] Colom’s campaign rightly touts him as the first Black U.S. senator to be elected by Mississippians. Mississippi sent two Black senators—Hiram Revels, the nation’s first Black senator, and later Blanche Bruce—to Washington at a time when they were selected by state legislators. Black men also served as secretary of state in Mississippi for nearly a decade after the Civil War. In 1870, 14 percent of the state Senate and 47 percent of the state House of Representatives were made up of Black men. By 1874, nearly 80 percent of the state House was Black. Because Reconstruction showed such promise in Mississippi, the backlash that followed was orchestrated, acute, and violent. A defining feature of Mississippi history is that white violence directly triggered an exodus . One historian estimates that from 1914 to 1920, during the Great Migration, one in five of the Black migrants leaving the South for economic opportunity, safety, dignity, and more came from Mississippi. White Mississippians waged yet more violence against Black folks who stayed, assassinating Medgar Evers, sickening and fatiguing Fannie Lou Hamer, and brutalizing everyday citizens into strange fruit . The remnants of that targeted violence are still visible today in the state’s stark inequality and lack of opportunity for Black Mississippians. But Colom’s campaign challenges the narrative that Mississippi should be defined through the lens of white harm, and that those with aspirations are better off leaving. On Wednesday night, Nadia Colom said to her and Scott’s twin girls, eighth-generation Mississippians, that she hoped the race reinforced the family motto to never quit, a value instilled in their father, who passed it to them. Persistence is a precious inheritance in a state that often ranks dead-last in indicators of prosperity, livelihood, health, well-being, and education. Scott Colom didn’t quit when donors wouldn’t answer the phone, when fewer than 10 people showed up at his first town hall, when it took eight days to rightfully claim his victory. For 200 years and counting, his ancestors didn’t quit on Mississippi, toiling and resisting on the lands that he traversed during his campaign. Now he is reaping the reward of remaining.

items.title: Acte V contre la vie chère : une mobilisation aux revendications multiples
items.description: Cinquième samedi de mobilisation contre la vie chère en France. Entre 50 et 60 cortèges sont attendus à travers le pays, autour de revendications variées mêlant pouvoir d'achat, climat et contestation du maintien de l'ordre. Cet "acte V" rassemble des profils et des mots d'ordre très différents. Sur place, notre journaliste Johan Bodin a notamment recueilli le témoignage de Mathis, membre d'Interfac, qui dénonce "l'installation d'un État policier en France".

items.title: La Tunisie s’endette pour construire une autoroute vers l’Algérie
items.description: Le projet de construction d’une autoroute reliant la Tunisie à la frontière avec l’Algérie a franchi une nouvelle étape décisive, avec l’obtention par Tunis d’un financement de la Banque islamique de développement (BID). La nouvelle a été annoncée par le ministre tunisien de l’Économie et de la Planification, Samir Abdelhafidh, rapporte ce samedi la presse locale. La BID a donné une suite favorable à la demande tunisienne en septembre dernier et la convention de financement entre les deux parties sera signée en 2027, selon la même source. Le montant approuvé s’élève à 335,49 millions d’euros. Autoroute vers l’Algérie : un projet stratégique pour la Tunisie Devant les membres de l’Assemblée des représentants du peuple (ARP) et du Conseil national des régions et des districts réunis pour examiner le Budget 2027, le ministre tunisien a souligné l’importance stratégique de cette autoroute qui permettra de compléter jusqu’en Tunisie l’autoroute est-ouest algérienne. Cette autoroute va faciliter les déplacements routiers entre les deux pays d’autant que la Tunisie est la destination touristique préférée des Algériens. De nombreux Tunisiens se rendent régulièrement en Algérie pour notamment acheter des produits de large consommation qui bénéficient du soutien de l’État. À cela s’ajoute le développement des liens économiques et du commerce entre les deux pays. L’Algérie, qui compte 1605 km d’autoroutes et 145615 km de routes, a achevé son autoroute reliant l’est à l’ouest du pays sur plus de 1200 km. Pour la Tunisie, qui compte 743 kilomètres autoroutes, elle ambitionne de porter ce chiffre à 1 323 kilomètres à l’horizon 2035. L’article La Tunisie s’endette pour construire une autoroute vers l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Ouagadougou: 7 boutiques fermées pour récidive et pratiques commerciales illicites
items.description: ​ (Ouagadougou, 13 novembre 2026) Dans le cadre de sa mission de protection des consommateurs et de régulation du marché, la Brigade Mobile de Contrôle Économique et de la Répression des Fraudes (BMCRF) a mené une série de contrôles inopinés sur le terrain. De Dapoya à Sankar Yaaré en passant par Paspanga, les commerces de produits de grande consommation ont été passés au peigne fin. Cette descente musclée a permis la fermeture de 7 boutiques pour non-respect des règles, pratiques de prix illicites, récidive et commercialisation de produits périmés et interdits. En plus de la fermeture, les contrevenants ont été réquisitionnés pour effectuer des travaux d’intérêt général. India stun Pakistan by one wicket in last-ball U-19 Asia Cup final thriller
items.description: Mohit Ulva and Chigurupati Venkata held their nerve to guide India to a dramatic one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the ACC Men’s U-19 Asia Cup final, chasing down a target of 338 on the final ball at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Saturday. India were staring at defeat at 252 for eight in the 42nd over before Ulva and Manal Chauhan revived their hopes with a 57-run partnership for the ninth wicket. Chauhan struck three fours and three sixes in his 32-ball 47 before falling at 309 in the 48th over, leaving India needing 29 from the final 16 deliveries. Ulva and Venkata then added an unbeaten 30 runs for the last wicket to take India home. With eight runs required in the final over, Ulva, who finished unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, including five fours and three sixes, struck the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain’s final delivery. Venkata remained not out on 11 off eight balls as India finished at 339 for nine in 50 overs. Captain Lakshya Raichandani had earlier top-scored with 80 off 101 balls, while Aaryavir Sehwag contributed 58 from 61 deliveries. The pair provided India with a strong start, putting on 95 for the opening wicket before Sehwag was dismissed in the 18th over. Pakistan, however, kept striking at regular intervals to regain control. Raichandani departed at 217 in the 37th over, and India lost their eighth wicket just one run later, with the scoreboard reading 252. Rizwanullah was Pakistan’s most successful bowler with three for 53 in his 10 overs, while Niqab Shafiq claimed two for 57. The defeat denied defending champions Pakistan a successful title defence after they had entered the final unbeaten, winning all three group matches, including an earlier victory over India, before overcoming Bangladesh in the semi-final. Earlier, Pakistan posted 337 for nine after opting to bat, with Usman Khan scoring a century and Abdul Qadir and captain Farhan Yousaf making valuable half-centuries. Usman and Hayam Khan provided Pakistan with a steady start, putting on 62 for the opening wicket. Hayam struck four boundaries in his 23-ball 21 before falling in the ninth over. Usman then combined with Qadir in a commanding 135-run partnership for the second wicket. Qadir provided the acceleration with an attacking 80 off just 54 balls, hitting three fours and eight sixes before being dismissed on the last ball of the 27th over with Pakistan at 197 for two. Usman continued to anchor the innings, reaching his second century of the tournament. The left-hander struck 107 off 111 deliveries, including 11 fours and three sixes, before falling in the 37th over with Pakistan at 240 for three. Farhan maintained the momentum with a 60-ball 63, including four fours and three sixes. He added 59 runs for the fourth wicket with Ahmed Hussain, who contributed 17 off 20 balls. Pakistan had looked set for a total in excess of 350 after reaching 204 for two at the halfway stage. However, India’s bowlers pulled things back in the closing overs, restricting Pakistan to 337 for nine. Kavya Paresh Patel led the Indian attack with four for 68 in his 10 overs, while Venkata, who came into the side in place of the injured Ishan Sood, claimed three for 40 from five overs. Arjun Rajput took one wicket for 43. Ulva was named player of the match for his decisive contribution in the chase, while Sehwag received the player of the tournament award.

items.title: China, Thailand eye higher-level cooperation in digital, green sectors
items.description: Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Saturday called on Chinese and Thai enterprises to seize new opportunities and elevate bilateral cooperation by expanding from "dining tables and taste buds" to "digital intelligence and green development." The two sides could strengthen industrial synergy and supply chain integration, and move up the global value chain, he said. Li made the remarks while attending a symposium with Chinese and Thai entrepreneurs, along with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, in Bangkok. After listening to remarks from representatives of both countries' business communities, Li said that as China and Thailand work together to usher in a new golden 50 years of bilateral relations, new opportunities are emerging for economic and trade cooperation. To begin with, China and Thailand enjoy the stability brought by high-level mutual trust and friendship, Li said. In today's world marked by turbulence and uncertainty, stability has become a scarce resource, he said, noting that China-Thailand relations and cooperation have demonstrated strong stability. Close and regular communication between the leaders of the two countries, along with strong people-to-people ties and cultural affinity, has provided businesses in both countries with a stable and predictable environment for expanding investment and making long-term plans, Li said. Growing connectivity between the two countries also brings an aggregation effect, Li said. The steady progress in the construction of the China-Thailand railway, the official opening of China's Pinglu Canal, and the strengthening "soft connectivity" in areas such as trade rules, standards and finance have facilitated more seamless interaction of the two markets, enabling more enterprises to generate greater economic benefits, he added. Flourishing innovative cooperation between the two countries also brings an empowering effect, Li said. China-Thailand economic and trade cooperation continues to expand beyond traditional areas into high-tech, emerging and cutting-edge fields, with new business models and areas of growth constantly emerging, he said. This makes it an opportune time for the two sides to leverage their respective strengths and deepen innovation cooperation, Li said. Li called for expanding traditional trade in agricultural and food products, advancing agricultural modernization in both countries, and pursuing cooperation in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence, clean energy and biomedicine to jointly foster and strengthen new growth drivers. The Chinese premier also called for upgrading cooperation from "production collaboration" to "industrial synergy," adding that the two sides should enhance complementarity and integration in industrial and supply chains, and promote the alignment and mutual recognition of industry standards, to jointly improve competitiveness through more efficient coordination and move up the global value chain. China encourages Chinese enterprises to expand localized operations in Thailand, he added. Li also called for upgrading cooperation from "a bilateral focus" to "regional outreach" by leveraging Thailand's geographic advantages, making good use of policy dividends such as the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and expanding cooperation in third-party markets worldwide to better achieve win-win and multi-win outcomes. The governments of China and Thailand will make active efforts to provide a sound business environment for enterprises of both countries and support their long-term development and deeper engagement in local markets, Li said. He also expressed hope that entrepreneurs from both countries would serve as envoys of friendship among the people and make China-Thailand relations even closer and stronger. Speaking at the event, Anutin said China is Thailand's most important trading partner. He noted that Thailand hopes to seize opportunities arising from technological advances and work with China to leverage their respective strengths and achieve higher-quality cooperation. The two countries should move beyond being merely trading partners to becoming long-term partners pursuing common development and mutual success, while further expanding cooperation in electric vehicles, agriculture, investment, connectivity and other areas, Anutin said. Thailand will introduce more policies and measures to create favorable conditions for Chinese enterprises to operate and develop in the country over the long term, while combating transnational crime and protecting investors' rights and interests, he said. Anutin also expressed confidence that the friendship captured in the saying "Thailand and China are as close as one family" would deliver more tangible results and bring benefits to the peoples of both countries. Business representatives from both countries also briefed the leaders on the progress and outcomes of their cooperation and offered specific suggestions. They expressed confidence in China-Thailand friendship and a willingness to further strengthen cooperation and contribute to the development and prosperity of both countries through more tangible achievements. (With input from Xinhua)

items.title: NCCIA warns youth against joining illegal call centres for lucrative salaries
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Saturday warned that loopholes in the existing system are being exploited by illegal call centres , online betting operators and international fraud networks to launder money and trap victims. Addressing a press conference, NCCIA (Islamabad/Rawalpindi) Additional Director Muhammad Shoaib Khan said fake companies were being registered with weak verification, after which bank accounts opened in their names were integrated with loan apps, betting and gaming portals to receive and transfer illicit funds. Therefore, he called for stricter rules on company registration and bank account verification. The press conference was primarily called to warn educated youths against becoming involved in cybercrime by joining illegal call centres in pursuit of lucrative salaries, urging those seeking jobs with call centres to ask their employers where they are registered and appealing to parents to check whether their children were working at an illegal call centre carrying out scams, fraud or other illicit activities. “Ask them what documents the company has, what registration it operates under, which company they work for, which company is providing the loans, where the money is coming from and who is putting money into these applications,” Khan said. Acknowledging that young people and university students were engaging in such jobs because the salaries were higher than average, he noted that they risked ending up becoming part of the entire trap and operation. “If your son or daughter is arrested in such an operation, the FIR (first information report) becomes part of their record. Tomorrow, when they need a character certificate or apply for a government job, that record can affect them,” the NCCIA officer warned. He said the issue concerns merchant accounts provided by banks and the accounts into which money is deposited. A bank account is linked to a company that may already have been registered despite weaknesses in proper verification, standard operating procedures or the Know Your Customer (KYC) process. “After the company has been registered, the bank opens an account for it. The operators then take that company’s bank account and integrate it with their online betting or gaming portal,” Khan said, adding that the NCCIA team is working on recommendations to these institutions so that they improve their checking systems. The additional director said the agency already raised the issue with senior officials at the policy level, and loopholes identified during investigations and interrogations are brought to light so they can be addressed. He said the NCCIA wants to address cases where one-person companies or similar companies were registered and their bank accounts were subsequently used in this way. Meanwhile, Khan said that the NCCIA identified the role and other details of each individual involved: who used which computer, what their role was, the extent of their involvement, who trapped victims, made the calls and edited the material. “We do not treat everyone as having played the same role. After establishing those roles, we prepare the proper FIR and proceed accordingly,” he explained. The NCCIA additional director noted the agency raided two call centres in the Islamabad-Rawalpindi Zone over the past three days. In the Rawalpindi raid, 11 people, including 10 women, were arrested, while in the Islamabad raid, 143 people were arrested, including 43 women. He said the centres were carrying out transnational scams and fraud, targeting countries in South Asia. Modus operandi Explaining the modus operandi, he said the two centres in the latest raids worked differently. At the Rawalpindi centre, an elaborate setup posing as the police had been created. The operators would offer loans, and when it was time to recover the loans — or when they had trapped someone and wanted to extract money — they would call and scam that victim. The suspects would tell a person that they were either being surveilled or on a hit list. Once someone fell into their trap, they would transfer the person to a setup made to look like the police in Bangladesh, put the victim in contact with someone posing as a police officer and then extort money. At the Islamabad centre, they worked in layers; first, they trapped the victim and convinced them to install an application on their mobile phone. Once it was installed, they obtained access to the person’s photo gallery. After accessing the gallery and obtaining a selfie, they would issue a loan for a minimal amount. But their real target was to collect the person’s credentials: mobile number, personal information and other data. They also obtained information about close family members whom the borrower had identified as guarantors, such as a wife, father, brother, cousin or other family members named as next of kin. Once they had collected all these credentials, the case would be passed to senior members. When they had extracted all of the money they could from someone, they would wipe out that person’s account and close the case. The second method was to take a person’s selfie and other pictures from their phone gallery and edit them into pornographic material, using the person’s face in what appeared to be a professional manner. They would then start threatening, harassing and blackmailing the victim. “Even though the resulting pictures might have been fabricated, the threats were still effective. The victim would be under tremendous pressure, fearing that the images would reach their community or family. Under that pressure, the person would start paying money,” Khan said. He said the scammers extracted personal information in the name of loans, manipulated it and used it against the victims, or created sexual content depicting the victim and extracted money through harassment and blackmail. Responding to a question about alleged masterminds, Khan said they were present at every call centre and also arrested. After that, the agency would investigate local facilitators, including whoever rented out the building, those who made the arrangements and connections and those who set up the operation through a fake company. “We also trace the people who pay the bills and pursue those involved. Then we work at the transnational and international level. We have liaison arrangements with different countries. If a handler or operator belongs to another country, we communicate through embassies and our international contacts,” he noted. A global problem The additional director further stated that international cooperation was being strengthened because such call centres had become a global problem. The NCCIA would handle investigations in Pakistan, while the relevant agencies in the United Kingdom, the United States, China and other countries would handle such matters in their respective jurisdictions. Khan added that in a previous Rawalpindi call centre case, foreign nationals were arrested and are in jail, and will face trial according to Pakistani law. On the changing methods of call centres, he acknowledged that they were no longer necessarily operating in large plazas. In one house, 10 to 12 people gathered with a computer setup and connected their applications and websites to bank accounts. Someone may be sitting in another country while the people here trap the victim, the NCCIA official pointed out. Once the victim starts depositing money into the account, the person in the other country receives the money. He noted that the Rawalpindi centre had been operating for about a month, while the Islamabad facility had been established only 15 or 20 days earlier. The floor managers and overall HR managers at both centres were locals, he added. “We will investigate and interrogate further to establish who is connected to the back-end operation. We need to find out in which country the application was developed, who developed it and who is handling it,” Khan stated. Staying safe Speaking about how the youth could tell which call centres are legal, Khan said the first thing is common understanding. “If an entire floor is generating sexual content, you know that is illegal. That is a matter of common sense.” Khan added that when applying for a job, young people should ask which organisation the business is registered with, who approved it and what approval it received from the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Moreover, he said many loan applications were operating legally because they have proper permission and follow a lawful procedure. The NCCIA inspects their whole system, including whether the applications are accessing people’s photo galleries, and examines their loan-recovery mechanism. If a borrower does not pay, there are legal channels and procedures for recovery. On foreign nationals allegedly involved in cybercrime, Khan said he did not have an exact number, but acknowledged that there have been many deportations. “The number in prison is in the hundreds. When the agency raids one call centre alone, it may find between 150 and 250 people on average,” he added. Khan also rejected attributing call-centre crime to one nationality, saying there are people of multiple nationalities who come to Pakistan and become involved in this work. The agency had also arrested 37 suspects allegedly involved in harassment and blackmail cases over the past two to three years, the official added. The suspects had extracted money from women through harassment and blackmail, and the victims had endured this for the past two or three years. On online betting and gambling, Khan said operators initially give users profits deliberately, enticing people to put more money into these portals. They then assess the victim’s financial capacity and, once convinced that the victim has invested their savings, they wipe out the money and cut off contact. “We are working on this issue and, God willing, will take further action soon. We are making every effort to address fraud involving millions and billions in the name of online betting and gaming,” he stressed. Appealing to young people and businesspeople, including major business owners, Khan urged them against putting business money into buying tokens online and depositing money into gaming applications, gaming websites or betting platforms. “Initially, they may even be allowed to withdraw their money, but essentially the operators are giving them time, playing with their mind and encouraging them to keep depositing more money,” he explained. Khan said the cyber-patrolling teams work around the clock, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

items.title: Suivi-évaluation de la campagne de reboisement : le préfet d’Assoli constate l’évolution des plants dans les communes 1 et 2
items.description: Bafilo, 14 nov. (ATOP) – Le préfet d’Assoli, Lt-Col. Viagbo Mensah, accompagné de son staff technique et du directeur préfectoral de l’environnement, le capitaine Panassa Dihèza, a effectué une tournée de suivi-évaluation des sites de reboisements dans les communes Assoli 1 et 2, le jeudi 12 novembre à Bafilo. Cette descente sur le terrain s’inscrit dans le cadre du suivi de la campagne de reboisement de 2024-2026, visant à contribuer à l’atteinte d’un milliard de plants reboisés d’ici 2030. Elle a permis au préfet et sa suite de se rendre respectivement à Awangala dans la commune Assoli 1, à Dikorodè et Tagbadè dans l’Assoli 2. Le but est d’apprécier l’évolution des plants reboisés d’identifier ceux qui sont morts et d’envisager des approches de solutions pour la prochaine campagne. Il s’est agi également de sensibiliser les communautés riveraines, sur l’importance de la protection, de l’entretien et du suivi constant et régulier des sites reboisés afin d’éviter les feux de brousse, la divagation des animaux sur ces sites. A la première étape de la tournée sur le site d’Awangala reboisé essentiellement des plants de Khaya sénélengalensis depuis 2024, la délégation constate que ces plants se distinguent nettement d’autres qui ont atteint une hauteur raisonnable. Cependant, certains plants sont morts ou endommagés et nécessite un remplacement. A l’occasion, le préfet a exhorté les communautés et leurs responsables à renforcer la surveillance du site à procéder au regarnissage des plants morts par de nouveaux à la prochaine campagne. Il a également donner des orientations pour la résolution de certains conflits liés au foncier, tout en demandant aux chefs traditionnels d’impliquer davantage la communauté fulbé dans l’entretien et la protection des plants afin qu’ils prennent conscience pour ne pas laisser les bœufs passer par le site. Les acteurs mobilisés ont entamé l’entretien du site, en désherbant, taillant les arbustes et traçant des pares-feux pour éviter les feux de brousses. A Dikorodè dans l’Assoli 2 , le préfet et sa suite accompagné du maire, a visité le site reboisé à la campagne de 2025 et 2026. Là, le constat est encourageant, sur ce site est déjà entretenu, les jeunes plants de Gmelina ou teck blanc croissent bien mais restent tout de même fragiles. Le Lt-Col. Viagbo a insisté sur le suivi régulier afin de mieux protéger les jeunes plants contre le passage des animaux et parfois certains insectes rongeurs. A Tagbadè, site reboisé en 2025, les eucalyptus ont atteint une hauteur tandis que les Gmelina qui croissent moins vite ont été visités par les animaux. Au terme de la sortie, le préfet a souligné que le bilan est globalement positif en termes de croissance des plants. Mais, il invite les populations riveraines à un entretien régulier des pares-feux, à la surveillance des animaux en divagation et ceux du pâturage et au regarnissage des plants morts dès la saison pluies prochaines afin de contribuer significativement à l’atteinte des objectifs fixés par le gouvernement en matière de la politique environnementale au Togo. Le directeur préfectoral, en charge de l’environnement a exhorté les communautés à pratiquer la régénération naturelle assistée en entretenant au même moment les petits arbustes qui poussent tout seuls au côté des plants reboisés afin favoriser des forêts denses. ATOP/TAL/BA
